2544E3D0DFE7013132C268A86D17958E.description: Identify various states of consciousness including sleep and dreams, hypnosis, meditation, and psychoactive drugs.

25447400DFE7013132C168A86D17958E.description: Describe the interaction of a person and the environment in determining perception including Gestalt principles and how one's experiences and expectations influence perception.

2543E360DFE7013132C068A86D17958E.description: Explain the processes of sensation and perception, as well as the capabilities and limitations of sensory processes including the visual, auditory, kinesthetic, olfactory, and gustatory sensory systems.

25437E50DFE7013132BF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the parts of a neuron and explain neurotransmission including the role and impact of various neurotransmitters.

25431F30DFE7013132BE68A86D17958E.description: Examine the structure and function of the nervous and endocrine system and how they affect behavior.

2542B6D0DFE7013132BD68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the structure and function of the brain including the hypothalamus, prefrontal lobe, corpus callosum, hemispheres, and amygdala.

254247D0DFE7013132BC68A86D17958E.description: The student will investigate the structure, biochemistry and circuitry of the brain and the nervous system to understand their roles in affecting behavior.

2541B9B0DFE7013132BB68A86D17958E.description: Explore the various modes of psychological testing including personality, intelligence, and projective while assessing the reliability of each.

25415650DFE7013132BA68A86D17958E.description: Identify ethical standards psychologists must address regarding research with human and non-human participants.

2540F3C0DFE7013132B968A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast quantitative and qualitative research strategies including experiments, surveys, focus groups, and narratives as the foundation of research in psychology.

25409030DFE7013132B868A86D17958E.description: Describe the scientific method as the framework for research and apply the principles of research design to an appropriate experiment.

254027C0DFE7013132B768A86D17958E.description: The student will examine the development of psychology as an empirical science by describing the scientific method, explaining research strategies and identifying ethical issues.

253FAED0DFE7013132B668A86D17958E.description: Classify the various subfields in psychology including vocational applications such as counseling, industrial, clinical, experimental, and educational psychology.

253F3B60DFE7013132B568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the origins of psychology based on significant historic figures including Wilhelm Wundt, William James, John B. Watson, and Karen Horney.

253ED7A0DFE7013132B468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the definition of psychology in the context of psychology as an empirical science and the major approaches to psychology including behavioral, psychoanalytical, cognitive, and humanistic.

253E7600DFE7013132B368A86D17958E.description: The student will examine the foundations of psychology and its origins as a separate social science discipline.

comments: Psychology is the study of human social behavior from an individual perspective including the foundations of psychology as an empirical social science, the structure and functions of the brain, human development, and how individuals adapt to their environment. Students will examine principles of motivation, how a person's culture and society influence the individual, psychological disorders, and the promotion of mental health.

253A4180DFE7013132A968A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual and visual evidence to analyze the causes and effects of the domestic terrorist attack on the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City including the responses of Oklahomans to the event, the concept of the "Oklahoma Standard" and the creation of the Oklahoma City National Memorial and Museum.

253D9EB0DFE7013132B168A86D17958E.description: Examine major cultural and ethnic groups' contributions to the social and economic transformation of the modern state of Oklahoma.

253D3AA0DFE7013132B068A86D17958E.description: Explain the leadership of Oklahoma and its people in the field of aeronautics including the Federal Aviation Administration, NASA space program, and the influence of weather research on national disaster preparedness.

253CD350DFE7013132AF68A86D17958E.description: Describe the contemporary role the state's agriculture plays in feeding the nation and the world including the wheat, corn, cattle, pork, and chicken industries.

253C48E0DFE7013132AE68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual and visual evidence to analyze the oil and gas boom of the 1970s and the subsequent bust of the energy industry during the 1980s including the impact of the Penn Square Bank Collapse on the state's economy, employment, and banking.

253BDAC0DFE7013132AD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the evolving relationship between state and tribal governments impacting tribal self-determination and control over Native American lands and resources including issues of joint jurisdiction, taxation, and gaming.

253B7860DFE7013132AC68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the impact of Oklahoma's leadership on state and national politics including the rise of viable two party elections, Governor Henry Bellmon, and United States Representative Carl Albert.

253B15D0DFE7013132AB68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual and visual evidence to describe the artistic contributions of Oklahomans in the fields of music, art, literature, theater and dance including Ralph Ellison and the Five Indian Ballerinas as well as the perceptions of Oklahoma by the rest of the nation because of the musical Oklahoma.

253AA8A0DFE7013132AA68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of economic growth in various sectors.
comments: A. Impact of rural to urban migration,
B. Development of water and timber resources,
C. Emergence of the tourism as an industry,
D. Discovery of new fossil fuel resources, Tulsa's designation as Oil Capital of the World, and the opening of the Anadarko Basin, and
E. Improvement of the state's transportation infrastructures and the Kerr-McClellan Navigation System.

2539CEE0DFE7013132A868A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual and visual evidence to evaluate the progress of race relations and actions of civil disobedience in the state.
comments: A. Judicial interpretation of the equal protection clause of the 14th Amendment which ultimately resulted in the desegregation of public facilities, and public schools and universities,
B. Landmark Supreme Court cases of Sipuel v. Board of Regents of the University of Oklahoma (1948) and McLaurin v. Oklahoma Board of Regents for Higher Education (1950),
C. Lunch counter sit-ins organized by Clara Luper and the NAACP, and
D. Leadership of Governor Gary in the peaceful integration of the public common and higher education systems.

25396C80DFE7013132A768A86D17958E.description: The student will investigate how post-war social, political, and economic events continued to transform the state of Oklahoma during the 1950s through the present.

25390890DFE7013132A668A86D17958E.description: Summarize and analyze the impact of mobilization for World War II including the establishment of military bases and prisoner of war installations and the contributions of Oklahomans to the war effort including the Native American code talkers and the 45th Infantry Division.

2538A140DFE7013132A568A86D17958E.description: Describe the contributions of Oklahomans in 1920s and 1930s including Deep Deuce and African-American jazz musicians, Will Rogers's and Woody Guthrie's political and social commentaries, Wiley Post's aviation milestones, and the artwork of the Kiowa Six (formerly the Kiowa Five).

25381CF0DFE7013132A468A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual and visual evidence of the environmental conditions and the impact of human mismanagement of resources resulting in the Dust Bowl including the migration of the Okies, the national perceptions of Oklahomans as shaped by The Grapes of Wrath, and the New Deal policies regarding conservation of natural resources.

2537A9C0DFE7013132A368A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual and visual evidence to evaluate the impact of the boom and bust cycle of Oklahoma's agricultural production as a response to the needs of World War I, and its effect as a precursor of the Great Depression.

253730A0DFE7013132A268A86D17958E.description: Examine how the economic cycles of boom and bust of the oil industry affected major sectors of employment, mining, and the subsequent development of communities, as well as the role of entrepreneurs including J.J. McAlester, Frank Phillips, E.W. Marland, and Robert S. Kerr.

2536C200DFE7013132A168A86D17958E.description: Summarize the impact of the national Socialist movement and organized labor on various segments of Oklahoma society including agriculture, mining, and state politics.

25364E80DFE7013132A068A86D17958E.description: Examine multiple points of view regarding the historic evolution of race relations in Oklahoma including Senate Bill 1 establishing Jim Crow laws, the growth of all-Black towns, the Tulsa Race Riot, and the resurgence of the Ku Klux Klan.

2535EC80DFE70131329F68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the successes and failures of the United States policy of assimilation of the Native Americans in Oklahoma including the passage of the Indian Citizenship Act of 1924 and the effects of the Indian boarding schools (1880s-1940s) upon Native Americans' identity, culture, traditions, and tribal government and sovereignty.

25358A30DFE70131329E68A86D17958E.description: The student will examine the transformation of Oklahoma during times of boom and bust of the 1920s through the 1940s.

25352530DFE70131329D68A86D17958E.description: Describe state constitutional provisions including the direct primary, initiative petition, referendum, and recall.

2534B690DFE70131329C68A86D17958E.description: Identify major sources of local and state revenues and the services provided including education, infrastructure, courts, and public safety.

25345030DFE70131329B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the division, function, and sharing of powers among levels of government including city, county, tribal, and state.

2533F160DFE70131329A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast Oklahoma's state government to the United States' national system of government including the branches of government, their functions, and powers.

25338D50DFE70131329968A86D17958E.description: Describe and summarize attempts to create a state constitution joining Indian and Oklahoma Territories including the impact of the Progressive and Labor Movements resulting in statehood on November 16, 1907.

25331E80DFE70131329868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the development of governments among the Native American tribes, the movement for the state of Sequoyah, the proposal for an all-Black state, and the impact of the Enabling Act on single statehood.

25329FC0DFE70131329768A86D17958E.description: The student will analyze the formation and development of constitutional government in Oklahoma.

253232F0DFE70131329668A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast multiple points of view to evaluate the impact of the Dawes Act which resulted in the loss of tribal communal lands and the redistribution of lands by various means including land runs as typified by the Unassigned Lands and the Cherokee Outlet, lotteries, and tribal allotments.

2531CE60DFE70131329568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the influence of the idea of Manifest Destiny on the Boomer Movement including the official closing of the frontier in 1890.

25316270DFE70131329468A86D17958E.description: Cite specific visual and textual evidence to assess the impact of the cattle and coal mining industries on the location of railroad lines, transportation routes, and the development of communities.

2530F6C0DFE70131329368A86D17958E.description: Summarize the impact of the Civil War and Reconstruction Treaties on Native American peoples, territories, and tribal sovereignty.
comments: A. Required enrollment of the Freedmen,
B. Second Indian Removal and the role of the Buffalo Soldiers,
C. Significance of the Massacre at the Washita,
D. Reasons for the reservation system, and
E. Establishment of the western military posts of Fort Sill, Fort Supply, and Fort Reno.

25308A80DFE70131329268A86D17958E.description: Integrate visual and textual evidence to explain the reasons for and trace the migrations of Native American peoples including the Five Tribes into present-day Oklahoma, the Indian Removal Act of 1830, and tribal resistance to the forced relocations.

25302A30DFE70131329168A86D17958E.description: Describe the major trading and peacekeeping goals of early military posts including Fort Gibson.

252FC200DFE70131329068A86D17958E.description: Summarize and analyze the role of river transportation to early trade and mercantile settlements including Chouteau's Trading Post at Three Forks.

252F5FB0DFE70131328F68A86D17958E.description: The student will evaluate the major political and economic events that transformed the land and its people prior to statehood.

252EF5F0DFE70131328E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast cultural perspectives of Native Americans and European Americans regarding land ownership and trading practices.

252E8290DFE70131328D68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the goals and significance of early Spanish, French, and American expeditions including the impact of disease, interactions with Native Americans, and the arrival of the horse and new technologies.

252E1190DFE70131328C68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the accomplishments of prehistoric cultures including the Spiro Mound Builders.

252D9DD0DFE70131328B68A86D17958E.description: Integrate visual information to identify and describe the significant physical and human features including major trails, railway lines, waterways, cities, ecological regions, natural resources, highways, and landforms.

252D1830DFE70131328A68A86D17958E.description: The student will describe the state's geography and the historic foundations laid by Native American, European, and American cultures.

comments: In Oklahoma History and Government, the student will examine the people and events that have formed and transformed the landscape and cultures of the place and peoples that have become Oklahoma. The student will examine important political and ideological movements, as well as economic, cultural, and political accomplishments of state, national, and world significance. The learning of Oklahoma History and Government should lead students to link Oklahoma's history to local, national, and global contexts.

25203740DFE70131326B68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the conditions under which the federal government and the Federal Reserve implement expansionary or contractionary policies.

251FCC90DFE70131326A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast fiscal and monetary policy and their impact on the economy.

251F6650DFE70131326968A86D17958E.description: The student will identify the potential economic impact of policy changes by the Federal Reserve and the federal government.

251F0490DFE70131326868A86D17958E.description: Define the different types of unemployment and determine how it is measured and the impact it has on different sectors of the United States economy.

251E92F0DFE70131326768A86D17958E.description: Define inflation and determine how it is measured and the impact it has on different sectors of the United States economy.

251E2950DFE70131326668A86D17958E.description: The student will explain the role of inflation and unemployment in an economic system.

251DC4B0DFE70131326568A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact on the economy when GDP and GNP are growing or declining.

251D6010DFE70131326468A86D17958E.description: Explain GDP and GNP and how they are used to describe economic output over time and compare the GDP of various countries representing free-market, command, and mixed economies.

251CF8A0DFE70131326368A86D17958E.description: The student will identify Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and Gross National Product (GNP) as basic measures of a nation's economic output and income.

251C8820DFE70131326268A86D17958E.description: Explain how these conditions have an impact on consumers, producers, and government policymakers.

251C14E0DFE70131326168A86D17958E.description: Determine how interest rates, unemployment, Consumer Price Index (CPI), individual savings and debt, government debt, labor supply, and inflation impact current economic conditions in the United States.

251BA2B0DFE70131326068A86D17958E.description: The student will examine current economic conditions in the United States.

252C4D40DFE70131328868A86D17958E.description: Describe the costs and benefits of government assistance programs, education, and other government funded services and projects.

252BEAC0DFE70131328768A86D17958E.description: Explain the role that government has in dealing with issues such as poverty, pollution, and medical research.

252B83B0DFE70131328668A86D17958E.description: The student will evaluate the economic role of government in a market economy.

252B1660DFE70131328568A86D17958E.description: Identify an entrepreneur and describe how his/her decisions affect job opportunities for others.

252AB620DFE70131328468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the potential risks and potential gains of entrepreneurs opening new businesses or inventing a new product, and determine the financial and nonfinancial incentives that motivate them.

252A5470DFE70131328368A86D17958E.description: The student will analyze the role of entrepreneurs in a market economy.

2529F090DFE70131328268A86D17958E.description: Determine how changes in real interest rates impact people's decisions to borrow money and purchase goods in a market economy.

25298BD0DFE70131328168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between interest rates and inflation rates.

25291E40DFE70131328068A86D17958E.description: The student will evaluate how interest rates impact decisions in the market economy.

2528B310DFE70131327F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the value of money is determined by the goods and services it can buy.

252845A0DFE70131327E68A86D17958E.description: Identify the components of the money supply, the different functions of money, and give examples of each.

2527DF60DFE70131327D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how individuals, businesses and the overall economy benefit from using and saving money.

25277B00DFE70131327C68A86D17958E.description: The student will analyze how money makes it easier to trade, borrow, save, invest, and compare the value of goods and services.

25271220DFE70131327B68A86D17958E.description: Identify how labor unions, corporations, and not-for-profits influence a market economy.

2526ADF0DFE70131327A68A86D17958E.description: Describe how banks match savers with borrowers and allow people to pool their incomes and provide future income through investing in stocks.

252642F0DFE70131327968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the impact of government ensuring the protection of private property rights and the rule of law in a market economy.

2525A320DFE70131327868A86D17958E.description: The student will describe the role of economic institutions including banks, labor unions, corporations, governments, and not-for-profits in a market economy.

25253500DFE70131327768A86D17958E.description: Explain how people's own self-interest, incentives and disincentives influence market decisions.

2524D200DFE70131327668A86D17958E.description: Explain how competition impacts the free market including the concepts that competition among sellers lowers costs and prices while encouraging increased production and competition among buyers increases prices and the allocation of goods and services to consumers willing and able to pay higher prices.

25246B60DFE70131327568A86D17958E.description: The student will evaluate how changes in the level of competition in different markets affect prices.

25240520DFE70131327468A86D17958E.description: Explain what causes shortages and surpluses including government imposed price floors, price ceilings, and other government regulations and the impact they have on prices and people's decisions to buy or sell.

252387C0DFE70131327368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how price and non-price factors affect the demand and supply of goods and services available in the marketplace.

25230870DFE70131327268A86D17958E.description: The student will explain how prices are set in a market economy using supply and demand graphs and will determine how price provides incentives to buyers and sellers.

2522A740DFE70131327168A86D17958E.description: Describe the role of the factors of production, land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship, and technology in economic systems.

252243E0DFE70131327068A86D17958E.description: Compare the world's basic economic systems of market (free enterprise), command, and mixed market economies identifying countries that have adopted each and comparing and contrasting the results those economic systems have produced in those countries as measured by GDP, national prosperity, and individual income and wealth.

2521D760DFE70131326F68A86D17958E.description: The student will evaluate how societies answer the three basic economic questions: what goods and services to produce, how to produce them, and for whom are they produced.

25217240DFE70131326E68A86D17958E.description:
Determine appropriate courses of economic actions using a variety of economic reasoning and decision-making models including the PACED Decision-Making Model by using the five step process of
P = Stating the PROBLEM,
A = Listing the ALTERNATIVES,
C = Identifying the CRITERIA,
E = EVALUATING the options, based on the criteria, and
D = Making a DECISION.

25210C90DFE70131326D68A86D17958E.description: Define and apply basic economic concepts of scarcity, surplus, choice, opportunity cost, cost/benefit analysis, risk/reward relationship, incentive, disincentive, and trade-off to a variety of economic situations.

2520A760DFE70131326C68A86D17958E.description: The student will develop and apply economic reasoning and decision-making skills.

comments: In high school Economics, the student will learn and apply basic economic reasoning skills, concepts, and skills. The student will apply a variety of economic decision-making models to real-life economic situations. The student will examine the American free-market system as contrasted with other economic systems. The roles of economic systems, money, entrepreneurs, the United States Government, and the Federal Reserve will be examined as well.

comments: The overall goal of Oklahoma's Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) for Physical Education is to promote the health and well-being of each student and guide them toward becoming physically active for life. The Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) are categorized under three major areas: Motor Skill and Lifetime Activity Development; Health-Enhancing Activity Development; and Personal and Social Skill Development. It is important to realize some skills are repeated because of the need for emphasizing those skills. Skills have been selected and placed under major headings to demonstrate the appropriateness of what is expected at the various grade levels.

comments: The Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) for Health and Safety represent standards that describe what students should know concerning health and safety. The standards are categorized under the following: HEALTH and SAFETY LITERACY, RESPONSIBLE HEALTH AND SAFETY BEHAVIOR, AND HEALTH AND SAFETY ADVOCACY. A well-informed, self-directed student has the foundation for leading a healthy, productive life. By recognizing that many health problems and causes of premature death can be prevented, children can reduce many of the risks generally encountered during adolescence and adulthood.

1E3D9820DFE70131264B68A86D17958E.description: Make observations, connections, and react, speculate, interpret, and raise questions in analysis of texts.

1E3DE190DFE70131264C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the main problem or conflict of the plot; the effect of the qualities of the characters and explain how the conflict is resolved.

1E3D3660DFE70131264A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the believability of a character and the impact they have on the plot.

1E3B0060DFE70131264368A86D17958E.description: Clarify understanding of text information in different ways (e.g., timelines, outlines, graphic organizer) to support and explain ideas.

1E3AB6E0DFE70131264268A86D17958E.description: Support reasonable statements and conclusions by reference to relevant aspects of text and examples.

1E3B4C00DFE70131264468A86D17958E.description: Make generalizations based on information gleaned from text.

1E3BAAF0DFE70131264568A86D17958E.description: Summarize and paraphrase information including the main idea and significant supporting details of a reading selection.

1E3E7270DFE70131264E68A86D17958E.description: Interpret and respond creatively to literature (e.g., art, drama, oral presentations, and Reader's Theater).

1E3F2130DFE70131265068A86D17958E.description: Make inferences or draw conclusions about characters' qualities and actions (i.e., based on knowledge of plot, setting, characters' motives, characters' appearances, other characters' responses to a character).

1E3EBBF0DFE70131264F68A86D17958E.description: Draw inferences and conclusions about text and support them with textual evidence and prior knowledge.

1E397670DFE70131263E68A86D17958E.description: Use the text's structure or progression of ideas, such as cause and effect or chronology to locate or recall information.

1E39CA30DFE70131263F68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend both fiction and nonfiction that is appropriately designed for sixth grade.

1E3914D0DFE70131263D68A86D17958E.description: Use prereading strategies independently (to preview, activate prior knowledge, predict content of text, formulate questions that might be answered by the text, establish purpose for reading).

1E3A1C90DFE70131264068A86D17958E.description: Recognize main ideas presented in a particular segment of text; identify and assess evidence that supports those ideas.

1E373800DFE70131263768A86D17958E.description: Comprehension/Critical Literacy -- The student will interact with the words and concepts in a text to construct an appropriate meaning.

1E362AF0DFE70131263468A86D17958E.description: Read silently for increased periods of time.

1E368E40DFE70131263568A86D17958E.description: Increase silent reading speed through daily independent reading.

1E36E2A0DFE70131263668A86D17958E.description: Read regularly in independent-level texts (texts in which no more than approximately 1 in 10 words is difficult for the reader) fluently and accurately, and with appropriate timing, change in voice, and expression.

1E359B00DFE70131263268A86D17958E.description: Fluency -- The student will identify words rapidly so that attention is directed at the meaning of the text.

1E410520DFE70131265668A86D17958E.description: Relate dictionary definitions to context of the reading in order to aid understanding.

1E415D80DFE70131265768A86D17958E.description: Determine the meanings, pronunciation, and derivations of unknown words by using a glossary, dictionary, and/or thesaurus.

1E428EA0DFE70131265B68A86D17958E.description: Use word origins, including knowledge of less common roots (graph = writing, logos = the study of) and word parts (auto = self, bio = life) from Greek and Latin to analyze the meaning of complex words (autograph, autobiography, biology).

1E41F660DFE70131265968A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of root words to determine the meaning of unknown words within a passage.

1E424320DFE70131265A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the origins and meanings of foreign words frequently used in English.

1E404400DFE70131265468A86D17958E.description: Use prior experience and context to analyze and explain the figurative use of words, similes (comparisons that use "like" or "as": "The Snowplow Reared Up Like a Stallion"), metaphors (implied comparisons: "Peace is a sunrise), and multiple meaning words.

1E3FFD10DFE70131265368A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of word parts and word relationships, as well as context clues (the meaning of the text around a word), to determine the meaning of technical and specialized vocabulary and to understand the precise meaning of grade-level-appropriate words in fiction and nonfiction texts.

1E3F6E00DFE70131265168A86D17958E.description: Vocabulary -- The student will develop and expand knowledge of words and word meanings to increase vocabulary.

1E2BB640DFE70131261368A86D17958E.description: Reading/Literature: The student will apply a wide range of strategies to comprehend, interpret, evaluate, appreciate, and respond to a wide variety of texts.

document.title: Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) for Mathematics

15B501E0DFE70131168768A86D17958E.description: Probability: Describe the probability (more, less, or equally likely) of chance events.

15B4BA20DFE70131168668A86D17958E.description: Construct bar graphs, frequency tables, line graphs (plots), and pictographs with labels and a title from a set of data.

15B462E0DFE70131168568A86D17958E.description: Read graphs and charts, identify the main idea, draw conclusions, and make predictions based on the data (e.g., predict how many children will bring their lunch based on a menu).

15B41580DFE70131168468A86D17958E.description: Pose questions, collect, record, and interpret data to help answer questions (e.g., which was the most popular booth at our carnival?).

15B375D0DFE70131168268A86D17958E.description: Data Analysis - The student will demonstrate an understanding of collection, display, and interpretation of data and probability.

15B32690DFE70131168168A86D17958E.description: Money: Determine the correct amount of change when a purchase is made with a five dollar bill.

15B2D100DFE70131168068A86D17958E.description: Read a thermometer and solve for temperature change.

15B28580DFE70131167F68A86D17958E.description: Tell time on a digital and analog clock to the nearest 5 minute.

15B244F0DFE70131167E68A86D17958E.description: Solve simple addition problems with time (e.g., 15 minutes added to 1:10 p.m.).

15B1BFB0DFE70131167C68A86D17958E.description: Develop and use strategies to choose an appropriate unit and measurement instrument to estimate measurements (e.g., use parts of the body as benchmarks for measuring length).

15B17E00DFE70131167B68A86D17958E.description: Develop and use the concept of perimeter of different shapes to solve problems.

15B137C0DFE70131167A68A86D17958E.description: Choose an appropriate measurement instrument and measure the length of objects to the nearest meter or centimeter and the weight of objects to the nearest gram or kilogram.

15B0EC40DFE70131167968A86D17958E.description: Choose an appropriate measurement instrument and measure the length of objects to the nearest inch or half-inch and the weight of objects to the nearest pound or ounce.

15B054B0DFE70131167768A86D17958E.description: Measurement - The student will use appropriate units of measure to solve problems.

15AEC810DFE70131167268A86D17958E.description: Estimate the product of 2-digit by 2-digit numbers by rounding to the nearest multiple of 10 to solve application problems.

15AE7360DFE70131167168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate fluency (memorize and apply) with basic multiplication facts up to 10 x 10 and the associated division facts (e.g., 5 x 6 = 30 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5).

15AE2D10DFE70131167068A86D17958E.description: Use physical models and a variety of multiplication algorithms to find the product of multiplication problems with one-digit multipliers.

15AD7890DFE70131166E68A86D17958E.description: Estimate and find the sum or difference (with and without regrouping) of 3- and 4-digit numbers using a variety of strategies to solve application problems.

15ACD430DFE70131166C68A86D17958E.description: Create and compare physical and pictorial models of equivalent and nonequivalent fractions including halves, thirds, fourths, eighths, tenths, twelfths, and common percents (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) (e.g., fraction circles, pictures, egg cartons, fraction strips, number lines).

15AC93E0DFE70131166B68A86D17958E.description: Compare and order whole numbers up to 4 digits.

15AC0FF0DFE70131166968A86D17958E.description: Read and write whole numbers up to 4 digits (e.g., expanded form, standard form).

15ABCBA0DFE70131166868A86D17958E.description: Model the concept of place value through 4 digits (e.g., base-10 blocks, bundles of 10s, place value mats).

15AAF8B0DFE70131166568A86D17958E.description: Number Sense and Operation – The student will use numbers and number relationships to acquire basic facts. The student will estimate and compute with whole numbers.

15AAB530DFE70131166468A86D17958E.description: Recognize and apply the commutative and identity properties of multiplication using models and manipulative to develop computational skills (e.g., 3 · 5 = 5 · 3, 7 · 1 = 7).

15AA6DA0DFE70131166368A86D17958E.description: Find unknowns in simple arithmetic problems by solving open sentences (equations) and other problems involving addition, subtraction, and multiplication.

15AA1C50DFE70131166268A86D17958E.description: Describe (orally or in written form), create, extend and predict patterns in a variety of situations (e.g., 3, 6, 9, 12 . . . , use a function machine to generate input and output values for a table, show multiplication patterns on a hundreds chart, determine a rule and generate additional pairs with the same relationship).

15A9AA30DFE70131166168A86D17958E.description: Algebraic Reasoning: Patterns and Relationships - The student will use a variety of problem-solving approaches to extend and create patterns.

15B00E60DFE70131167668A86D17958E.description: Make and use coordinate systems to specify locations and shapes on a grid with ordered pairs and to describe paths from one point to another point on a grid.

15AFC5B0DFE70131167568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effects of combining and subdividing two- and three-dimensional figures (e.g., folding paper, tiling, nets, and rearranging pieces of solids).

15AF7700DFE70131167468A86D17958E.description: Identify and compare attributes of two- and three-dimensional shapes and develop vocabulary to describe the attributes (e.g., count the edges and faces of a cube, the radius is half of a circle, lines of symmetry).

15AF22C0DFE70131167368A86D17958E.description: Geometry - The student will use geometric properties and relationships to recognize and describe shapes.

15A91C60DFE70131165F68A86D17958E.description: Use representations to model and interpret physical, social, and mathematical situations (e.g., counters, pictures, tally marks, number sentences, geometric models; translate between diagrams, tables, charts, graphs).

15A8DA80DFE70131165E68A86D17958E.description: Create and use a variety of representations appropriately and with flexibility to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas (e.g., dramatizations, manipulatives, drawings, diagrams, tables, graphs, symbolic representations).

15A84D00DFE70131165C68A86D17958E.description: Use mathematical strategies to solve problems that relate to other curriculum areas and the real world (e.g., use a timeline to sequence events, use symmetry in art work, explore fractions in quilt designs and to describe pizza slices).

15A7F620DFE70131165B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize relationships among different topics within mathematics (e.g., the length of an object can be represented by a number, multiplication facts can be modeled with geometric arrays, ½ can be written as .5 and 50%).

15A7A930DFE70131165A68A86D17958E.description: Link concepts to procedures and eventually to symbolic notation (e.g., represent actions like snap, clap, clap with symbols A B B, demonstrate 3 • 4 with a geometric array, divide a candy bar into 3 equal pieces that represent one piece as ⅓).

15A76550DFE70131165968A86D17958E.description: Relate various concrete and pictorial models of concepts and procedures to one another (e.g., use two colors of cubes to represent addition facts for the number 5, relate patterns on a hundreds chart to multiples, use base-10 blocks to represent decimals).

15A6E3D0DFE70131165768A86D17958E.description: Make predictions and draw conclusions about mathematical ideas and concepts. Predictions become conjectures and conclusions become more logical as students mature mathematically.

15A69C80DFE70131165668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate thinking processes using a variety of age-appropriate materials and reasoning processes (e.g., manipulatives, models, known facts, properties and relationships, inductive [specific to general], deductive [general to specific], spatial, proportional, logical reasoning ["and" "or" "not"] and recursive reasoning).

15A642F0DFE70131165568A86D17958E.description: Explain mathematical situations using patterns and relationships (e.g., identify patterns in situations, represent patterns in a variety of ways, extend patterns to connect with more general cases).

15A5C240DFE70131165368A86D17958E.description: Represent, discuss, write, and read mathematical ideas and concepts. Start by relating everyday language to mathematical language and symbols and progress toward the use of appropriate terminology (e.g., "add more" becomes "plus", "repeated addition" becomes "multiplication", "fair share" becomes "divide", "balance the equation" becomes "solve the equation").

15A580C0DFE70131165268A86D17958E.description: Relate manipulatives, pictures, diagrams, and symbols to mathematical ideas.

15A53BE0DFE70131165168A86D17958E.description: Extend mathematical knowledge by considering the thinking and strategies of others (e.g., agree or disagree, rephrase another student's explanation, analyze another student's explanation).

15A4F760DFE70131165068A86D17958E.description: Express mathematical ideas coherently and clearly to peers, teachers, and others (e.g., with verbal ideas, models or manipulatives, pictures, or symbols).

15A42F90DFE70131164E68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between necessary and irrelevant information in solving problems (e.g., play games and discuss "best" clues, write riddles with sufficient information, identify unnecessary information in written story problems).

15A3EC30DFE70131164D68A86D17958E.description: Verify and interpret results with respect to the original problem (e.g., students explain verbally why an answer makes sense, explain in a written format why an answer makes sense, verify the validity of each step taken to obtain a final result).

15A3A8F0DFE70131164C68A86D17958E.description: Develop, test, and apply strategies to solve a variety of routine and non-routine problems (e.g., look for patterns, make a table, make a problem simpler, process of elimination, trial and error).

15A364D0DFE70131164B68A86D17958E.description: Formulate problems from everyday and mathematical situations (e.g., how many forks are needed?, how many students are absent?, how can we share/divide these cookies?, how many different ways can we find to compare these fractions?).

15A31F80DFE70131164A68A86D17958E.description: Use problem-solving approaches (e.g., act out situations, represent problems with drawings and lists, use concrete, pictorial, graphical, oral, written, and/or algebraic models, understand a problem, devise a plan, carry out the plan, look back).

  4. Articulation (staccato, legato, and accent).

  2. Families of orchestral instruments (e.g., strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion), and

06CAA0974DB74189AA79C3CCAC1920A0.description: Identify basic notational symbols (written representation of music), including: treble and bass clef, time signatures (e.g., 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, and 6/8), and note values (whole note, half note, quarter note, eighth note, dotted half note, dotted quarter note, and the corresponding rests).

Define and use correct terminology to identify and discuss the elements of music, including:
  1. Melody (e.g., steps, wide and narrow leaps, repeated tones, phrases, pentatonic scale [five - tone scale], intervals, and major and minor scales),
  2. Rhythm (e.g., steady beat, back beat, syncopation, triplets, dotted rhythms, and 2/2 meter),
  3. Harmony (e.g., partner songs, rounds, descants, countermelody, and major and minor chords),
  4. Form (e.g., unity and variety, AB, ABA, round, rondo, theme and variations, marching, introduction, coda, interlude, verse and refrain, and prelude),
  5. Tone color (e.g., opera, musical theater, duet, trio, quartet, chorus, voice ranges, and instrument ranges, and a capella),
  6. Pitch (e.g., range and register, change pitch with compositional devices, such as imitation, inversion, and transposition),
  7. Tempo [e.g., (allegro (fast), lento (slow), andante (walking), and moderato (moderate)], and
  8. Dynamics [e.g., (forte (loud), piano (soft), mezzo forte (medium loud), mezzo piano (medium soft), crescendo, and decrescendo)].

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Science

7F04D36BF5F74A81AF09E4EEB86EC8A2.description: Use mathematical representations to support explanations of how natural selection may lead to increases and decreases of specific traits in populations over time.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on using mathematical models, probability statements, and proportional reasoning to support explanations of trends in changes to populations over time.

Assessment Boundary: The assessment should provide evidence of students' abilities to explain trends in data for the number of individuals with specific traits changing over time. Assessment does not include Hardy Weinberg calculations.

1B5B9D5A3B1D4B049B1116B66E721482.description: Gather and synthesize information about the technologies that have changed the way humans influence the inheritance of desired traits in organisms.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on synthesizing information from reliable sources about the influence of humans on genetic outcomes in artificial selection (such as genetic modification, animal husbandry, gene therapy); and, on the impacts these technologies have on society as well as the technologies leading to these scientific discoveries.
Assessment Boundary: The assessment should provide evidence of students' abilities to understand and communicate how technology affects both individuals and society.

FE0D33B05328435D927CA57F0B89B94F.description: Construct an explanation based on evidence that describes how genetic variations of traits in a population increase some individuals' probability of surviving and reproducing in a specific environment.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on using simple probability statements and proportional reasoning to construct explanations.

Assessment Boundary: The assessment should provide evidence of students' abilities to explain why some traits are suppressed and other traits become more prevalent for those individuals better at finding food, shelter, or avoiding predators.

C1077EDC325249AF9147D3226FF13585.description: Analyze displays of pictorial data to compare patterns of similarities in the embryological development across multiple species to identify relationships not evident in the fully formed anatomy.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on inferring general patterns of relatedness among embryos of different organisms by comparing the macroscopic appearance of diagrams or pictures.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment of comparisons is limited to gross appearance of anatomical structures in embryological development.

9EC56434149C432EAB226CEE5C0CC20B.description: Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after the substances interact to determine if a chemical reaction has occurred.

7C08109A640C441E82D34F3863EFD6C1.description: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on developing models of molecules that vary in complexity. Examples of simple molecules could include ammonia and methanol. Examples of extended structures could include sodium chloride or diamonds. Examples of molecular-level models could include drawings, 3D ball and stick structures, or computer representations showing different molecules with different types of atoms.

Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include valence electrons and bonding energy, discussing the ionic nature of subunits of complex structures, or a complete depiction of all individual atoms in a complex molecule or extended structure.

985E5016285F4B0C8F004B8955E9F095.description: Analyze and interpret data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the analysis of data from Earth-based instruments, space-based telescopes, and spacecraft to determine similarities and differences among solar system objects. Examples of scale properties include the sizes of an object's layers (such as crust and atmosphere), surface features (such as volcanoes), and orbital radius. Examples of data include statistical information, drawings and photographs, and models.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include recalling facts about properties of the planets and other solar system bodies.

C21FA9CB84C244B195467D7815C1410B.description: Develop and use a model to describe the role of gravity in the motions within galaxies and the solar system.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis for the model is on gravity as the force that holds together the solar system and Milky Way galaxy and controls orbital motions within them. Examples of models can be physical (such as the analogy of distance along a football field or computer visualizations of elliptical orbits) or conceptual (such as mathematical proportions relative to the size of familiar objects such as their school or state).
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include Kepler's Laws of orbital motion or the apparent retrograde motion of the planets as viewed from Earth.

53FC83373B8E47219573F3F2BBD97752.description: Develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to describe the cyclic patterns of lunar phases, eclipses of the sun and moon, and seasons.
comments: Clarification Statement: Earth's rotation relative to the positions of the moon and sun describes the occurrence of tides; the revolution of Earth around the sun explains the annual cycle of the apparent movement of the constellations in the night sky; the moon's revolution around Earth explains the cycle of spring/neap tides and the occurrence of eclipses; the moon's elliptical orbit mostly explains the occurrence of total and annular eclipses. Examples of models can be physical, graphical, or conceptual.

Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on using models such as Punnett squares, diagrams, and simulations to describe the cause and effect relationship of gene transmission from parent(s) to offspring and resulting genetic variation.
Assessment Boundary: The assessment should measure the students' abilities to explain the general outcomes of sexual versus asexual reproduction in terms of variation seen in the offspring.
E8F2073941A1424CABBA5B3B6DB93E32.description: Develop and use a model to describe why asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information and sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation.

749FD0BDFBAC4821A1E6D31D00E12E35.description: Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

A954B9A387DD4A7995473560FEBF6998.description: Develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and rotation of the Earth causes patterns of atmospheric and oceanic circulation that determine regional climates.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how patterns vary by latitude, altitude, and geographic land distribution. Emphasis of atmospheric circulation is on the sunlight-driven latitudinal banding, the Coriolis effect, and resulting prevailing winds; emphasis of ocean circulation (e.g. el niño/la niña) is on the transfer of heat by the global ocean convection cycle, which is constrained by the Coriolis effect and the outlines of continents. Examples of models can be diagrams, maps and globes, or digital representations.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include the dynamics of the Coriolis effect.

6E70AB602EFA48E0BFFA584239D43BFF.description: Collect data to provide evidence for how the motions and complex interactions of air masses results in changes in weather conditions.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how air masses flow from regions of high pressure to low pressure, causing weather (defined by temperature, pressure, humidity, precipitation, and wind) at a fixed location to change over time, and how sudden changes in weather can result when different air masses collide. Emphasis is on how weather can be predicted within probabilistic ranges. Examples of data can be provided to students (such as weather maps, diagrams, and visualizations) or obtained through laboratory experiments (such as with condensation).
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include recalling the names of cloud types or weather symbols used on weather maps or the reported diagrams from weather stations.

062F047D24744628BF62ED16A02C5334.description: Develop and use a model to describe why structural changes to genes (mutations) located on chromosomes may affect proteins and may result in harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects to the structure and function of the organism.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on conceptual understanding that changes in genetic material may result in making different proteins. Examples: Radiation treated plants, genetically modified organisms (e.g. roundup resistant crops, bioluminescence), mutations both harmful and beneficial.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include specific changes at the molecular level, mechanisms for protein synthesis, or specific types of mutations.

Assessment Boundary: The assessment should provide evidence of students' abilities to provide a basic and conceptual explanation that sensory cells respond to stimuli in the environment and send electrical impulses to the brain where they are processed as either response or memory. Assessment does not include mechanisms for the transmission of this information.
9B6E80DC8D7144109BBDCB4A9CBC275F.description: Gather and synthesize information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli by sending messages to the brain for immediate behavior or storage as memories.

35BED9B4C5C24608A45881A19CE89116.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors influence the growth of organisms.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of local environmental conditions could include availability of food, light, space, and water. Examples of genetic factors could include large breed cattle and species of grass affecting growth of organisms. Examples of evidence could include drought decreasing plant growth, fertilizer increasing plant growth, different varieties of plant seeds growing at different rates in different conditions, and fish growing larger in large ponds than they do in small ponds.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include genetic mechanisms, gene regulation, or biochemical processes.

7D63C73420144BE7984540A9C29731E8.description: Use arguments based on empirical evidence and scientific reasoning to support an explanation for how characteristic animal behaviors and specialized plant structures affect the probability of successful reproduction of animals and plants respectively.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of behaviors that affect the probability of animal reproduction could include nest building to protect young from cold, herding of animals to protect young from predators, and vocalization of animals and colorful plumage to attract mates for breeding. Examples of animal behaviors that affect the probability of plant reproduction could include transferring pollen or seeds and creating conditions for seed germination and growth. Examples of plant structures could include bright flowers attracting butterflies that transfer pollen, flower nectar and odors that attract insects that transfer pollen, and hard shells on nuts that squirrels bury.

4859D27404854B1B9135AEBA605BECCF.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structure and Processes

7E9686F3631C4DCC8AF86BBC0880E5D4.description: Construct, use, and present arguments to support the claim that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of empirical evidence used in arguments could include an inventory or other representation of the energy before and after the transfer in the form of temperature changes or motion of object.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include calculations of energy.

A3EF4A3CB11548C1835549840429AC9D.description: Construct and present arguments using evidence to support the claim that gravitational interactions are attractive and depend on the masses of interacting objects.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of evidence for arguments could include data generated from simulations or digital tools; and charts displaying mass, strength of interaction, distance from the Sun, and orbital periods of objects within the solar system.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include Newton's Law of Gravitation or Kepler's Laws.

CFB5D8919FBA41B8951A1A28DAB71C50.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

22E3CBD0DFE701312F6468A86D17958E.description: Recognize and practice appropriate audience or performer behavior appropriate for the context and style of music performed.

22E389B0DFE701312F6368A86D17958E.description: Music Appreciation - The student will learn to appreciate music and expand listening beyond music currently familiar to the student

22E0BDB0DFE701312F5A68A86D17958E.description:
Recognize and identify the appropriate ways to use the following elements of musical style:
  1. Dynamics - (piano, forte)
  2. Tempo - (Allegro, Lento, Andante, Moderato)
  3. Conducting patterns of simple meters (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8)
  4. Articulation (staccato, legato, accent)

22E33F50DFE701312F6268A86D17958E.description: Identify uses of music in everyday life (film, television, background music, and commercials).

22E2AB00DFE701312F6068A86D17958E.description: Sing or play musical compositions demonstrating knowledge of tonal and rhythmic elements (including syncopated patterns, beats and offbeats).

22E25BD0DFE701312F5F68A86D17958E.description: Perform and create melodies and accompaniments in solo or group ensembles through singing and playing instruments (e.g. four-chord songs on autoharp).

22E1FD40DFE701312F5E68A86D17958E.description: Respond physically or using classroom instruments to basic rhythm patterns (including triplets, dotted rhythms, syncopation).

22E18D90DFE701312F5D68A86D17958E.description: Compose music using a variety of sound sources, including electronic and computer.

22E13EE0DFE701312F5C68A86D17958E.description: Sing with an acceptable tone quality throughout his/her singing ranges or play an instrument with an acceptable tone quality throughout an appropriate range.

22E0FF20DFE701312F5B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to read music from basic notation in treble or bass clef (e.g. folk songs, patriotic songs,).

22E07D40DFE701312F5968A86D17958E.description: Perform basic tonal patterns and rhythm patterns on classroom instruments (autoharp, recorder, percussion instruments, and guitar).

22E036F0DFE701312F5868A86D17958E.description: Music Expression - The student will perform, compose, improvise and arrange a variety of music within specified guidelines

22DFEC20DFE701312F5768A86D17958E.description:
Recognize, describe and listen to music from a variety of:
  1. Styles (jazz, mariachi band, opera, musical, call-response);
  2. Periods (Baroque, Classical, Romantic, Impressionism and Contemporary);
  3. Cultures including European, Native American, African American, Hispanic, and Asian.

22DF9FB0DFE701312F5668A86D17958E.description: Identify and differentiate the use of musical elements and instruments from other parts of the world and compare them to the use of musical elements in American music (patriotic, orchestral, band and folk).

22DF5EA0DFE701312F5568A86D17958E.description: Sing or play a variety of folk, ethnic, classical, and contemporary musical compositions.

22DF1E90DFE701312F5468A86D17958E.description: Music History and Culture - The student will recognize the development of music from an historical and cultural perspective

22DE96C0DFE701312F5268A86D17958E.description:
Define and use correct terminology to identify and discuss the elements of music including:
  1. Melody (steps, wide and narrow leaps, repeated tones, phrases, pentatonic scale [five-tone scale]).
  2. Rhythm (steady beat, back beat, syncopation, triplets, dotted rhythms, 2/2 meter).
  3. Harmony (partner songs, rounds, descants, countermelody, major and minor chords).
  4. Form (AB, ABA, round, rondo, theme and variations, introduction, coda, interlude, verse and refrain, prelude).
  5. Tone color (opera, musical theater, duet, trio, quartet, chorus, voice ranges and instrument ranges).
  6. Pitch (range and register).
  7. Tempo - allegro (fast), lento (slow), andante (walking), moderato (moderate).
  8. Dynamics - forte (loud), piano (soft), mezzo forte (medium loud), mezzo piano (medium soft).

22DEDE70DFE701312F5368A86D17958E.description:
Identify visually and aurally:
  1. instrumental ensembles (marching band, symphony orchestra, jazz band).
  2. families of orchestral instruments (strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion).
  3. classification of voice ranges (soprano, alto, tenor, bass).

22DE5500DFE701312F5168A86D17958E.description: Identify basic notational symbols (written representation of music), including: treble and bass clef, time signatures; (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, and 6/8); note values (whole note, half note, quarter note, eighth note, dotted half note, dotted quarter note, and the corresponding rests).

22DE0510DFE701312F5068A86D17958E.description: Experiment with variations in and demonstrate understanding of tempo (speed), tone quality (sound quality), dynamics (degree of loudness) and phrasing for expressive purpose in performing music.

22DDB1B0DFE701312F4F68A86D17958E.description: Notate (written representation of music) simple pitch and rhythm patterns presented aurally (listening).

22DD57A0DFE701312F4E68A86D17958E.description: Language of Music - The student will read, notate and interpret music.

22DC40C0DFE701312F4A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate appropriate behavior while attending a visual art exhibition in a museum or art gallery.

22DBD930DFE701312F4968A86D17958E.description: Visual Art Appreciation - The student will appreciate visual art as a vehicle of human expression.

Demonstrate a basic knowledge of media, techniques and processes in:
  • Painting
    • media: tempera, watercolor, oil, and acrylic.
    • processes: wet-on-wet, wet-on-dry, wash, resist, sponge.
  • Sculpture or Architecture
    • media: paper, papier-mâché, clay, plaster, cardboard, wood, found objects, beads, sand, wire.
    • processes: carving, constructing, and assembling
  • Drawing
    • media: pencils, colored pencils, markers, chalks, crayons, oil-pastels,
    • processes: sketching, contour line, hatching, crosshatching,
  • Printmaking
    • media: printing ink, styrofoam, stencil, found object.
    • processes: relief, silkscreen, and monoprint.
  • Fiber Arts
    • media: cloth, yarn, ribbon, found objects, paper, and rope
    • processes: weaving, stitchery, braiding, and basketry.

22DB56D0DFE701312F4768A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of a basic art vocabulary through experiences in making original works of art.

22DB19E0DFE701312F4668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate safe and proper use, care, and storage of media, materials, and equipment.

22DA9A90DFE701312F4468A86D17958E.description: Make original works of art using a variety materials (media), and techniques (skills), and sources for ideas.

22DADB60DFE701312F4568A86D17958E.description: Use observation, memory and imagination in making original works of art.

22DA54E0DFE701312F4368A86D17958E.description: Visual Art Expression - The student will observe, select, and utilize a variety of ideas and subject matter in creating original works of art.

22D9FD30DFE701312F4268A86D17958E.description: Communicate in-depth knowledge gained through integrated study of a visual art theme, historical period, or event.

22D7F360DFE701312F3B68A86D17958E.description: Compare works which are similar or different in expressive quality, composition, and style.

comments: The overall goal of Oklahoma's Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) for Physical Education is to promote the health and well-being of each student and guide them toward becoming physically active for life. The Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) are categorized under three major areas: Motor Skill and Lifetime Activity Development; Health-Enhancing Activity Development; and Personal and Social Skill Development. It is important to realize some skills are repeated because of the need for emphasizing those skills. Skills have been selected and placed under major headings to demonstrate the appropriateness of what is expected at the various grade levels.

comments: The Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) for Health and Safety represent standards that describe what students should know concerning health and safety. The standards are categorized under the following: HEALTH and SAFETY LITERACY, RESPONSIBLE HEALTH AND SAFETY BEHAVIOR, AND HEALTH AND SAFETY ADVOCACY. A well-informed, self-directed student has the foundation for leading a healthy, productive life. By recognizing that many health problems and causes of premature death can be prevented, children can reduce many of the risks generally encountered during adolescence and adulthood.

comments: The overall goal of Oklahoma's Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) for Physical Education is to promote the health and well-being of each student and guide them toward becoming physically active for life. The Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) are categorized under three major areas: Motor Skill and Lifetime Activity Development; Health-Enhancing Activity Development; and Personal and Social Skill Development. It is important to realize some skills are repeated because of the need for emphasizing those skills. Skills have been selected and placed under major headings to demonstrate the appropriateness of what is expected at the various grade levels.

comments: The overall goal of Oklahoma's Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) for Physical Education is to promote the health and well-being of each student and guide them toward becoming physically active for life. The Priority Academic Student Skills (PASS) are categorized under three major areas: Motor Skill and Lifetime Activity Development; Health-Enhancing Activity Development; and Personal and Social Skill Development. It is important to realize some skills are repeated because of the need for emphasizing those skills. Skills have been selected and placed under major headings to demonstrate the appropriateness of what is expected at the various grade levels.
