9F9905E701CA4E6997F6493F837D3B8A.description: Students will correctly form letters to write their first and last name and most uppercase and lowercase letters correctly.

3875259E1B2F41C6B5D2BD5EEC9B3981.description: Print Concepts: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the organization and basic features of print, including book handling skills and the understanding that printed materials provide information and tell stories.

9C3F8CFE1A4F4976855A91C7978B3322.description: Students will add, delete, and substitute phonemes in one syllable spoken words (e.g., "add /c/ to the beginning of "at" to say "cat;" "remove the /p/ from "pin," to say "in;" "change the /d/ in "dog" to /f/ /r/ to say "frog").

400F2FB326BE46D5A273489AABB0D35E.description: Students will segment phonemes in one syllable spoken words with 3 to 5 phonemes (e.g., "fast" = /f/ /a/ /s/ /t/).

867FFD16B71E4DC599594DB5D8EAAAC9.description: Students will blend phonemes to form one syllable spoken words with 3 to 5 phonemes (e.g., /f/ /a/ /s/ /t/= fast)

ACCC1C7CF51946798F3A55CF10148009.description: Students will blend and segment onset and rime in one syllable spoken words (e.g., Blending: /ch/ + at = chat; segmenting: cat = /c/+ at).

A7469D3191F64B2095747AF3942AFB91.description: Students will count, pronounce, blend, segment, and delete syllables in spoken words.

990AD6C48FCF435DA919A1238598FA74.description: Students will recognize the short or long vowel sound in one syllable words.

F21C730CC06C40FB85C8EF59DBEFA420.description: Students will isolate and pronounce the same initial sounds in a set of spoken words (i.e., alliteration) (e.g., "the puppy pounces").

C69D55163AF7404DB3815A8C7EE4727D.description: Students will recognize and produce pairs of rhyming words, and distinguish them from non-rhyming pairs.

8CA132FD6E414686A056C1C7739785E0.description: Students will distinguish spoken words in a sentence.

C7C613C777B640E8A71A477B3ABAB115.description: Phonological Awareness: Phonological awareness is the ability to recognize, think about, and manipulate sounds in spoken language without using text.

6532FBCFF8D04D8CB981F703DA3AC206.description: Reading Foundations - Students will develop foundational skills for future reading success by working with sounds, letters, and text.

2702582B3D4A4E5F8DCE3DCB4E78BD15.description: Students will work respectfully with others with guidance and support.

08F02394AA384F42BFFC959B2C80FB49.description: Students will orally describe personal interests or tell stories, facing the audience and speaking clearly in complete sentences and following implicit rules for conversation, including taking turns and staying on topic.

EB7110E1994F44C5901060911B3EA2B8.description: Writing: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening to create individual and group projects and presentations.

81E1E14024694F7F887C2C1E46764835.description: Students will follow one and two step directions.

9B02B298F4F14221B9ADD24872EAFC56.description: Students will engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts with peers and adults in small and large groups with guidance and support.

7FB7920AB25D4E95BB688002E6457184.description: Students will ask and answer questions to seek help, get information, or clarify about information presented orally or through text or other media with guidance and support.

4F479D53207C4F07881D20D431AB34D7.description: Students will actively listen and speak using agreed-upon rules for discussion with guidance and support.

226E7A181D774C12B3C85966464FC406.description: Reading: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening.

5B40A0978EDA4B96959D54E94FD9F440.description: Speaking and Listening - Students will speak and listen effectively in a variety of situations including, but not limited to, responses to reading and writing.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Physical Education

5BDE3200D8614C0DB0ECD9AB042EFB42.description: Analyzes the positive impact of verbal and non-verbal encouragement in physical activity.

F00A22BC66F446BBB39775292A20AA33.description: Analyzes different physical activities for enjoyment and challenge, identifying reasons for a positive or negative response.

CF10F16368134A7EBEB720D4F7E49FAE.description: Expresses (e.g., written essay, visual art, creative dance) the enjoyment and/or challenge of participating in a favorite physical activity.

2E131A5FAD8143A1B9606DD4C2BF91C9.description: Compares the health benefits of participating in selected physical activities.

4132BF619088414686F9A8D13A384C62.description: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction.

AD12F08E2954464CA2FDE6658E1B9889.description: Applies safety principles with age-appropriate physical activities.

0D9BE9F63D694D2C940F7B30C6272B3C.description: Critiques the etiquette involved in rules of various game activities.

816A6B36BAB044848620CD7C8BFA9E1B.description: Accepts, recognizes and actively involves others with both higher and lower skill abilities into physical activities and group projects.

C02885B9D6664AA2A1582657BC3FC157.description: Exhibits respect for self with appropriate behavior while engaging in physical activity.

DFF4EEE053224416B458F1CC68FA0878.description: Participates with responsible personal behavior in a variety of physical activity contexts, environments and facilities.

9FCAD5A8E43D41818CBF87BE6B72B15F.description: Engages in physical activity with responsible inter-personal behavior (e.g., peer to peer, student to teacher, student to referee).

09B7706774A44CBD841A242E2DC16AC6.description: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others.

9246F149A3FC464A8A540FF8EC7E2D55.description: Analyzes the impact of food choices relative to physical activity, youth sports and personal health.

750EF491EB4549A0BCB1F15900718806.description: Designs a fitness plan utilizing FITT.

AE5E91D107274D0F844FF6994B0A4A58.description: Analyzes results of fitness assessment (pre and post), comparing results with fitness components for good health.

8BBF7DE8958D4DF1AF33845FDB993BA7.description: Identify and apply FITT to a fitness plan.

B98751A628FF4209A965F316E4495CA0.description: Identifies the need for warm up and cool-down relative to various physical activities.

ACA559D7A3E349F494CAB4559A61ABBA.description: Differentiates between skill related and health related fitness.

C18F131033BB48F89E83EC96AE2ADE6F.description: Engaged in MVPA 50% of class time.

10FA03AF060648DE88A7F0A820B62C96.description: Actively engages in all the activities of physical education.

4ADFB39AACF4475A970E06C5BD3B15D7.description: Student charts and analyzes physical activity outside physical education class for fitness benefits of activities.

01EC364216534A3EB4DD645943C5A3B7.description: Demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness.

D75936D4E5294779BB65CDB0B6291D88.description: Recognizes the type of throw, volley or striking action needed for different games and sports situations.

610789CEE1BA401E827EC85F7BFB1DC7.description: Applies basic offensive & defensive strategies & tactics in invasion small-sided practice tasks, and in net/wall small-sided practice tasks.

1739527DB6AF41CCB8AC030599D29F11.description: Analyzes movement situations and applies movement concepts (e.g., force, direction, speed, pathways, extensions) in small-sided practice tasks in game environments, dance and gymnastics.

4524D00C7AFD4855BCA314E1025CC81C.description: Applies the concepts of direction and force to strike an object with a long-handled implement.

2708192D29B148A588C72BA910E7CF05.description: Applies movement concepts to strategy in game situations.

4F9B89638BFE4068926C9C364823C748.description: Combines movement concepts with skills in small-sided practice tasks in game environments, gymnastics & dance with self-direction.

866344DFFBC64366A0E7D822F7E507A2.description: Combines spatial concepts with locomotor and non-locomotor movements for small groups (e.g., gymnastics, dance, & games).

E57C914D7AA1476FA33CF221C9F68000.description: Applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance.

134E4FB2615945EFB1420260CA4B2CE9.description: Creates a jump rope routine with a partner using either a short or long jump rope.

AFF893531B454B07B69C611687EBCAE8.description: Combines manipulative skills and traveling for execution to a target. (e.g., scoring in soccer, hockey, and basketball).

26288DF3ED474AD780C2523B527ACBDA.description: Combines striking with a long-implement (e.g., bat, hockey stick) with receiving and traveling skills in a small-sided game.

15FF07EC15A6443AAF84C215AC10C9E7.description: Strikes a pitched ball with a bat using a mature pattern.

B9C117FCD55548C68256224E4BFE29F7.description: Strikes an object consecutively with a partner using a short-handled implement, over a net or against a wall, in either a competitive or cooperative game environment.

2EF109FDE10142BB82F00E02613987C3.description: Volleys the ball using a two-handed pattern sending it upward to a target.

C23364238F544A7AA67BE8EA59877ABC.description: Demonstrates mature patterns of kicking and punting in small-sided practice tasks environments.

913F85E5F3584E0B84E77099DA9CDD73.description: Dribbles with the hands or feet with mature patterns in a variety of small-sided game forms.

14E6FE6B68754C03B5DCEDED638E9A30.description: Passes and receives with the feet using a mature pattern as both partners travel.

5782E613AF8A4554ACD912214584A297.description: Combines foot dribbling with other skills in one vs. one practice tasks.

C22C7B7E254C495BAACE419765F2DB77.description: Combines hand dribbling with other skills during one vs. one practice skills.

3F6C7CB547E44598BCC020DF05002DD7.description: Catches with accuracy with both partners moving. Catches with reasonable accuracy in dynamic, small-sided practice tasks.

0B5BC0905B9148FF8D2A65EF3B044A13.description: Catches a batted ball above the head, at the chest or waist level, and along the ground using a mature pattern in a non-dynamic environment (closed skills).

D2014FF0953E4635A0BE44D22C8F953A.description: Throws with reasonable accuracy in dynamic, small-sided practice tasks.

1C3E77DE3BE941BDB5555E75906BF794.description: Throws with accuracy while both partners are moving.

DA0F2957488646C8BCE0EA17601941E1.description: Throws underhand/overhand to a large target with accuracy.

719F1DC9765B467EA797919015CEDC76.description: Throws underhand and overhand in a mature pattern in a non-dynamic environment with different sizes and types of objects.

F7A8CEA1E9E84555ABB3FAB0D5A21B0F.description: Combines traveling with balance and weight transfers to create a gymnastics sequence with and without equipment or apparatus.

C78CCBA9AF1B41E69B1A219FC0EF537A.description: Combines locomotor skills and movement concepts (levels, shapes, extensions, pathways, force, time, flow) to create and perform a dance with a group.

077294E0F3B648E8B2B0628B70BCB760.description: Performs curling, twisting, and stretching actions with correct application in dance, gymnastics, and small-sided practice tasks in game environments.

BF0E58233A634992A9FA8948899596F2.description: Transfers weight in gymnastic and dance environments.

ABB03958A5A64646B17BFBB97D717A47.description: Combines balance and transferring weight in a gymnastic sequence or dance with a partner.

804802EF2D3040FC9F326AD2FA15ACB3.description: Combines locomotor skills and cultural as well as creative dances (self and group) with correct rhythm and pattern.

2D40E023471E41A0B3417EE5337A901C.description: Combines jumping and landing patterns with locomotor and manipulative skills in dance, gymnastics, and small-sided practice tasks in game environments.

BAB9A3DB79AE4675830744D58C1949DD.description: Combines jumping and landing patterns with locomotor and manipulative skills in dance, gymnastics, and small-sided practice tasks in game environments.

F94A1D071E08495F979CEA7B1A37A807.description: Uses appropriate pacing for a variety of running distances.

E911AE59538C4944A7A2574A304650CE.description: Combines traveling with manipulative skills for execution to a target (e.g., scoring in soccer, hockey, and basketball).

6C6F1831796C489ABA0C14077AF1799E.description: Combines locomotor and manipulative skills in a variety of small-sided practice tasks and game environments.

E122D66A657543488838C88FAFAE9D82.description: Demonstrates mature patterns of locomotor skills in dynamic and small-sided practice tasks, gymnastics, and dance.

B431F8E0EFA14A3C8CB7BB1E08737869.description: Demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for English Language Arts

A8BF8FCD21BA4FD9B5049B8D053700D9.description: Students will write independently for extended and shorter periods of time through a combination of emergent and conventional writing with guidance and support.

B88AF01AA93947A4A7E266EDC1A5C24F.description: Writing: Students will write independently for extended periods of time. Students will vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task.

20E90C2F3368406B81C70349AFB90E74.description: Students will select appropriate texts for academic and personal purposes and read independently for extended periods of time with guidance and support.

CF4B6D0351CA4BB1B543A9BED31D320A.description: Reading: Students will read independently for a variety of purposes and for extended periods of time. Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes.

EBAC840469184A0CBE26BEDF703BD7EC.description: Independent Reading and Writing - Students will read and write for a variety of purposes including, but not limited to, academic and personal.

09E09DE8090441099AB47CBFE0FA4F02.description: Students will use visual displays to support verbal communication and clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

99EFB6BF6C89474F8537B95AB5A92017.description: Students will select and use appropriate technology or media to communicate with others with guidance and support.

449C902C82E94691815198BC5D6A3F6E.description: Writing: Students will create multimodal texts to communicate knowledge and develop arguments.

7547F11839E6407BA86A9DE1907C6DD4.description: Students will explore and compare how ideas and topics are depicted in a variety of media and formats.

55FB4DF322114C6ABB1CC3671EDA69CF.description: Students will use provided print and digital resources with guidance and support.

A80190250CD84A09913EAE34C6D963E5.description: Reading: Students will evaluate written, oral, visual, and digital texts in order to draw conclusions and analyze arguments.

9336217D8EC54548A5E58CD375F15FCC.description: Multimodal Literacies - Students will acquire, refine, and share knowledge through a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts.

5842FCDF5DB542539516C1B2BAE75670.description: Students will make informal presentations of information gathered.

F4743B955E894F258E9854B3F7DE26B2.description: Students will organize information found during group or individual research, using graphic organizers or other aids with guidance and support.

92AFA09D89024420B0605206B3669E33.description: Students will generate questions about topics of interest.

7AD1F72DE5484FAEBF66A2D513B2C3A6.description: Writing: Students will summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create reports, projects, papers, texts, and presentations for multiple purposes.

FA24E70990F3486B9C853293B6BF1F87.description: Students will identify the location and purpose of various visual and text reference sources.

948FC077C537479BAA9A143792D02BCF.description: Students will identify graphic features including photos, illustrations, titles, labels, headings, charts, and graphs to understand a text.

2EE86A9D41304E4DB657414ED9647B1B.description: Students will decide who can answer questions about their topic or what resources they will need to find the information.

388976786B394220A6FB34DD489B80BE.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize resources to acquire and refine knowledge.

1453384AE6D848629421F6EB36241530.description: Research - Students will engage in inquiry to acquire, refine, and share knowledge.

7A632478ED5D4D638BC03D4CDE70DD92.description: Students will compose grammatically correct simple and compound sentences and questions (interrogatives) with appropriate end marks.

B82A7EA5D688495F804031C7923E3FDB.description:
Students will capitalize:
  • the first letter of a sentence
  • proper names
  • months and days of the week

7B02163423874D45837199DD586AB4A0.description:
Writing: Students will demonstrate command of Standard English grammar, mechanics, and usage through writing and other modes of communication. These standards begin in Kindergarten. K.5.W.1 Students will capitalize, with guidance and support:
  • their first name
  • the pronoun "I."

374696B4D7594CFEAF36F4B3ACD0CC1B.description: Students will recognize singular and plural nouns with correct verbs in simple sentences (e.g. He sits; we sit).

9E43E4483EF940A39E5A9354E727E2EF.description: Students will recognize the prepositions (e.g., The dog is on top of the doghouse) through pictures and movement.

3F248D5FF3E14C2E8A1A90E5910AFC35.description: Students will recognize color and number adjectives.

696DD0DD84EA43D380BC0664588BD457.description: Students will recognize verbs as actions

DFD96EC9C0E04B2883838C1CD5196D68.description: Students will recognize nouns as concrete objects (i.e., people persons, places, and things) and use the pronoun "I".

6BCEDF05C209495BA170470E686695B2.description: Reading: Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to analyze and evaluate a variety of texts.

197230E23A7C47E7A3791FE1B13F19F0.description: Language - Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to reading and writing.

3E9ED355CE124A9F9CA4E98F6DF9F2CA.description: Students will select appropriate language according to purpose in writing with guidance and support.

154C729BA1FA46D7B236B7E5B1594DA6.description: Students will use domain-appropriate vocabulary to communicate ideas in writing with guidance and support.

F58E597006A942DDA7D4735C64A3E432.description: Writing: Students will apply knowledge of vocabularies to communicate by using descriptive, academic, and domain-appropriate abstract and concrete words in their writing.

989603E7D8A14E58B3C9F90A12644D4E.description: Students will use a dictionary (print and/or electronic) to find words.

319105444D6A46B4BEE8B0C4FDD29875.description: Students will name and sort words into categories based on common attributes.

B5BBA6F80FD0426C8C7D91760A077B6E.description: Students will use context clues to determine the meaning of words with guidance and support.

D876A9FE8CC54FBE8D758282184EFC0D.description: Students will use word parts (e.g., affixes, roots, stems) to define unfamiliar words with guidance and support.

EF069D5EF19342B7B599650AB1D0144C.description: Students will acquire new academic, content-specific, grade-level vocabulary, relate new words to prior knowledge, and apply vocabulary in new situations.

6132636675E242AABC37C6663009DCD0.description: Reading: Students will expand academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabularies through reading, word study, and class discussion.

F4AD94D46C9A439B8AEFE586E6BABF7D.description: Vocabulary - Students will expand their working vocabularies to effectively communicate and understand texts.

F30496E65C124262933C1841A7F99866.description: Opinion: Students will express an opinion in writing about a topic and provide a reason to support the opinion.

CAF75BEC03774D85B74E0DE2BC07CD80.description: Informative: Students will begin to write facts about a subject in response to a text read aloud to demonstrate understanding with guidance and support.

EE7C8E194FFE4EEA95DFC8FC359934AC.description: Narrative: Students will begin to write narratives incorporating characters, plot (i.e., beginning, middle, end) , and a basic setting (i.e., time, place) with guidance and support.

22284A828C7846539FA9FAE838F41DBE.description: Writing: Students will write for varied purposes and audiences in all modes, using fully developed ideas, strong organization, well-chosen words, fluent sentences, and appropriate voice.

531E983BB51E42E58A5D68DB9F081653.description: Students will begin to locate facts that are clearly stated in a text.

4BFF773B19E048438502E485B9D8F48F.description: Students will ask and answer basic questions (e.g., who, what, where, why, and when) about texts.

6BD1B47094CF41A3A515A7D87E0A0909.description:
Students will find textual evidence when provided with examples of literary elements and organization:
  • setting (i.e., time, place)
  • plot
  • main characters and their traits in a story

4CC1126B39FE4A7F8C43AB92A96C2785.description: Students will describe who is telling the story (i.e., point of view).

CBAE5236F9F24EB9B573B27CE993781E.description: Students will identify the author's purpose (i.e., tell a story, provide information) with guidance and support.

4AE924BA11E3447EBBDD1A26D8B8152E.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts of all literary and informational genres from a variety of historical, cultural, ethnic, and global perspectives.

630A850BCF894C91B5369FAD6CCB7100.description: Critical Reading and Writing - Students will apply critical thinking skills to reading and writing.

DC3B53723E044770ABB865B8B000C10C.description: Students will use resources to find correct spellings of words (e.g., word wall, vocabulary notebook).

8EA1AE25E7154290AE06C5509949D12A.description: Students will correctly spell grade-appropriate, highly decodable words (e.g., cup, like, cart) and common, irregularly spelled sight words (e.g., the) while editing.

3AE05C21E89A46B7A6A1927876175C3D.description: Students will develop drafts by sequencing the action or details in a story or about a topic through writing sentences with guidance and support.

5D5E314A9B454146844DD7DC7F829CB5.description: Students will develop and edit first drafts using appropriate spacing between letters, words, and sentences using left-to-right and top-to-bottom progression.

704F9959CF044558B3D7D33668FDA4D6.description: Writing: Students will develop and strengthen writing by engaging in a recursive process that includes prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, and publishing.

E382793790A8474A954FC757813936EE.description: Students will sequence the events/plot (i.e., beginning, middle, and end) of a story or text.

DCCE6E63C4E94D3397837D64F10516FE.description: Students will discriminate between fiction and nonfiction/informational text.

1946B323AADC4916A8444FAC134E40B3.description: Students will retell or reenact major events in a text, focusing on important details to recognize the main idea.

67233483B8104205903E8023517C8DF4.description: Reading: Students will read and comprehend increasingly complex literary and informational texts.

F4E69196A9BB4612885CC81D637010FF.description: Reading and Writing Process - Students will use a variety of recursive reading and writing processes.

46B574BFD14E4B62BE036C55A129F407.description: Students will orally read grade-level text at an appropriate rate, smoothly and accurately, with expression that connotes comprehension.

86EA67B418FD497FA4C8CDBEB9C3EA4A.description: Students will read high frequency and/or common irregularly spelled grade-level words with automaticity in text.

5FBF1832F8C54AD4996FB2FD356C34C9.description: Fluency: Students will recognize high-frequency words and read grade-level text smoothly and accurately, with expression that connotes comprehension.

F44BB42C4A6D4F84B8476FF3A5568FA1.description: Students will read words in common word families (e.g., -at, -ab, -am, -in).

8276701622E542B7824AF2EFDCCA947D.description:
Students will decode words by applying knowledge of structural analysis:
  • most major syllable patterns (e.g., closed, open, vowel team, vowel silent e, r-controlled)
  • inflectional endings (e.g., -s, -ed, -ing)
  • compound words
  • contractions

CC7A5E35716F4A93B4F09E2CBEB5ED42.description:
Students will decode phonetically regular words by using their knowledge of:
  • single consonants (e.g., c = /k/, c = /s/, s = /s/, s = /z/, x = /ks/, x = /z/)
  • consonant blends (e.g., bl, br, cr)
  • consonant digraphs and trigraphs (e.g., sh-, -tch)
  • vowel sounds:
    • long
    • short
  • r -controlled vowels (e.g., ar, er, ir or, ur)
  • vowel spelling patterns:
    • vowel digraphs (e.g., ea, oa, ee)
    • vowel-consonant-silent-e (e.g., lake)

A38BC2F5B60244D482DC2D8788579584.description: Phonics and Word Study: Students will decode and read words in context and isolation by applying phonics and word analysis skills.

5AE4CF7F51E74710AD2E6E9B7F677A2C.description: Students will recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., capitalization of the first word, ending punctuation, comma, quotation marks).

4A07F26280FE4AAAB844C7F821FD07EB.description: Students will correctly form letters and use appropriate spacing for letters, words, and sentences using left-to-right and top-to-bottom progression.

23F8BCABBDE944D58BE69854DEDA0598.description: Print Concepts: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the organization and basic features of print, including book handling skills and the understanding that printed materials provide information and tell stories.

0B580391E08C47C09C0A8C65ADABCD01.description: Students will add, delete, and substitute phonemes in spoken words (e.g., "add /g/ to the beginning of low to say 'glow;' "remove the /idge/ from 'bridge,' to say 'br;' "change the /ar/ in 'charm' to /u/ to say 'chum').

E5E9A933567F44FF89C6923CA49011F4.description: Students will segment phonemes in spoken words with 4 to 6 phonemes into individual phonemes (e.g. string= /s/ /t/ /r/ /i/ /ng/).

0AE4956CD9DF4BE28C3F76AD2ED329F6.description: Students will blend phonemes to form spoken words with 4 to 6 phonemes including consonant blends (e.g., /s/ /t/ /r/ /i/ /ng/ = string).

41B51311AC99438BA91D89710C1D0423.description: Students will isolate and pronounce initial, medial, and final sounds in spoken words.

F6FC2C2B546D4CE187EFFF87DFA988C8.description: Students will differentiate short from long vowel sounds in one syllable words.

BE8E1A0202064160953B60BDAC34F7BC.description: Students will blend and segment onset and rime in spoken words (e.g., /ch/+ /at/ = chat).

F8E293D1C1BA4E58B28FD4BD518CEE36.description: Phonological Awareness: Phonological awareness is the ability to recognize, think about, and manipulate sounds in spoken language without using text.

66B8C118BBD04F6395D10318AA25A5AB.description: Reading Foundations - Students will develop foundational skills for future reading success by working with sounds, letters, and text.

1835CE0D28B345AB917B7183FF420EC7.description: Students will work respectfully in groups.

85572EEEEC0B49E9AF3AB59421537E56.description: Students will orally describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details expressing their ideas.

3ECEC1AE7C3A49CCA73765E07FE06760.description: Writing: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening to create individual and group projects and presentations.

CE06BE94F3B5458A808C68D7AE18002A.description: Students will restate and follow simple two-step directions.

8E7A1B5496304B368461855C01ADFF69.description: Students will engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts with peers and adults in small and large groups.

6156FAED380A4EEA9CA65EAD847D00AB.description: Students will ask and answer questions to seek help, get information, or clarify about information presented orally through text or other media, to confirm understanding.

5442CC7B1EF74C89950B0AF77006B0DA.description: Students will actively listen and speak using agreed-upon rules for discussion.

18120E7AD215450392634E5B0D2D7205.description: Reading: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening.

A10B0EB5CDC24166B0EA4F26D8BDC21D.description: Speaking and Listening - Students will speak and listen effectively in a variety of situations including, but not limited to, responses to reading and writing.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Mathematics

AE1FEB5DDACA474DB0810BCBA2E75E8D.description: Identify and explain misleading uses of data. Recognize when arguments based on data confuse correlation and causation.

19C99E91DF434A8ABD148B8D4AB1BA31.description: Evaluate reports based on data published in the media by identifying the source of the data, the design of the study, and the way the data are analyzed and displayed. Given spreadsheets, tables, or graphs, recognize and analyze distortions in data displays. Show how graphs and data can be distorted to support different points of view.

8CD83944DDCC468A9A8423AAA1E9BB41.description: Analyze statistical thinking to draw inferences, make predictions, and justify conclusions.

F311ED79AB814FCAA2DDFDE56BF166D3.description: Based upon a real-world context, recognize whether a discrete or continuous graphical representation is appropriate and then create the graph.

905F6F250F764D68AE7C7789E9A398CC.description: Collect data and use scatterplots to analyze patterns and describe linear, exponential or quadratic relationships between two variables. Using graphing calculators or other appropriate technology, determine regression equation and correlation coefficients; use regression equations to make predictions and correlation coefficients to assess the reliability of those predictions.

B95E56D526B74D078BB434D4C3B5B289.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution (bell-shaped curve).

3F4A1ED5D7DB4D1E8BBB11AD7E32DA3C.description: Display, describe, and compare data. For linear and nonlinear relationships, make predictions and assess the reliability of those predictions.

B85908B9C5A94D088DAFC43A05EF08A4.description: Apply the inverse relationship between exponential and logarithmic functions to convert from one form to another.

E2E43966392347F6A9DA2310A97C6854.description: Find and graph the inverse of a function, if it exists, in real-world and mathematical situations. Know that the domain of a function f is the range of the inverse function f<sup>-1</sup>, and the range of the function f is the domain of the inverse function f<sup>-1</sup>.

89E802F7C5CF4040B7EB6D101EA0A552.description: Combine functions by composition and recognize that g(x) = f<sup>-1</sup>(x), the inverse function of f(x), if and only if f(g(x)) = g(f(x)) = x.

574487BE64114FEE8915CD2067B25DF9.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide functions using function notation and recognize domain restrictions.

1C2409C88EA4469AA04E4AF9C8B8A5F1.description: Analyze functions through algebraic combinations, compositions, and inverses, if they exist.

5CF1AE606C2840178CB3394EDACDDCDC.description: Graph piecewise functions with no more than three branches (including linear, quadratic, or exponential branches) and analyze the function by identifying the domain, range, intercepts, and intervals for which it is increasing, decreasing, and constant.

8B684C4949C44C93AA73EDED9EE26C6A.description: Graph a radical function (square root and cube root only) and identify the x- and y-intercepts using various methods and tools that may include a graphing calculator or other appropriate technology.

6AAA29E63E6D4EAB9DD26CD445221463.description: Graph a rational function and identify the x- and y-intercepts, vertical and horizontal asymptotes, using various methods and tools that may include a graphing calculator or other appropriate technology. (Excluding slant or oblique asymptotes and holes.)

97606D1F578141B3BF489E6B5A389716.description: Analyze the graph of a polynomial function by identifying the domain, range, intercepts, zeros, relative maxima, relative minima, and intervals of increase and decrease.

CAAF21B4005349C6ADC8D9CA4ABD2647.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions. Identify asymptotes and x- and y-intercepts using various methods and tools that may include graphing calculators or other appropriate technology. Recognize exponential decay and growth graphically and algebraically.

1285A92EE5F3437899861EE06A04C4E4.description: Graph a quadratic function. Identify the x- and y-intercepts, maximum or minimum value, axis of symmetry, and vertex using various methods and tools that may include a graphing calculator or appropriate technology.

6919BFDEA339470E9B0E6C8B00011B81.description: Recognize the graphs of exponential, radical (square root and cube root only), quadratic, and logarithmic functions. Predict the effects of transformations [f(x + c), f(x) + c, f(cx), and cf(x), where c is a positive or negative real-valued constant] algebraically and graphically, using various methods and tools that may include graphing calculators or other appropriate technology.

17647E6FD3F24373B0C399C3C640B10C.description: Use algebraic, interval, and set notations to specify the domain and range of functions of various types and evaluate a function at a given point in its domain.

785F45E4A1E04CA2ADAA129789466D6A.description: Understand functions as descriptions of covariation (how related quantities vary together).

E9AEA079858B42EF909B6BFE8405E990.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

2054C5FED33442BFAAAB6FB638343809.description: Recognize that a quadratic function has different equivalent representations [f(x) = ax² + bx + c, f(x) = a(x − h)² + k, and f(x) = (x − h)(x − k)]. Identify and use the representation that is most appropriate to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

EED09617CAA94E4497B2C0B28BEB0A95.description: Add, subtract, multiply, divide, and simplify polynomial and rational expressions.

461A2E6D1E1945EEACC2DC422BBE04CE.description: Factor polynomial expressions including but not limited to trinomials, differences of squares, sum and difference of cubes, and factoring by grouping using a variety of tools and strategies.

38D89DC0352C44E7A2478339D24C3C88.description: Represent and analyze mathematical situations and structures using algebraic symbols using various strategies to write equivalent forms of expressions.

D7490C84F77448939DE4B66D67F7B29A.description: Solve systems of equations containing one linear equation and one quadratic equation using tools that may include graphing calculators or other appropriate technology.

4FB2779543424CFBA66E3FE5BDBA2303.description: Represent real-world or mathematical problems using systems of linear equations with a maximum of three variables and solve using various methods that may include substitution, elimination, and graphing (may include graphing calculators or other appropriate technology).

02FFBB0673A0464EB31D9CEFF496FE3B.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems that can be modeled using arithmetic or finite geometric sequences or series given the n<sup>th</sup> terms and sum formulas. Graphing calculators or other appropriate technology may be used.

AEB3EB4630FE46C888D585EF5B917D93.description: Solve common and natural logarithmic equations using the properties of logarithms.

935F364F325C4E59A8A392D28E302DF8.description: Solve square root equations with one variable and check for extraneous solutions.

8EBF9448EF314A2DAF092BDEAFE705CD.description: Solve polynomial equations with real roots using various methods and tools that may include factoring, polynomial division, synthetic division, graphing calculators or other appropriate technology.

A6372BB11B344A41BCAB3F42E75C1203.description: Solve one-variable rational equations and check for extraneous solutions.

3BE748FC93A9499D8DE1B8C0C7F83961.description: Represent real-world or mathematical problems using exponential equations, such as compound interest, depreciation, and population growth, and solve these equations graphically (including graphing calculator or other appropriate technology) or algebraically.

0C16416ABCE1454A99CA8584524643B9.description: Represent real-world or mathematical problems using quadratic equations and solve using various methods (including graphing calculator or other appropriate technology), factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula. Find non-real roots when they exist.

2A208A9D0BA04B6F88F3B54808C41040.description: Represent and solve mathematical and real-world problems using nonlinear equations and systems of linear equations; interpret the solutions in the original context.

915CE93020A54FCCB08D97EB34D9F7C1.description: Understand and apply the relationship of rational exponents to integer exponents and radicals to solve problems.

622D9481B98947329A395FBA8E5B0B1A.description: Use matrices to organize and represent data. Identify the order (dimension) of a matrix, add and subtract matrices of appropriate dimensions, and multiply a matrix by a scalar to create a new matrix to solve problems.

3C49EF39534E4B0D9F935BD8DE8A0DBB.description: Simplify, add, subtract, multiply, and divide complex numbers.

047D38600B2F448F9CB194538295AE4C.description: Find the value of i<sup>n</sup> for any whole number n.

E54427759B844FD388817D9E7F9F5819.description: Extend the understanding of number and operations to include complex numbers, matrices, radical expressions, and expressions written with rational exponents.

96A5EB86ABA942338443E47B704372B4.description: Apply the trigonometric functions as ratios (sine, cosine, and tangent) to find side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems.

78AFB0024A5F4D499183B71B5048E7E4.description: Use the definition of the trigonometric functions to determine the sine, cosine, and tangent ratio of an acute angle in a right triangle. Apply the inverse trigonometric functions to find the measure of an acute angle in right triangles.

A45A9707C3224A99AE8A4AA8B1D1DE96.description: Verify and apply properties of right triangles, including properties of 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles, to solve problems using algebraic and logical reasoning.

3D4B90E7FE784DC2BD203D482D58C3B9.description: Apply the distance formula and the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse to solve real-world and mathematical problems, as approximate and exact values, using algebraic and logical reasoning (include Pythagorean Triples).

ABF44C929DF9429AAB7FF8F7ABCFE39C.description: Develop and verify mathematical relationships of right triangles and trigonometric ratios to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

5B6633F8C81D42E3B410BB9EAC692695.description: Apply the distance and midpoint formula, where appropriate, to develop the equation of a circle in standard form.

40CC11FD0D5F4CC29D84FABDFD610168.description: Recognize and write the radius r, center (h,k), and standard form of the equation of a circle (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² with and without graphs.

B93AF1509F8644F68C95AC11ABCB8C7B.description: Apply the properties of circles and relationships among angles; arcs; and distances in a circle among radii, chords, secants and tangents to solve problems using algebraic and logical reasoning.

3975073366694EF5B1FDA60225C9F3E5.description: Apply the properties of circles to solve problems involving circumference and area, approximate values and in terms of π, using algebraic and logical reasoning.

B61917203D224082AE23C4DAD89426E8.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems using the properties of circles.

E82B20AF3D9841B3A013B1F01A553EB1.description: Use ratios derived from similar three-dimensional figures to make conjectures, generalize, and to solve for unknown values such as angles, side lengths, perimeter or circumference of a face, area of a face, and volume.

395DEDF072C040EFB95A6B43DAC1FE89.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems using the surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, spheres, and composites of these figures. Use nets, measuring devices, or formulas as appropriate.

C8E51461FEEE4F07895245865A609890.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving three-dimensional figures.

BE98F75E19CE43F7BE57AA1EB6AD6E81.description: Use numeric, graphic and algebraic representations of transformations in two dimensions, such as reflections, translations, dilations, and rotations about the origin by multiples of 90̊, to solve problems involving figures on a coordinate plane and identify types of symmetry.

A15475CC223044079767D6F24AAE6319.description: Construct logical arguments to prove triangle congruence (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and HL) and triangle similarity (AA, SSS, SAS).

5E7D180FB4C943B49A35A294351CD46A.description: Apply the properties of congruent or similar polygons to solve real-world and mathematical problems using algebraic and logical reasoning.

BBC36F047743449A85495E69FA592C23.description: Apply the properties of polygons to solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeter and area (e.g., triangles, special quadrilaterals, regular polygons up to 12 sides, composite figures).

CCFDDD399D7944B58916532BDBC3D61B.description: Use coordinate geometry to represent and analyze line segments and polygons, including determining lengths, midpoints, and slopes of line segments.

ECCA24C0625C43F88F92025BFA6897BE.description: Apply the properties of special quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, trapezoid, isosceles trapezoid, rhombus, kite, parallelogram) and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems involving angle measures and segment lengths using algebraic reasoning and proofs.

51F75C4839B345EF90B087CDB8C831DD.description: Apply theorems involving the interior and exterior angle sums of polygons and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems using algebraic reasoning and proofs.

6B1A010C8E4D44E59CD9032D2EEFD017.description: Apply the properties of angles, including corresponding, exterior, interior, vertical, complementary, and supplementary angles to solve real-world and mathematical problems using algebraic reasoning and proofs.

4196286357B940929BFE7EB9B1F1F731.description: Apply the properties of parallel and perpendicular lines, including properties of angles formed by a transversal, to solve real-world and mathematical problems and determine if two lines are parallel, using algebraic reasoning and proofs.

145DF9639B1742F3885C791CC8103677.description: Discover, evaluate and analyze the relationships between lines, angles, and polygons to solve real-world and mathematical problems; express proofs in a form that clearly justifies the reasoning, such as two-column proofs, paragraph proofs, flow charts, or illustrations.

773A738FE71C4FA28B9720BC0E8D3EB8.description: Assess the validity of a logical argument and give counterexamples to disprove a statement.

AEA0039AA3854BD090211FD3FACD089F.description: Analyze and draw conclusions based on a set of conditions using inductive and deductive reasoning. Recognize the logical relationships between a conditional statement and its inverse, converse, and contrapositive.

DD99B6848FA84E4AB7D79C9635F7E2D0.description: Understand the use of undefined terms, definitions, postulates, and theorems in logical arguments/proofs.

1CE994BB4B24494A91F0793FDEAC223A.description: Use appropriate tools and logic to evaluate mathematical arguments.

E3B6486DA895490088AA185F6AF3A735.description: Apply probability concepts to real-world situations to make informed decisions.

BF8AA27FE7E14C9BB1F3FB0D50D07D7E.description: Calculate experimental probabilities by performing simulations or experiments involving a probability model and using relative frequencies of outcomes.

333EFEFC79484B648612F8EA003E6909.description: Describe the concepts of intersections, unions, and complements using Venn diagrams to evaluate probabilities. Understand the relationships between these concepts and the words AND, OR, and NOT.

F97045909B37453B8E27A099218C24E7.description: Select and apply counting procedures, such as the multiplication and addition principles and tree diagrams, to determine the size of a sample space (the number of possible outcomes) and to calculate probabilities.

3B34BE99867841938A51E940DA5C0212.description: Calculate probabilities and apply probability concepts.

E167F25B9BF7444D86FCE3EFD6BE058B.description: Interpret graphs as being discrete or continuous.

97D86FF276F34C58AF23A2E8A589BBB4.description: Collect data and use scatterplots to analyze patterns and describe linear relationships between two variables. Using graphing technology, determine regression lines and correlation coefficients; use regression lines to make predictions and correlation coefficients to assess the reliability of those predictions.

2ADDE1284AA44920A64DD4D9AEF288BB.description: Describe a data set using data displays, describe and compare data sets using summary statistics, including measures of central tendency, location, and spread. Know how to use calculators, spreadsheets, or other appropriate technology to display data and calculate summary statistics.

A1BEB91DFE2B4B47A211E7BDA7E19944.description: Display, describe, and compare data. For linear relationships, make predictions and assess the reliability of those predictions.

57E8DFDBFBCB4E0196D0B5F2104303CE.description: Add, subtract, and multiply functions using function notation.

32CD9D80C2464A2AB0AD1431590FA7CC.description: Use function notation; evaluate a function, including nonlinear, at a given point in its domain algebraically and graphically. Interpret the results in terms of real-world and mathematical problems.

A2543BE094FA4158A9D40B9ECB043813.description: Identify and generate equivalent representations of linear equations, graphs, tables, and real-world situations.

FF981BC03347414B98B73B15B2F4846C.description: Represent functions in multiple ways and use the representation to interpret real-world and mathematical problems.

FECDED0C1EF34A9B97EB3F31BB055A0D.description: Recognize the graph of the functions f(x) = x and f(x) = |x| and predict the effects of transformations [f(x + c) and f(x) + c, where c is a positive or negative constant] algebraically and graphically using various methods and tools that may include graphing calculators.

5F9ACBAA807A4775886EB9ACC1D71D28.description: Distinguish between linear and nonlinear (including exponential) functions arising from real-world and mathematical situations that are represented in tables, graphs, and equations. Understand that linear functions grow by equal intervals and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

03C6CECC2AF240849655867469F384BF.description: Recognize functions and understand that families of functions are characterized by their rate of change.

EE0F17FD0B954EDAB5A927E39A92C6D1.description: Given a graph modeling a real-world situation, read and interpret the linear piecewise function (excluding step functions).

56A880636C714F2D8E53C2C19DC16CFB.description: Write linear functions, using function notation, to model real-world and mathematical situations.

FAE4A225B6484B0F96373D4FB6EF6382.description: Identify the dependent and independent variables as well as the domain and range given a function, equation, or graph. Identify restrictions on the domain and range in real-world contexts.

028E3980546445EDAF24DEE62B27C923.description: Understand functions as descriptions of covariation (how related quantities vary together) in real-world and mathematical problems.

0578411C4DFA4E8584C63EFFB01F7CFB.description: Translate between a graph and a situation described qualitatively.

02BFCED4137540CCB8EB8BF591ACC7B1.description: Express linear equations in slope-intercept, point-slope, and standard forms and convert between these forms. Given sufficient information (slope and y-intercept, slope and one-point on the line, two points on the line, x- and y-intercept, or a set of data points), write the equation of a line.

E1729840F6374164B5414045A378781C.description: Solve mathematical and real-world problems involving lines that are parallel, perpendicular, horizontal, or vertical.

F7E282F2BFD9413A9859F9531A42C8DA.description: Calculate and interpret slope and the x- and y-intercepts of a line using a graph, an equation, two points, or a set of data points to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

9A4BC7D08A424F46928626C5B32EADB7.description: Analyze mathematical change involving linear equations in real-world and mathematical problems.

4DDE58B2504142B083DB831E88DC5B42.description: Recognize that geometric sequences are exponential using equations, tables, graphs and verbal descriptions. Given the formula f(x) = a(r)<sup>x</sup>, find the next term and define the meaning of a and r within the context of the problem.

04A73C3F93BD46FBA4C91389C8EA7C80.description: Recognize that arithmetic sequences are linear using equations, tables, graphs, and verbal descriptions. Use the pattern, find the next term.

0CC6510D1D444313B75FEA321AD2E524.description: Evaluate linear, absolute value, rational, and radical expressions. Include applying a nonstandard operation such as a⊙b = 2a + b.

ACDA8D9B8A874CBC98A33DC5ABD77FD9.description: Factor common monomial factors from polynomial expressions and factor quadratic expressions with a leading coefficient of 1.

826BAFB2C6914E82928F94A022B7EC3E.description: Simplify polynomial expressions by adding, subtracting, or multiplying.

252B94794D2943368F0F52D0290CB900.description: Solve equations involving several variables for one variable in terms of the others.

98A247C1E4E148969752A055A677B5E0.description: Generate equivalent algebraic expressions and use algebraic properties to evaluate expressions and arithmetic and geometric sequences.

3B7169D1A0BA4E06995FC3199F9072CB.description: Solve systems of linear inequalities with a maximum of two variables; graph and interpret the solutions on a coordinate plane.

70FC4899348940A5B9B4C3AA2CD599A4.description: Represent relationships in various contexts with compound and absolute value inequalities and solve the resulting inequalities by graphing and interpreting the solutions on a number line.

96E6F7CB9E4B429EBC543290049A3483.description: Represent relationships in various contexts with linear inequalities; solve the resulting inequalities, graph on a coordinate plane, and interpret the solutions.

89D29CD2B050486D8DAADD97877D8FB5.description: Represent and solve real-world and mathematical problems using linear inequalities, compound inequalities and systems of linear inequalities; interpret solutions in the original context.

C7807F270B45495693C4F5966197B319.description: Analyze and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving systems of linear equations with a maximum of two variables by graphing (may include graphing calculator or other appropriate technology), substitution, and elimination. Interpret the solutions in the original context.

A7DA5B321404452298061BC9BBA869AD.description: Solve absolute value equations and interpret the solutions in the original context.

BAE432171CBD4233B727F4B75038A1A7.description: Use knowledge of solving equations with rational values to represent and solve mathematical and real-world problems (e.g., angle measures, geometric formulas, science, or statistics) and interpret the solutions in the original context.

3922970D444E4A54830F51FBB6DC4333.description: Represent and solve mathematical and real-world problems using linear equations, absolute value equations, and systems of equations; interpret solutions in the original context.

45552378DF05414AB168C7CD354A3AD4.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and simplify square roots of monomial algebraic expressions and divide square roots of whole numbers, rationalizing the denominator when necessary.

DBC766814AE54C72AD87AA31D695EFBA.description: Write square roots and cube roots of monomial algebraic expressions in simplest radical form.

9D91B202D2DE40BA83FFEF3DCD01527E.description: Extend the understanding of number and operations to include square roots and cube roots.

53976C5263F14D3AA01996F20593E3EC.description: Develop the ability to communicate mathematically

752477ECCC314CDBAD7EF1737922EA46.description: Develop the ability to make conjectures, model, and generalize

DB8EFEB47CDE4C038D03676BE9145708.description: Develop accurate and appropriate procedural fluency

557529490F5A42C2B873DC69ADFB0F5E.description: Develop a deep and flexible conceptual understanding

document.title: Practical Nursing

3B9A970A5316447782FC775C306FF5DF.description: Evaluate patient needs, strengths and problems in order to determine if treatment goals are being met.

AB654F404322414592CED030E9CE2570.description: Utilize processes for assessing, monitoring and reporting patient's health status to the treatment team within protocol and scope of practice.

6E1AA071E0EC44CABB5A673453E50B16.description: Communicate patient information among healthcare team members to facilitate a team approach to patient care.

DF4C40F4853149EF919CEC5CBB7D7382.description: Utilize communication strategies to answer patient questions and concerns on planned procedures and goals.

AB02EFBC60AA49C683580AA80E4E60A8.description: Implement healthcare facility standards in order to maintain high-quality healthcare facilities.

6C3221B323484F8B9EAFD416EC2A43F4.description: Maximize available resources for proper care and use of healthcare equipment and materials.

0C14BB4C5E8A47EA93891BA47769A900.description: Follow established internal and external guidelines in order to provide high-quality, effective support services in the healthcare facility.

202A3CB6F4EB418F9E6A4512526749D7.description: Demonstrate work practices that maintain a clean and healthy healthcare facility to reduce or eliminate pathogenic organisms.

7AB8A3F171FE4BA4B2FEEFF3B9617AF7.description: Describe, differentiate and safely perform the responsibilities of healthcare support services roles.

39F4BC2A5E1C421BA908CF83BBBABDF7.description: Demonstrate the use of systems used to capture, retrieve and maintain confidential health information from internal and external sources.

9BC31477833A450E8E5413EC683A4800.description: Describe the content and diverse uses of health information.

55D82EF22BEB436484BC16C6C0EC3B58.description: Communicate health information accurately and within legal and regulatory guidelines, upholding the strictest standards of confidentiality.

BD40E77D988542CC97D24CADE36BD500.description: Select, demonstrate and interpret diagnostic procedures.

1B9A79DE61EB492CB3F73DCE91F9E778.description: Explain procedures and goals to the patient accurately and effectively, using strategies to respond to questions and concerns.

680D399415DE4EC5BA786E576F97ED11.description: Demonstrate the principles of body mechanics for positioning, transferring and transporting of patients, and perform them without injury to the patient or self.

658BAE250CFE45098689E9D65B23031D.description: Assess and report patient's health status in order to monitor and document patient progress.

5093844743DA41769AA9C04DB13142D1.description: Communicate key diagnostic information to healthcare workers and patients in an accurate and timely manner.

77B448D1CF3848CD9F13F01EE4324393.description: Evaluate accepted ethical practices with respect to cultural, social, and ethnic differences within the healthcare workplace.

F552E81DBA33405C85DB11B3398B3C63.description: Analyze the legal and ethical responsibilities, limitations and implications of actions within the healthcare workplace.

18E39666FCDE410D8FD9AF9C0C761298.description: Evaluate the roles and responsibilities of individual members as part of the healthcare team and explain their role in promoting the delivery of quality health care.

DF6DB7F5D51F477186AD4DC5E3334720.description: Identify existing and potential hazards to clients, coworkers, visitors, and self in the healthcare workplace.

AA56356B7C16498D93C4F82E7BB02F30.description: Explain the healthcare worker's role within their department, their organization, and the overall healthcare system.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Mathematics

6D3E0BE0D4D24CFD8DC57313E7F4659A.description: Compare and contrast dependent and independent events.

EE98BF2F8D54459C8C15283768AA888E.description: Determine how samples are chosen (random, limited, biased) to draw and support conclusions about generalizing a sample to a population.

CCF83F580D8B4C7F886C6340378C995D.description: Calculate experimental probabilities and represent them as percents, fractions and decimals between 0 and 1 inclusive. Use experimental probabilities to make predictions when actual probabilities are unknown.

694817B26053417BB2A5235410BA7F0D.description: Calculate experimental probabilities and reason about probabilities to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

0922A3A095F34FC8BAF5DCA0C19882E9.description: Collect, display and interpret data using scatterplots. Use the shape of the scatterplot to informally estimate a line of best fit, make statements about average rate of change, and make predictions about values not in the original data set. Use appropriate titles, labels and units.

3AF49B5AD0324CB499ACBA4ECFF738AD.description: Explain how outliers affect measures of central tendency.

1F0EBAE464B649BAB15041B8D49A99FE.description: Describe the impact that inserting or deleting a data point has on the mean and the median of a data set. Know how to create data displays using a spreadsheet and use a calculator to examine this impact.

C70F664D5D134A7DA06DE65703EFEAD3.description: Display and interpret data in a variety of ways, including using scatterplots and approximate lines of best fit. Use line of best fit and average rate of change to make predictions and draw conclusions about data.

485B7BB8642048D683B39A277981C1D2.description: Develop and use the formulas V = πr²h and V = Bh to determine the volume of right cylinders, in terms of π and using approximations for π. document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for English Language Arts

C85023CF0DF34715A18EB0B4022483E2.description: Students will write independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for research, reflection, and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two), vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task, and draw and justify appropriate conclusions.

84E13365F3784D98922F258669FB736D.description: Writing: Students will write independently for extended periods of time. Students will vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task.

8CB4C192D25843309754BD313BB95584.description: Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes and read independently for extended periods of time.

3C60CA6E297E4AFC9C496B963137FE71.description: Reading: Students will read independently for a variety of purposes and for extended periods of time. Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes.

1A7D6CA81ECE4CDFB39F775888AE51E2.description: Independent Reading and Writing - Students will read and write for a variety of purposes including, but not limited to, academic and personal.

F21B7931617E472C85D5BB77E31AF313.description: Students will create visual and/or multimedia presentations using a variety of media forms to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence for diverse audiences.

CBA24248E7414AB3AC212900B31634B5.description: Students will critique the sources of multimodal content.

243E553F0A4F448FB97F8E0956A56246.description: Writing: Students will create multimodal texts to communicate knowledge and develop arguments.

404D575F365C4184B436ED91BA85B128.description: Students will analyze the impact of selected media and formats on meaning.

3F3AD762B0B34FC4994646E40D914BEE.description: Students will analyze techniques used to achieve the intended rhetorical purposes in written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts to generate and answer interpretive and applied questions to create new understandings.

0BBC5B6E8CC34CF6AD3419E113C5E1D1.description: Reading: Students will evaluate written, oral, visual, and digital texts in order to draw conclusions and analyze arguments.

F2971F5BB196486CA86E7E3C2DFC5B2F.description: Multimodal Literacies - Students will acquire, refine, and share knowledge through a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts.

93BACCF919134BBC98DE170B784F8ABD.description: Students will synthesize and present information in a report.

66C3CDCDF11F47058D4ADC4AB790890F.description: Students will integrate into their own writing quotes, paraphrases, and summaries of findings following an appropriate citation style (e.g., MLA, APA, etc.) and avoiding plagiarism.

277986A8EA8D477EA759A25201DC2B05.description: Students will refine and formulate a viable research question, integrate findings from sources, and clearly use a well-developed thesis statement.

CB15632CC11849379CB12002A36A45F4.description: Students will write research papers and/or texts independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for research, reflection, and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two).

2DC0E92EDBBA419C85247F05A305C2E2.description: Writing: Students will summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create reports, projects, papers, texts, and presentations for multiple purposes.

603C574EA2174C119E376628070E71CA.description: Students will evaluate the relevance, reliability, and validity of the information gathered.

598A54113D06400F8E0342D4FE2A0A43.description: Students will synthesize the most relevant information from a variety of primary and secondary sources (e.g., print and digital), following ethical and legal citation guidelines.

26B1A92793224AABBC1632DF7BAF2AF7.description: Students will use their own viable research questions and well-developed thesis statements to find information about a specific topic.

5235B087A4194D9EBC86549D72A6B961.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize resources to acquire and refine knowledge.

13D7D8D8EA32414589DC60C1CDBBD433.description: Research - Students will engage in inquiry to acquire, refine, and share knowledge.

93EFAD3031844D8BB600092D20DD6AC2.description: Students will practice their use of Standard American English, grammar, mechanics, and usage through writing, presentations, and/or other modes of communication to convey specific meanings and interests.

B211BF8C533F4F58AF5AD100557C1FEE.description: Students will compose simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences and questions, to signal differing relationships among ideas.

A76AEC3752504B009D8ED6AA7DECB77F.description: Students will write using correct mechanics.

F371EC68D68E41FDA7CAC74626E80BBC.description:
Writing: Students will demonstrate command of Standard English grammar, mechanics, and usage through writing and other modes of communication. These standards begin in Kindergarten. K.5.W.1 Students will capitalize, with guidance and support:
  • their first name
  • the pronoun "I."

7A8DB7E4D93D4BAB9444833CD93FD98A.description: Students will examine the function of parallel structures, various types of phrases, clauses, and active and passive voice to convey specific meanings and/or reflect specific rhetorical styles.

E14BF762104B49B59A2AD44661B8B59D.description: Reading: Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to analyze and evaluate a variety of texts.

4F39FEB439324CBC8774EDE9A9CE6487.description: Language - Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to reading and writing.

C7DEFCE96A834304A14185DEA55428BF.description: Students will select appropriate language to create a specific effect according to purpose in writing.

84147525D5EF4F0F92E6F116ECED2328.description: Students will use domain-appropriate vocabulary to communicate complex ideas in writing clearly.

E06085FBE87540F187CDFF724F9EE36F.description: Writing: Students will apply knowledge of vocabularies to communicate by using descriptive, academic, and domain-appropriate abstract and concrete words in their writing.

5ECCFCAE9D804AF194D638DD8C37F3D6.description: Students will use a dictionary, glossary, or a thesaurus (print and/or electronic) to determine or clarify the meanings, syllabication, pronunciation, synonyms, parts of speech, and etymology of words or phrases.

00DAC4B1D70F40E59F93D7C7C4FF8058.description: Students will analyze the relationships among words with multiple meanings and recognize the connotation and denotation of words.

D51FB9A643994CA09EB46DF0A1486F85.description: Students will use context clues to determine or clarify the meaning of words or distinguish among multiple-meaning words.

DE5EED08346147E8A594B2B73D31EC75.description: Students will use word parts (e.g., affixes, Greek and Latin roots, stems) to define and determine the meaning of increasingly complex words.

76BCCAE82012471A88774AA53BDF685C.description: Students will increase knowledge of academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabulary to infer meaning of grade-level text.

572C4ECD38D9441BB4598A224FBD2DEA.description: Reading: Students will expand academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabularies through reading, word study, and class discussion.

6C0F19E79F2D41F58102F8B959FA1777.description: Vocabulary - Students will expand their working vocabularies to effectively communicate and understand texts.

BDCEA4A3F7B7480697330667A84D2D7F.description: Students will blend multiple modes of writing to produce effective argumentative essays.

98830F4AA8C642649B4767AFE5A980BC.description: Students will use words, phrases, and clauses to connect claims, counterclaims, evidence, and commentary to create a cohesive argument and include a conclusion that follows logically from the information presented and supports the argument.

3D1AAFE7221244C4A3C013867859C1D8.description: Argument: Students will introduce precise claims and distinguish them from counterclaims and provide sufficient evidences to develop balanced arguments, using credible sources.

F4FA062780DA4AC68A7DA129D0F56CC4.description: Students will elaborate on ideas by using logical reasoning and illustrative examples to connect evidences to claim(s).

E99477402B784275BFEAF55F1117A609.description: Informative: Students will compose essays and reports to objectively introduce and develop topics, incorporating evidence (e.g., specific facts, examples, details, data) and maintaining an organized structure and a formal style.

5A574B85AE2D4D91ADB05785AE0C5160.description: Narrative: Students will write narratives embedded in other modes as appropriate.

D47CF8D20FE64F1A9BAD010BE11DF6BA.description: Writing: Students will write for varied purposes and audiences in all modes, using fully developed ideas, strong organization, well-chosen words, fluent sentences, and appropriate voice.

EDBE1305A2AC4E6BA96D355C6016EBF5.description: Students will make connections (e.g., thematic links, literary analysis) between and across multiple texts and provide textual evidence to support their inferences.

A68B00A22AF0495DA62408A3FB8724BD.description: Students will comparatively analyze the structures of texts (e.g., compare/contrast, problem/solution, cause/effect, claims/counterclaims/evidence) and content by inferring connections among multiple texts and providing textual evidence to support their inferences.

50972A2B1B874D0D9FE7C38F1F55ADF2.description: Students will distinguish among different kinds of evidence (e.g., logical, empirical, anecdotal) used to support conclusions and arguments in texts.

C29BB54B1C054DA3B008C0E8E7AC6A36.description:
Students will evaluate literary devices to support interpretations of texts, including comparisons across texts:
  • figurative language
  • imagery
  • tone
  • symbolism
  • irony

491F279F039E414DA50CB26E7FCA0D58.description:
Students will analyze how authors use key literary elements to contribute to meaning and interpret how themes are connected across texts:
  • character development
  • theme
  • conflict (i.e., internal and external)
  • archetypes

66CB02DB17D644538814D11DA9AE7526.description: Students will evaluate points of view and perspectives in more than one grade-level literary and/or informational text and explain how multiple points of view contribute to the meaning of a work.

19D2387B4E9841E2AA11CE825017BA53.description: Students will evaluate the extent to which historical, cultural, and/or global perspectives affect authors' stylistic and organizational choices in grade-level literary and informational genres.

ABB4A52A675F4D52A21FD8856623C191.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts of all literary and informational genres from a variety of historical, cultural, ethnic, and global perspectives.

C9E9C613B1E24FB992D741FF3BA361BA.description: Critical Reading and Writing - Students will apply critical thinking skills to reading and writing.

DE396B1BE6394EE4947158D7DFA7EFF3.description: Students will use resources to find correct spellings of words (e.g., word wall, vocabulary notebook, print and electronic dictionaries, and spell-check).

D419ADAA6254438CBA0F237DAD62A19C.description: Students will edit and revise multiple drafts for organization, enhanced transitions and coherence, sentence variety, and consistency in tone and point of view to establish meaningful texts.

9782B3063D83401B969A7328A3B97F75.description: Students will develop drafts by choosing an organizational structure (e.g., description, compare/contrast, sequential, problem/solution, cause/effect, etc.) and building on ideas in multi-paragraph essays.

ED445B3B677A4F37BD672BC49225FF6C.description: Students will plan (e.g., outline) and prewrite a first draft as necessary.

194D37065E5E4868B3D3248B91651495.description: Students will apply components of a recursive writing process for multiple purposes to create a focused, organized, and coherent piece of writing.

38FD3C826DD44F1A9E299EBDB9A07CA5.description: Writing: Students will develop and strengthen writing by engaging in a recursive process that includes prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, and publishing.

5C08E054BFC0400FA792A90A535EDC14.description: Students will analyze details in literary and nonfiction/informational texts to connect how genre supports the author's purpose.

F90F0F32D2334C8CA021465549C385FB.description: Students will summarize, paraphrase, and synthesize ideas, while maintaining meaning and a logical sequence of events, within and between texts.

4A0C872702F04438A494DD6DDF23C0DD.description: Reading: Students will read and comprehend increasingly complex literary and informational texts.

25FB370EEA7A426AB9EAC4414233926B.description: Reading and Writing Process - Students will use a variety of recursive reading and writing processes.

9BC793D694C041C596AF424B25C153AA.description: Students will work effectively and respectfully within diverse groups, show willingness to make necessary compromises to accomplish a goal, share responsibility for collaborative work, and value individual contributions made by each group member.

6CB5859B8B414F5FA3F3AB1AEDD425EA.description: Students will give formal and informal presentations in a group or individually, providing textual and visual evidence to support a main idea.

02FCD28B2A1B4DC1AB9F40B937035CB6.description: Writing: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening to create individual and group projects and presentations.

F3095ADBC6524D8FA0B238D38F176A35.description: Students will engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts, expressing their own ideas clearly while building on the ideas of others in pairs, diverse groups, and whole class settings.

E44505BE67834EC9B18B850D1870FDE0.description: Students will actively listen and evaluate, analyze, and synthesize a speaker's messages (both verbal and nonverbal) and ask questions to clarify the speaker's purpose and perspective.

4265CAFBA48C4D0EA2CCA174103E1DE3.description: Students will actively listen and speak clearly using appropriate discussion rules with control of verbal and nonverbal cues.

BB9DE28AEAE44F95ACF8438B53E3C438.description: Reading: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening.

788AC63DE9F843FFBB9BEBE40617D980.description: Speaking and Listening - Students will speak and listen effectively in a variety of situations including, but not limited to, responses to reading and writing.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for English Language Arts

0A8CFEDBD7874CD2B5B41881CACB9C61.description: Students will write independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for research, reflection, and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two), vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task, and be able to apply new understandings in an original way.

84B3AC466E004C368ACAB97331194EB2.description: Writing: Students will write independently for extended periods of time. Students will vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task.

59C5C7A55AF746C0AC436A46857C574B.description: Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes and read independently for extended periods of time.

BE95B4A5D2B9457D906FCB0BF6680182.description: Reading: Students will read independently for a variety of purposes and for extended periods of time. Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes.

40A1E4F5786C4887B042BABB2ACFEA0A.description: Independent Reading and Writing - Students will read and write for a variety of purposes including, but not limited to, academic and personal.

E115234F283844A48E317B5F88B7BFCF.description: Students will construct engaging visual and/or multimedia presentations using a variety of media forms to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence for diverse audiences.

158E7623D4104A13AA06AB64E6D7FF9C.description: Students will design and develop multimodal content for a variety of purposes.

53F7D57072B34271A59C8A59B18FF4FC.description: Writing: Students will create multimodal texts to communicate knowledge and develop arguments.

D8DD0CD88A4641F096C39E70CF9F708D.description: Students will analyze the impact of selected media and formats on meaning.

BA220CFBD7864721B0F3730D067A34D8.description: Students will analyze and evaluate the various techniques used to construct arguments in written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts, to generate and answer applied questions, and to create new understandings.

D744577BE2C041659FD82A8103E998C3.description: Reading: Students will evaluate written, oral, visual, and digital texts in order to draw conclusions and analyze arguments.

DE4CA9A8087C42DB9B1A44099F093647.description: Multimodal Literacies - Students will acquire, refine, and share knowledge through a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts.

4293544092384F2794DF1606F4EDF22E.description: Students will synthesize and present information in a report.

DC567F1629204B49A2658574E151D13C.description: Students will integrate into their own writing quotes, paraphrases, and summaries of findings following an appropriate citation style (e.g., MLA, APA, etc.) and avoiding plagiarism.

A9932816BA0C4F49BCE2184B426D6108.description: Students will integrate findings from sources using a well-developed thesis statement.

C3D5249EC2BE473D8C0797E5BF06526D.description: Students will write research papers and/or texts independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for research, reflection, and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two).

D00301411B724F8A84855F42272C4ECD.description: Writing: Students will summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create reports, projects, papers, texts, and presentations for multiple purposes.

487F861567E64B998F9286C6B36CCF8E.description: Students will evaluate the relevance, reliability, and validity of the information gathered.

88EBC786E9504221A1C4BB03EEAB5041.description: Students will synthesize the most relevant information from a variety of primary and secondary sources (e.g., print and digital), following ethical and legal citation guidelines.

2E72438A39D94B65ABB8F56F1B89B346.description: Students will use their own viable research questions and well-developed thesis statements to find information about a specific topic.

FD6F9BCC5393473BAB142A89114DA7A9.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize resources to acquire and refine knowledge.

8D69776C0D0F4CDE9C8601B9DBBE6B44.description: Reading and Writing Process - Students will use a variety of recursive reading and writing processes.

43A08B7E5AB94B5D88EFDAEB0F3B291A.description: Students will engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts, expressing their own ideas by contributing to, building on, and questioning the ideas of others in pairs, diverse groups, and whole class settings.
