FD6D85C5595A4F8DAA09E6ACEB804091.description: Students will begin to develop an awareness of context clues through read-alouds and other text experiences.

CB9D326059FA458D87E6C87ECD0391E0.description: Students will acquire new academic, content-specific, grade-level vocabulary and relate new words to prior knowledge with guidance and support.

2A0BF236B2A64193BD65E9D6F9CB3CA7.description: Reading: Students will expand academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabularies through reading, word study, and class discussion.

7F442D40A4EC455A9CCAC0CBBE9B4E75.description: Vocabulary - Students will expand their working vocabularies to effectively communicate and understand texts.

5E3D686F4AAE4049AD229518C09B2D1A.description: Students will use drawing, labeling, and dictating to express thoughts and ideas with guidance and support.

2CBB8CF59DFD4E65BABA843C60F029D8.description: Writing: Students will write for varied purposes and audiences in all modes, using fully developed ideas, strong organization, well-chosen words, fluent sentences, and appropriate voice.

89511AFA699448DBAD824DCBB576A009.description: Students will ask and answer basic questions (e.g., who, what, where, and when) about texts during shared reading or other text experiences with guidance and support.

9285D3D818934890A24326D81793EEAF.description: Students will tell what is happening in a picture or illustration with guidance and support.

27D745C08C964917A5CC6D40B26E7086.description: Students will describe characters in a story with guidance and support.

F843EDAA400649438A7E2E06118AA4AC.description: Students will describe the role of an author and illustrator, telling how they contribute to a story, with guidance and support.

CD234763925448AF86D61718E0B06568.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts of all literary and informational genres from a variety of historical, cultural, ethnic, and global perspectives.

214907EC7DD84D1E8E828AE1DB7C3645.description: Critical Reading and Writing - Students will apply critical thinking skills to reading and writing.

5F278E69AE1A4878991BFF42919627F0.description: Students will begin to express themselves through drawing, dictating, and emergent writing.

0686433C32E24DCE91D16646781E62B7.description: Writing: Students will develop and strengthen writing by engaging in a recursive process that includes prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, and publishing.

AF075D3921354CF78DA7496A4A58EBE2.description: Students will begin to retell or reenact major events from a read-aloud with guidance and support to recognize the main idea.

FBFBE5D7FA92490CBCFF344202E055FA.description: Reading: Students will read and comprehend increasingly complex literary and informational texts.

C41FDC8466514E338638AEEB0D0E17AE.description: Reading and Writing Process - Students will use a variety of recursive reading and writing processes.

877EEE37087E47C89B684609D53DBA1C.description: Students will read first name in print.

01D9B64D190D4EE5862B04A26459DA85.description: Fluency: Students will recognize high-frequency words and read grade-level text smoothly and accurately, with expression that connotes comprehension.

7E819F0AC71741A1B97E8B38038773C0.description: Students will produce some sounds represented by letters with guidance and support.

02E1862AB5F34C08B8F5D28F11D998DE.description: Students will name the majority of the letters in their first name and many uppercase and lowercase letters with guidance and support.

C19763798246431A921C16BA748AFCA6.description: Phonics and Word Study: Students will decode and read words in context and isolation by applying phonics and word analysis skills.

F0A434D2AEA3432A9DE32F089E7A7531.description: Students will recognize ending punctuation marks in print during shared reading or other text experiences with guidance and support.

CA6D5EED39D94C099EE2149F894A4AFD.description: Students will begin to understand that print moves from top to bottom, left to right, and front to back.

BB5AB41DA2904A778FEB73354EDCF02E.description: Students will recognize that written words are made up of letters and are separated by spaces with guidance and support.

2A326DFCBBD84EEEBB1439364DD82714.description: Students will begin to demonstrate correct book orientation and identify the front and back covers of a book.

4231EC2626B74851AF6A475FCA2FDA70.description: Students will understand that print carries a message by recognizing labels, signs, and other print in the environment with guidance and support.

49DD34089E1A47059746D63ABBCEBDAE.description: Students will write the majority of the letters in their first name and some uppercase and lowercase letters with guidance and support.

E9DBE4DCAD364655889249319FE644F7.description: Print Concepts: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the organization and basic features of print, including book handling skills and the understanding that printed materials provide information and tell stories.

C6B665C7D3424A12B67F24BBC461FA52.description: Students will combine onsets and rimes to form familiar one syllable spoken words with pictorial support (e.g., /c/ + at = cat)

E067A1B8992944A787159CF5A21CF0E2.description: Students will begin to recognize initial sounds in a set of spoken words (i.e., alliteration).

EA253E8CD77A40F5B9E09118A27B3F8A.description: Students will begin to isolate initial and final sounds in spoken words.

EE20E35B286C452891D5A559495842C7.description: Students will begin to recognize syllables in spoken words (e.g., sunshine = sun + shine).

8326C73DD1B84E48B38627E9E0533AC0.description: Students will recognize spoken words that rhyme.

B4350F2382844F7A8B553FF55C795BBB.description: Students will distinguish spoken words in a sentence with guidance and support.

CC4827A2CBEB4107B2C6E74E056D66CE.description: Phonological Awareness: Phonological awareness is the ability to recognize, think about, and manipulate sounds in spoken language without using text.

ABFEF7EA816B4C32B7D6E553CC75A8C7.description: Reading Foundations - Students will develop foundational skills for future reading success by working with sounds, letters, and text.

2EEC6586E05F407F95CBE24275E7411C.description: Students will work respectfully with others with guidance and support.

6E0040EF74BC49569B1D18480720DFB9.description: Students will begin to orally describe personal interests or tell stories to classmates with guidance and support.

7491355647D745A59534A9EE28086960.description: Writing: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening to create individual and group projects and presentations.

86567E656BB24178B37EA038187DB7A5.description: Students will follow simple oral directions.

CC2FD99D077441D3BF5E7762FE7B474E.description: Students will begin to engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts with peers and adults in small and large groups with guidance and support.

36E65DF9326447DFA24E8D9BF6F25098.description: Students will begin to ask and answer questions about information presented orally or through text or other media with guidance and support.

DC7FBB65A8044DE69FD16F46C512E67E.description: Students will actively listen and speak using agreed-upon rules with guidance and support.

160DB29F4056405BA0A45812BA731593.description: Reading: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening.

6E7C4F4AF0074A2BB337479A45F786EB.description: Speaking and Listening - Students will speak and listen effectively in a variety of situations including, but not limited to, responses to reading and writing.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for English Language Arts

CF385E9786CB49689144861CEC446F27.description: Students will write independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for research, reflection, and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two), vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task, and discover different perspectives.

F8B0738A6E4D4E93A05A5E97734DEEC9.description: Writing: Students will write independently for extended periods of time. Students will vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task.

BD81DC9009EA486B8E593F503214666A.description: Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes and read independently for extended periods of time.

79EEF0021AA74ACE85D9621354C931B6.description: Reading: Students will read independently for a variety of purposes and for extended periods of time. Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes.

DF1ED74BC4DE49418DF881C0104DF9D7.description: Independent Reading and Writing - Students will read and write for a variety of purposes including, but not limited to, academic and personal.

E026F80F0C6E4D7D890B5640AC657671.description: Students will utilize multimedia to clarify information and strengthen claims or evidence.

9087C0504F4944DCBD034E46D185A9A2.description: Students will select, organize, or create multimodal content to complement and extend meaning for a selected topic.

8E6817531EF44215BFD8BE286D982B47.description: Writing: Students will create multimodal texts to communicate knowledge and develop arguments.

C108C465545740309A44174447286481.description: Students will analyze the impact of selected media and formats on meaning.

D68321EDA01B4A7DA4EE7CAB0FD9F664.description: Students will compare and contrast the effectiveness of techniques used in a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts to generate and answer literal, interpretive, and applied questions to create new understandings.

353C7EF349E74242AEC41334015BF61A.description: Reading: Students will evaluate written, oral, visual, and digital texts in order to draw conclusions and analyze arguments.

71171CE4D29B47428BF8533B26AF4F95.description: Multimodal Literacies - Students will acquire, refine, and share knowledge through a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts.

B58AC6C64C7F4A1199600A12E61AAA23.description: Students will summarize and present information in a report.

905B2086272E4CF2998C02B989DA1663.description: Students will quote, paraphrase, and summarize findings following an appropriate citation style (e.g., MLA, APA, etc.) and avoiding plagiarism.

A00402A794F6488E96941A30B887DCB8.description: Students will refine and formulate a viable research question and report findings clearly and concisely, using a thesis statement.

2804E09080DB4CC2B289456D4B8387FB.description: Students will write research papers and/or texts independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for research, reflection, and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two).

CCC997B5B8C24E4D9B64B69BAF825096.description: Writing: Students will summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create reports, projects, papers, texts, and presentations for multiple purposes.

325B34EFFA694FE3AA2E95DA860D4E98.description: Students will determine the relevance, reliability, and validity of the information gathered.

12E979FEC5AE4769A92186C545EC8049.description: Students will follow ethical and legal guidelines for finding and recording information from a variety of primary and secondary sources (e.g., print and digital).

80EF50D1050F4467A513515DA42F21B0.description: Students will use their own viable research questions and thesis statements to find information about a specific topic.

7C9C0277E268473A850BB47E834BBA42.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize resources to acquire and refine knowledge.

DC1CEFBCF7274D16A074B405BF5314E3.description: Research - Students will engage in inquiry to acquire, refine, and share knowledge.

9F4E73D3738F496A922AA19153DD280C.description: Students will use prepositional phrases and clauses (e.g., dependent and independent) in writing.

ACA96479673049109523E7A2D5FABAA1.description: Students will compose simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences and questions to signal differing relationships among ideas.

821A10418354403EADA93802CEAF5A53.description: Students will write using correct mechanics with a focus on commas, apostrophes, quotation marks, colons, and semi-colons.

016D6BB87E544DEC83386FCABBB1F678.description:
Writing: Students will demonstrate command of Standard English grammar, mechanics, and usage through writing and other modes of communication. These standards begin in Kindergarten. K.5.W.1 Students will capitalize, with guidance and support:
  • their first name
  • the pronoun "I."

95B4222656774D329B11CEC431B91911.description: Students will recognize and correct misplaced and dangling modifiers.

C16DFE48A81D466D8CD3C194C9746066.description: Students will recognize the subject and verb agreement.

E53DADBB578345EFAF34B12022DBCD91.description: Students will recognize simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal differing relationships among ideas.

1A4DCBFD9CD544F2B97630DC399FC703.description: Students will recognize the correct use of prepositional phrases and dependent clauses.

60CE217FE11449489C0883538CA747E2.description: Reading: Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to analyze and evaluate a variety of texts.

946F7ECC395542EAB790D4691074C81D.description: Language - Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to reading and writing.

56EBC9DD4062404785D0DD42A2B675FB.description: Students will select appropriate language to create a specific effect according to purpose in writing.

54209205DA624D96BD24499FF180CC53.description: Students will use domain-appropriate vocabulary to communicate ideas in writing clearly.

98C1FDB4D603453EB876E2F0CB566752.description: Writing: Students will apply knowledge of vocabularies to communicate by using descriptive, academic, and domain-appropriate abstract and concrete words in their writing.

A9751034261B44A5B8FEE47D6C3160E7.description: Students will use a dictionary, glossary, or a thesaurus (print and/or electronic) to determine or clarify the meanings, syllabication, pronunciation, synonyms, and parts of speech of words.

14B7D2B92A394ED198CABA80E540BB7A.description: Students will infer the relationships among words with multiple meanings and recognize the connotation and denotation of words.

41D95C9119D1457C9843F4A48AD1779D.description: Students will use context clues to determine or clarify the meaning of words or distinguish among multiple-meaning words.

C96CFE60B2A5429AB1C048AB1FE8436D.description: Students will use word parts (e.g., affixes, Greek and Latin roots, stems) to define and determine the meaning of increasingly complex words.

917B62E39EB34DC593240CAC314DBA1E.description: Students will increase knowledge of academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabulary to infer meaning of grade-level text.

169ED1D74C694C348A06F366337778C6.description: Reading: Students will expand academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabularies through reading, word study, and class discussion.

B3CB3EFA94D944E7AD72DB1E8F306B06.description: Vocabulary - Students will expand their working vocabularies to effectively communicate and understand texts.

796A6453E94B4C58B198261A1DCD6879.description: Students will show relationships among the claim, reasons, and evidence.

90C3175809FC4841B21E33549D327C38.description: Argument: Students will introduce a claim and organize reasons and evidence, using credible sources.

0CE3D3E4E6184ABEAADB1073DE83E426.description: Informative: Students will compose essays and reports about topics, incorporating evidence (e.g., specific facts, examples, details) and maintaining an organized structure and a formal style.

0AED10394C0942E1ACCB39393F74BC78.description: Narrative: Students will write narratives incorporating characters, plot, setting, point of view, conflict, dialogue, and sensory details to convey experiences and events.

8AB74B80E1CB4BA58D62B6C6968213F2.description: Writing: Students will write for varied purposes and audiences in all modes, using fully developed ideas, strong organization, well-chosen words, fluent sentences, and appropriate voice.

68B91F285BBC48EE8A983E2332AAEC5F.description: Students will make connections (e.g., thematic links) between and across multiple texts and provide textual evidence to support their inferences.

471C50D8E517446E8291773C122D18F0.description: Students will analyze the structures of texts (e.g., compare/contrast, problem/solution, cause/effect, claims/evidence) and content by making inferences about texts and use textual evidence to draw simple logical conclusions.

DCDEDD44811146F99F592627AFD425D5.description: Students will distinguish factual claims from opinions.

B620550C254E457C84E475C67C940278.description:
Students will evaluate literary devices to support interpretations of literary texts:
  • simile
  • metaphor
  • personification
  • onomatopoeia
  • hyperbole
  • imagery
  • symbolism
  • tone
  • irony (Students will find textual evidence when provided with examples.)

622929A840D74316A5DADE2DED3F089F.description:
Students will analyze how key literary elements contribute to the meaning of the literary work:
  • setting
  • plot
  • characters (i.e., protagonist, antagonist)
  • characterization
  • theme
  • conflict (i.e., internal and external)

681976CF18BD4C549AB5B92D2C18DF3A.description: Students will evaluate how the point of view and perspective affect grade-level literary and/or informational text.

50A9C27AAFB542A9B53CC64D14732790.description: Students will compare and contrast stated or implied purposes of authors writing on the same topic in grade-level literary and/or informational texts.

244CAF8789AE4848A2AEEAC85024B0CF.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts of all literary and informational genres from a variety of historical, cultural, ethnic, and global perspectives.

A56F407114984EB1B696AA5251FA88DF.description: Critical Reading and Writing - Students will apply critical thinking skills to reading and writing.

3D63FEC99CEB4D34A0F0D140BFDE993A.description: Students will use resources to find correct spellings of words (e.g., word wall, vocabulary notebook, print and electronic dictionaries, and spell-check).

EB81A87C1CCC4ECA97D3E095E5718DFF.description: Students will edit and revise multiple drafts for organization, transitions to improve coherence and meaning, using a consistent point of view.

C5225ECFA2AD45C98CE0926AFA76D6AF.description: Students will develop drafts by choosing an organizational structure (e.g., description, compare/contrast, sequential, problem/solution, cause/effect, etc.) and building on ideas in multi-paragraph essays.

36B45345EFB0420CB3409C76267021AF.description: Students will plan (e.g., outline) and prewrite a first draft as necessary.

1D5E6244AE6F4BC1B78427F5CCA7529D.description: Students will apply components of a recursive writing process for multiple purposes to create a focused, organized, and coherent piece of writing.

DE55F343F74D45D99B076F8E8B6D8202.description: Writing: Students will develop and strengthen writing by engaging in a recursive process that includes prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, and publishing.

CC91533615F64F209D998972A4995448.description: Students will paraphrase main ideas with supporting details in a text.

0F65F141B4BC4C7EA859FE3916054A6A.description: Students will analyze details in literary and nonfiction/informational texts to distinguish genres.

4693CE9BB6B745B1BE436713231690ED.description: Students will create an objective summary, including main idea and supporting details, while maintaining meaning and a logical sequence of events.

108A184BE78B4738A884AB7F967B2189.description: Reading: Students will read and comprehend increasingly complex literary and informational texts.

FD7F8AA6582D47269E9E3E6DBB51A439.description: Reading and Writing Process - Students will use a variety of recursive reading and writing processes.

9D37A0B16B1B4216B789C0803291FF9C.description: Students will work effectively and respectfully within diverse groups, show willingness to make necessary compromises to accomplish a goal, share responsibility for collaborative work, and value individual contributions made by each group member.

BDCA9488DC1842A7A63AB9F2456C99A9.description: Students will give formal and informal presentations in a group or individually, providing evidence to support a main idea.

DA3D7B6562684F8BBAC524257DD4AB15.description: Writing: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening to create individual and group projects and presentations.

041D493E0C534E6E8DE0EE0BC5ECE48D.description: Students will engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts, expressing their own ideas clearly while building on the ideas of others in pairs, diverse groups, and whole class settings.

EBBAC45A0865449F8B891529FBDE6E2B.description: Students will actively listen and interpret a speaker's messages (both verbal and nonverbal) and ask questions to clarify the speaker's purpose and perspective.

D515109149E44EABB0B508EB8E4558CD.description: Students will actively listen and speak clearly using appropriate discussion rules with awareness and control of verbal and nonverbal cues.

07D23B7CA6DF4ED4B8D61C866244FBCB.description: Reading: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening.

5D0BA842519847FD9513BCA03F4977D5.description: Speaking and Listening - Students will speak and listen effectively in a variety of situations including, but not limited to, responses to reading and writing.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Physical Education

565FF6B57182497EA3F6158CE4CB12F3.description: Evaluates the opportunity for social interaction and social support in a self-selected physical activity or dance.

CFA3242FDF104F91BE6BD3B9DE52F2EB.description: Identifies the opportunity for social support in a self-selected physical activity or dance.

0E09FF48F76E47338B561401BC2A2806.description: Identifies the uniqueness of creative dance as a means of self-expression.

EA6F3754EFB4404795397366230CD704.description: Selects and participates in physical activities or dance that meets the need for self-expression and enjoyment.

3A7CE79CD642444BA2E112EAD132FB13.description: Chooses an appropriate level of challenge to experience success and desire to participate in a self-selected physical activity.

079CBEB101FE4C029816E798D785DFCD.description: Chooses an appropriate level of challenge in a self-selected activity.

4C94678955A9473F8AB5DA68F0976DE1.description: Analyzes the health benefits of more than one self-selected physical activity.

E7B7B9EA3FC645469F43BD5E4B4BD93A.description: Analyzes the health benefits of a self-selected physical activity.

7ACCCE3928254015917847747AE938DD.description: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction.

C94AF0381EC445EC81B0273CA0283ACC.description: Applies best practices for participating safely in physical activity, exercise, and dance (e.g., injury prevention, aquatics, proper alignment, hydration, use of equipment, implementation of rules, sun protection).

9C405611742D4C12867CA73CC868BCE2.description: Understands best practices for participating safely in physical activity, exercise, and dance (e.g., injury prevention, aquatics, proper alignment, hydration, use of equipment, implementation or rules, sun protection).

24530C7D79F142F48FC4B97196B221F4.description: Accepts others' ideas cultural diversity and body types by engaging in cooperative and collaborative movement projects.

5A842C7389714BDC9470AEE2CBF857B5.description: Solves problems and thinks critically in physical activity and/or dance settings, both as an individual and in groups.

F5B056A2FAC847B18207F6A7383EF8A9.description: Assumes a leadership role (e.g., task or group leader, referee, coach) in a physical activity setting.

3E8D0A402B0848129843A573F038CF5E.description: Uses communication skills and strategies that promote team or group dynamics.

45BFAB2025ED426C871AE4D5A5CF0411.description: Examines moral and ethical conduct in specific competitive situations (e.g., intentional fouls, performance-enhancing substances, gambling, current events in sport).

85E415C320F54B658475B4D250AFB857.description: Exhibits proper etiquette, respect for others and teamwork while engaging in physical activity and/or social dance.

A4D27BD1FE88466DAA8A59DFA59987C7.description: Accepts differences between personal characteristics and the idealized body images and elite performance levels portrayed in various media.

60FF3459AD654BDBAB81369908D51F14.description: Employs effective self-management skills to analyze barriers and modify physical activity patterns appropriately as needed.

8327BD55C1074452A3AE58E66B2A3620.description: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others.

C019191D3A304A36A0A5D8AD370FC943.description: Applies stress-management strategies (e.g., mental imagery, relaxation techniques, deep breathing, aerobic exercises, meditation) to reduce stress.

B553A6E8974B496FA40AEAC44375ED3B.description: Identifies stress-management strategies (e.g., mental imagery, relaxation techniques, deep breathing, aerobic exercises, meditation) to reduce stress.

DB9AE4656D2C45D885CF037FF002717E.description: Creates a snack plan for before, during and after exercise that addresses nutrition needs for each phase.

0A2FCDFBEF5D4B519C66501C9EF431A7.description: Designs and implements a nutrition plan to maintain and appropriate energy balance for a healthy, active lifestyle.

E6B4DF9BCEE14C668DA450D292CA1494.description: Analyzes the components of skill-related fitness in relation to life and career goals and designs an appropriate fitness program for those goals.

2FA3669776054D9A8EC7A2A386C39C63.description: Designs a fitness program, including all components of health-related fitness, for a college student and an employee in the learner's chosen field of work.

7BEE2EA0DA4A4BD5A1AA516B41AF09DC.description: Develops and maintains a fitness portfolio (e.g., assessment scores, goals for improvement, plan of activities for improvement, log of activities being done to reach goals, timeline for improvement).

06968B20B4EA457183622DA6525941FD.description: Creates and implements a behavior-modification plan that enhances a healthy, active lifestyle in college or career settings.

8B09C5462FC943A9B0B9FA2EE051F196.description: Adjusts pacing to keep heart rate in target zone, using available technology to self-monitor aerobic intensity.

1025011911A04CCB999596531C00AE07.description: Calculates target heart rate and applies that information to personal fitness plan.

651582258849404787D238D5C7BBA1A9.description: Identifies the structure of skeletal muscle and fiber types as they relate to muscle development.

9DB02DC3869B476A95D9A8E1CDC61C1E.description: Identifies types of strength exercises (isometric, concentric, eccentric) and stretching exercises (static, proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF), dynamic) for personal fitness development (e.g., strength, endurance, range of motion).

64671C35E5524B42A8061CBB5A4D33AD.description: Identifies the different energy systems used in a selected physical activity (e.g., adenosine triphosphate and phosphocreatine, anaerobic glycolysis, aerobic).

AF0CC5938EBB464CA4143112EF39F077.description: Relates physiological response to individual levels of fitness and nutritional balance.

DB1E732087A4428AB9003A4E75917EE2.description: Designs and implements strength and conditioning program that develops balance in opposing muscle groups and supports a healthy, active lifestyle.

A2BE17FCE50F4E96B469C2433DBC0914.description: Demonstrates appropriate technique in resistance-training machines and free weights.

1883AA9EBC3F4DBA8DEE8EA4EA0568BC.description: Creates a plan, trains for and participates in a community event with a focus on physical activity (e.g., 5K, triathlon, tournament, dance performance, cycling event).

8088F7AA6C844CC9900369D2D42F7CA4.description: Participates several times a week in a self-selected lifetime activity, dance or fitness activity outside of the school day.

30C3B70A8E1847B78EAB6225EC51F6EF.description: Analyzes the impact of life choices, economics, motivation, and accessibility on exercise adherence and participation in physical activity in college or career settings.

2B00706320ED490694B53C93AF9CD4D1.description: Evaluates risks and safety factors that might affect physical activity preferences throughout the life cycle.

A919E4159D604AFCACFE1BF661E4D74E.description: Evaluates - according to their benefits, social support network, and participation requirements - activities that can be pursued in and outside the local environment.

C73746D8A0224A8C840345DAB9E89D19.description: Evaluates - according to their benefits, social support network, and participation requirements - activities that can be pursued in the local environment.

D9F3B043D0DB4D87918C9E96B1DFE662.description: Applies rates of perceived exertion and pacing.

9176DFDC6B904FBBB139BBC5133DF0E4.description: Identifies issues associated with exercising in heat, humidity, and cold.

E693553CC03F4E6E81AFFD1C7F77CA6E.description: Analyzes and applies technology and social media as tools for supporting a healthy, active lifestyle.

4D85FEDEE5704364B0571D66697A51F3.description: Evaluates the validity of claims made by commercial products and programs pertaining to fitness and healthy, active lifestyle.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for English Language Arts

89CBCCCCD1DE4409849B342C61995376.description: Students will write independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for research, reflection, and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two) to communicate with different audiences for a variety of purposes.

37CBA4DCF5AF4CD0A42E4460563AC1FD.description: Writing: Students will write independently for extended periods of time. Students will vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task.

9FD09B4BDB4944209B1FEE3FE90D2A57.description: Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes and read independently for extended periods of time.

EF82C05109E8478FBC2E19750919D7A3.description: Reading: Students will read independently for a variety of purposes and for extended periods of time. Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes.

7245C65405E74DD084364D4C7CD7C5D5.description: Independent Reading and Writing - Students will read and write for a variety of purposes including, but not limited to, academic and personal.

C9D4BC658CB0449BAE4163805F9E617C.description: Students will create presentations that integrate visual displays and other multimedia to enrich the presentation.

21EE2BA8991945D688DE60C732B27074.description: Students will create multimodal content that effectively communicates an idea using technology and appropriate media.

47BEA4F86FDB4D3CA63AC0208DCED6B3.description: Writing: Students will create multimodal texts to communicate knowledge and develop arguments.

0251EF90C4B249578A58B95C4F91793B.description: Students will compare and contrast how ideas and topics are depicted in a variety of media and formats.

3A028AC00C3D4EB1A35263C51567721E.description: Students will analyze the characteristics and effectiveness of a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts to generate and answer literal and interpretive questions to create new understandings.

665E1B6C2641482ABB23246C29CA006F.description: Reading: Students will evaluate written, oral, visual, and digital texts in order to draw conclusions and analyze arguments.

D344AEAA71114D09B43849269C747E5D.description: Multimodal Literacies - Students will acquire, refine, and share knowledge through a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts.

489DB4648F824B7F9D63B46A74466890.description: Students will summarize and present information in a report.

D57F41C9529F43D7BACBB8DBC1834A85.description: Students will organize information found during research, following a modified citation style (e.g., author, title, publication date) with guidance and support.

0CE588BDB2AB4A90B96301DFDB466A10.description: Students will formulate a viable research question from findings.

A6AA28B53C904679997845AEADC97690.description: Students will write research papers and/or texts independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for research, reflection, and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two).

C664E93DBAE84AA5B211161500B1F910.description: Writing: Students will summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create reports, projects, papers, texts, and presentations for multiple purposes.

AB638830081B4B10A10DF26DB9401D0A.description: Students will determine the relevance and reliability of the information gathered.

846BE8CA828548B4BB3920EC5F1A2E4E.description: Students will record and organize information from various print and/or digital sources.

A6303F78C45E4C6E8E809234ADD2CA0E.description: Students will use their own viable research questions to find information about a specific topic.

6B00030200894FCF9DD35D53D5687964.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize resources to acquire and refine knowledge.

0672F0729F1D4C3DB909ED52BED5A9AA.description: Research - Students will engage in inquiry to acquire, refine, and share knowledge.

A3A27FF466E64B9EB5784CC572679D97.description: Students will recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.

D7F3FEBED7CC48CFB3B6A9F626E43965.description: Students will form and use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions.

3178B0E6D9D841239FC7FC98DE9E8467.description: Students will form and use the present and past verb tenses.

A72916165F2D40098022696618CA3AF7.description: Students will compose simple, compound, and complex sentences and questions, create sentences with an understood subject, and correct fragments and run-on sentences.

6C2618F81BD3481CA8029F50DD00CCEF.description: Students will write using correct mechanics with a focus on commas, apostrophes, and quotation marks as needed for dialogue and quoted material.

08B7FF0DDE9846A89B3080D7D2DFD214.description:
Writing: Students will demonstrate command of Standard English grammar, mechanics, and usage through writing and other modes of communication. These standards begin in Kindergarten. K.5.W.1 Students will capitalize, with guidance and support:
  • their first name
  • the pronoun "I."

A9AE8B483F8146EAA078D9FE9EA52A66.description: Students will recognize the subject and verb agreement.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Physical Education

6C824EA1477B4FCCA1990A9027CFAEE3.description: Demonstrates respect for self and others in activities and games by following the rules, encouraging others and playing in the spirit of the game or activity.

9D8D6976B9A646368E971B9DFAD52524.description: Identifies how self-expression and physical activity are related.

4CFA4824D8B04A828403C4E6F3F77AAD.description: Describes how moving competently in a physical activity setting creates enjoyment.

17749C171F794AD9BD9E49954CDAA335.description: Recognize individual challenges and copes in a positive way, such as, extending effort, asking for help and/or feedback or modifying the tasks.

0437C398299942188021C017EC011151.description: Identifies components of physical activity that provide opportunities for reducing stress and for social interaction.

ADB0AD6A761B4311B3605E66F9CF4BFC.description: Describes how being physically active leads to a healthy body.

FEFDC075B0264A3A85AEC7E875B0E3C4.description: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction.

FE6DB696418E40BFBEA460FAB251DF68.description: Uses physical activity and fitness equipment appropriately and safely, with the teacher's guidance.

29F58BFD6443426C985F075DA015CA23.description: Identifies the rules and etiquette for physical activities, games, and dance activities.

D3C792A3D05D4BD4944D9A3A40E64B46.description: Cooperates with a small group of classmates during adventure activities, game play, or team-building activities.

0A559F2B36F340D69E26E1F8D86B1249.description: Accepts differences among classmates in physical development, maturation, and varying skill levels by providing encouragement and positive feedback.

E12BA2B62F5044549F86B3C199479692.description: Demonstrating self-responsibility by implementing specific corrective feedback to improve performance.

BAEE27192F6E4296AAA5CFE094143DEC.description: Identifies and uses appropriate strategies to self-reinforce positive fitness behaviors, such as positive self-talk.

935C0AFC798E441A84368546249C3461.description: Exhibits personal responsibility by using appropriate etiquette, demonstrating respect for facilities, and exhibiting safe behaviors.

E02E88CADF3B4808A9F50174565A3EC5.description: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others.

26B78587E24149D6B85B298B1A297B5A.description: Identifies positive and negative results of stress and appropriate ways of dealing with each.

7C90840E20CA4C53B292C7160BA6A2F7.description: Identifies foods within each of the basic food groups and selects appropriate servings and portions for her/his age and physical activity levels.

39B0CD47BCB647FAB81A19797302B04F.description: Maintains a physical activity log for at least two weeks and reflects on activity levels as documented in the log.

2C44BE44473C4F349E14A6D996F0815F.description: Designs and implements a program of remediation for any areas of weakness based on the results of health-related fitness assessment.

62D7ADF3F2B846DCB720A12B9CD76406.description: Identifies major muscles used in selected physical activities.

1DF58AF4B3F94BFB93A4CE85A4796F28.description: Describes the role of warm-ups and cool-downs before and after physical activity.

6E83CA7E705449CBA47D4491D2AB0415.description: Identifies each of the components of the overload principle (FITT Formula: frequency, intensity, time and type) for different types of physical activity (aerobic, muscular fitness, and flexibility).

CDCFD23E60214AF8964230988F6754F4.description: Differentiates between aerobic and anaerobic capacity and between muscular strength and endurance.

18098BEF926943E1A06AD44AFE2010C7.description: Employs correct techniques and methods of stretching.

567C6C364D4C4A05A12C494C5C1DF29E.description: Set and monitors a self-selected physical activity goal for aerobic and/or muscle-and bone-strengthening activity based on current fitness level.

63209B4400F646FDAA82A2CF748D9885.description: Identifies the components of skill-related fitness.

3F6DA2C949464E9FA2DF26AD4432A25D.description: Participates in moderate to vigorous physical activity that includes intermittent or continuous aerobic physical activity of both moderate and vigorous intensity for at least 60 minutes per day.

471D8CB2DA5248EAA6118CEC44969527.description: Participates in a variety of lifetime recreational team sports, outdoor pursuits or dance activities.

2B8071768617403AB242B79ACC15B7DE.description: Participates in a variety of aerobic fitness activities with or without technology, (e.g., Dance, Dance Revolution or Wii-Fit).

831D6755C890434AAB1C6D1B62DD4CE9.description: Participates in a variety of aerobic fitness activities (e.g., cardio-kick, step aerobics and aerobic dance).

A149E4427FC845D089818690414A3D01.description: Participates in self-selected physical activity outside of physical education class.

E6FF5A3C2C244A8E86352AA65F25A88B.description: Describes how being physically active leads to a healthy body.

EEE57231F694412FBCC8BEC9F5A7B6AB.description: Demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness.

EB613B1A1BB34EB79975967A5A5A4A17.description: Makes appropriate decisions, based on the weather, level of difficulty due to conditions or ability to ensure safety of self and others.

BA316D78EFF046B5B4DC5CC6F92F6AC1.description: Varies application of force during dance or gymnastic activities.

FC1AAF6D13A3423CA3AA57157F005EA4.description: Identifies the correct defensive play based on the situation (e.g., number of outs).

4DB627A98ED34203AC2EF813F71513A4.description: Identifies open spaces and attempts to strike object into that space.

7BE5E4B9A03C4794890B101BC96B1154.description: Selects appropriate shot and/or club based on location of the object in relation to the target.

1FB28DA73D6843118E1DBB80474293C6.description: Reduces open space on defense by making the body larger and reducing passing angles.

B5EE06666DE442F2953ADEDAE7B05585.description: Creates open space by using the width and length of the field/court on offense.

1979BFCC652F4FD19F2C213081543292.description: Executes at least one of the following offensive tactics to create open space: moves to open space without the ball; uses a variety of passes, pivots and fakes; give & go.

8594C59334754F44815C7B9B8723BB93.description: Creates open space by using locomotor movements (e.g., walking, running, jumping and landing) in combination with movement (e.g., varying pathways; change of speed, direction or pace).

6BE5FE3F47AE46E39A351E00D3BCAB0F.description: Applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance.

4735AC9009F24CEFAD94D8A7D5B15867.description: Demonstrates correct technique for basic skills in one self-selected individual-performance activity.

F803DCAD481C448DAE9B0B55AA735BDC.description: Demonstrates correct technique for basic skills in one self-selected outdoor pursuit.

C95512721EB84518AC5ABFF00D6F80AB.description: Catches, with a mature pattern, from different trajectories using a variety of objects in varying practice tasks.

8E6C8E1A486C4FC6B950355ADBAACE96.description: Strikes a pitched ball, with an implement, in a variety of practice tasks.

DFF8B5054E404CF6A5DF0574E49648F1.description: Strikes, with an implement, a stationary object for accuracy in activities (e.g., croquet, shuffleboard, or golf).

FE3C07E1541645D893B186A35D70B9D6.description: Demonstrates a mature underhand pattern for a modified target game (e.g., bowling, bocce, bean bags, or horseshoes).

9ECE36E8D93249E6BAEE6F76C7DF80FC.description: Two-hand-volleys with control in a variety of practice tasks.

528F245286C04652B1386937B132BB6E.description: Forehand volleys with a mature form and control using a short-handled implement.

F4A3B6D604924796AB17A7B6F0A9C8EF.description: Demonstrates the mature form of the forehand and backhand strokes with a short-handled implement in net games (e.g., paddleball, pickle ball, or tennis).

C15A928B124B40F397E3BEB27034F9D9.description: Strikes with a mature overhand pattern in a non-dynamic environment (closed skills) for net/wall games (e.g., volleyball, badminton and tennis).

31538A6001144F4B880785DC22228083.description: Performs a legal underhand serve with control for net/wall games (e.g., badminton, volleyball, or pickle ball).

39124B0B897A44B5BAF8EF20D3A57907.description: Shoots on goal with power in a dynamic environment as appropriate to the activity.

80115784C54F482C9D1956C1490D34BF.description: Dribbles with dominant hand using a change of speed and direction in a variety of practice tasks.

EAC11B2E432C42168A1F60F0DAA9AC0A.description: Performs pivots, fakes and jab steps designed to create open space during practice tasks.

BE5EA7E842F3435A8147909C3C646A30.description: Throws, while stationary, a leading pass to a moving receiver.

5CFE813898E24D1090BCBFC18768133C.description: Passes and receives with hands in combination with locomotor patterns of running, change of direction and speed with competency in modified invasion games (e.g., basketball, flag football).

F313C53243074569BC1A6C8037C759B7.description: Catches with a mature pattern from a variety of trajectories using different objects in varying practice tasks.

1DE8ACF610F2466CA97730FAF0B869CB.description: Throws with a mature pattern for distance or power appropriate to the practice task (e.g., distance = outfield to home plate; power = second base to first base).

09F74AE1831B4D5CB76E4F3761254892.description: Combines actions, balances and weight transfers to create a gymnastics sequence with a partner on equipment or apparatus.

2C754D4BDD394DE88B685D1C7F853534.description: Demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for English Language Arts

FA7EEB4F483F486BB53435AEE2B8D93E.description: Students will write independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for reflection and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two) to communicate with different audiences for a variety of purposes.

58672715DC1543B79ADFCAC23E116017.description: Writing: Students will write independently for extended periods of time. Students will vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task.

E725D94EBE9D459998881368D8749D33.description: Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes and read independently for extended periods of time.

575B5BDA605D48D4813C7160610B8B8C.description: Reading: Students will read independently for a variety of purposes and for extended periods of time. Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes.

CD4F7B1D731C4EE9B58662AF458CB761.description: Independent Reading and Writing - Students will read and write for a variety of purposes including, but not limited to, academic and personal.

B4123D089A4D4D9A9865A55F47601486.description: Students will create presentations using videos, photos, and other multimedia elements to support communication and clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

43B8D3CACCBC40669CC6DF690B1B57ED.description: Students will create multimodal content that effectively communicates an idea using technology or appropriate media.

3772043684FF4FADAAF9B88610307F19.description: Writing: Students will create multimodal texts to communicate knowledge and develop arguments.

7872849485B5434CA3C30C362A3B451E.description: Students will compare and contrast how ideas and topics are depicted in a variety of media and formats.

1EB9E10BFDC3461E988962DB40D996C9.description: Students will locate, organize, and analyze information from a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts to generate and answer literal and interpretive questions to create new understandings.

75AEBEA2336043B2972EC2B7EC8B57FD.description: Reading: Students will evaluate written, oral, visual, and digital texts in order to draw conclusions and analyze arguments.

F2935C51A45B43CE8005495D7750EB72.description: Multimodal Literacies - Students will acquire, refine, and share knowledge through a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts.

847BB4BB6A594ED2A133F6F75D3BB0D3.description: Students will summarize and present information in a report.

0F7CB8C2587E456D9D32A5BCC09DA66E.description: Students will organize information found during research, following a modified citation style (e.g., author, title, publication date) with guidance and support.

6A030EC14E464E2BA70CADD4A774ACB3.description: Students will generate a viable research question about a specific topic.

5EBB43DAFD0A470EA53335EA81B619CF.description: Writing: Students will summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create reports, projects, papers, texts, and presentations for multiple purposes.

A3A982010E674FC0AB4EEA6B1720A9C7.description: Students will determine the relevance and reliability of the information gathered.

34B60C6E571042279B18A1A415E166D1.description: Students will use graphic features including photos, illustrations, captions, titles, labels, headings, subheadings, italics, sidebars, charts, graphs, and legends to interpret a text.

E885D83559F84784851151709BA452C8.description: Students will use their own viable research questions to find information about a specific topic.

3E0D2396244A40E089597768A6D328C1.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize resources to acquire and refine knowledge.

E538BFE642664912A535674AA9B27313.description: Research - Students will engage in inquiry to acquire, refine, and share knowledge.

9D7259EEF7E246EDA72476DBD29E3B17.description: Students will compose declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences.

A3C36DD21F3A4716A1B6D9EDE981FF1C.description: Students will compose simple, compound, and complex sentences and questions, create sentences with an understood subject, and correct fragments and run-on sentences.

3FEAE3B3D3DA4925A3D753603F1D09CD.description: Students will compose and expand grammatically correct sentences and questions with appropriate commas, end marks, apostrophes, and quotation marks as needed for dialogue.

EEF47AADCC1E49C3BB770A884008754A.description:
Students will capitalize
  • familial relations
  • proper adjectives
  • conventions of letter writing

7743177814EF45648BC99488F4862F22.description:
Writing: Students will demonstrate command of Standard English grammar, mechanics, and usage through writing and other modes of communication. These standards begin in Kindergarten. K.5.W.1 Students will capitalize, with guidance and support:
  • their first name
  • the pronoun "I."

D3A053F7CEE841AEA3E84A35CEA41D08.description: Students will recognize the subject and verb agreement.

BCEA29478DCD458BAB2331C881062F34.description: Students will recognize prepositional phrases and conjunctions.

1DFF9CB7D21F472A9DBF859B4DE6A1BF.description: Students will recognize comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs.

9AAD40057A7B471EB4B86DB0878BA06D.description: Students will recognize present perfect verbs and verb tense to identify settings, times, sequences, and conditions in text.

2DDA9C05EF8C4F618B8869D31A7C7240.description: Students will recognize pronouns and irregular possessive nouns.

03A355284B6C463BA31C0B2B043C4EB0.description: Reading: Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to analyze and evaluate a variety of texts.

6808AE5D7828483DA4DD37CBF7333858.description: Language - Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to reading and writing.

D4B2B1E453344D63A478B1F53F9BCA7A.description: Students will select appropriate language to create a specific effect according to purpose in writing.

B5D32F483E8040FDA6CCC3EC9CC1BCCF.description: Students will use domain-appropriate vocabulary to communicate ideas in writing.

52E88030A4644A59A19683DBFF9E8CDE.description: Writing: Students will apply knowledge of vocabularies to communicate by using descriptive, academic, and domain-appropriate abstract and concrete words in their writing.

8F7F43E4942B41F7B6292ED3836B9DC6.description: Students will use a dictionary or glossary (print and/or electronic) to determine or clarify the meanings, syllabication, and pronunciation of words.

92D0C3F620FA463C99A8E0413FE2A437.description: Students will infer relationships among words with multiple meanings, including synonyms, antonyms, and more complex homographs and homonyms.

7C94EA8B660A4A39A94A1E4DB7B9A22E.description: Students will use context clues to determine the meaning of words or distinguish among multiple-meaning words.

60246A5BBA5A455AB2EC3FA1DA920723.description: Students will use word parts (e.g., affixes, Greek and Latin roots, stems) to define and determine the meaning of new words.

CA9C2FC956DB483F9A0AEC5864253EA6.description: Students will increase knowledge of academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabulary to infer meaning of grade-level text.

5D3BB2423FF24E9FBC980CB1FA200F1C.description: Reading: Students will expand academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabularies through reading, word study, and class discussion.

3EB611A64B2946A39A8F5E88DCDC2FF2.description: Vocabulary - Students will expand their working vocabularies to effectively communicate and understand texts.

63234090D96743A4B41598A0E0EE0676.description: Opinion: Students will express an opinion about a topic and provide fact-based reasons as support.

3393FAD00A34418C8783108E6F1004B7.description: Informative: Students will write facts about a subject, including a clear main idea with supporting details, and use transitional and signal words.

E54057370E8A4F7185B9002EE745C31A.description: Narrative: Students will write narratives incorporating characters, plot, setting, point of view, conflict (i.e., solution and resolution), and dialogue.

71E9A21D80724AEAAF56291E573400DC.description: Writing: Students will write for varied purposes and audiences in all modes, using fully developed ideas, strong organization, well-chosen words, fluent sentences, and appropriate voice.

E20B47C245A542598F10B85A35DCFE3F.description: Students will ask and answer inferential questions using the text to support answers.

460D36F158084B299D9E07B4CCDDD54B.description: Students will describe the structure of a text (e.g., description, compare/contrast, sequential, problem/solution, cause/effect).

9721B04851FB4AC088BA7B83DB61D0D2.description: Students will distinguish fact from opinion in a text and investigate facts for accuracy.

AD7F39291FBD41B4A50F419A093075ED.description:
Students will find examples of literary devices:
  • simile
  • metaphor
  • personification
  • onomatopoeia
  • hyperbole
  • imagery
  • symbolism (Students will find textual evidence when provided with examples.)
  • tone (Students will find textual evidence when provided with examples.)

CC7D7AB718AA4E35B7E737ADA1B98178.description:
Students will describe key literary elements:
  • setting
  • plot
  • characters (i.e., protagonist, antagonist)
  • characterization
  • theme

BC2960B1A65C4573916D81AD74A3389C.description: Students will infer whether a story is narrated in first or third person point of view in grade-level literary and/or informational text.

2866A17C47E7404684BCBB0688D21080.description: Students will determine the author's purpose (i.e., entertain, inform, persuade) and infer the difference between the stated and implied purpose.

36075337A02440CCBA693137678C3767.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts of all literary and informational genres from a variety of historical, cultural, ethnic, and global perspectives.

CD5A7963F163439FB7681FB2470FC3A1.description: Critical Reading and Writing - Students will apply critical thinking skills to reading and writing.

F37C27831B9746098C32257F7B271FFD.description: Students will use resources to find correct spellings of words (e.g., word wall, vocabulary notebook, print and electronic dictionaries, and spell-check).

6B1B1B7578C146A79262D02A6E353472.description: Students will correctly spell grade-appropriate words while editing.

A03AFF6EF33B4EB9B16F62F74E9AE69E.description: Students will edit drafts and revise for clarity and organization.

1B924802CE1A4845A05813D781287393.description: Students will develop drafts by categorizing ideas and organizing them into paragraphs.

44FC10121477493CBBA809FC4927D21E.description: Writing: Students will develop and strengthen writing by engaging in a recursive process that includes prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, and publishing.

0A371937BAE049B992A6C9B872B0E9E6.description: Students will begin to paraphrase main ideas with supporting details in a text.

43CDDE6CA4184331B64CE6A10DD67E46.description: Students will summarize events or plots (i.e., beginning, middle, end, conflict, and climax) of a story or text.

643E216120C0407D9F445610FC6C2080.description: Students will compare and contrast details in literary and nonfiction/informational texts to discriminate various genres.

73612B785DCC4CAB94705B56CB5E9F5A.description: Students will distinguish how key details support the main idea of a passage.

778D45A3867A4BCF9C2CBCA75D4B2B1A.description: Reading: Students will read and comprehend increasingly complex literary and informational texts.

18AF1C7501104CA387B8855AD8FAB4B1.description: Reading and Writing Process - Students will use a variety of recursive reading and writing processes.

E19F913505B642CEB2413E59767E53A8.description: Students will orally read grade-level text at an appropriate rate, smoothly and accurately, with expression that connotes comprehension.

A5C2D907CDB049D39CB3E4F4A14A6FD1.description: Students will read high frequency and irregularly spelled grade-level words with automaticity in text.

1C30E1B72BC844B29B24227B0192AA77.description: Fluency: Students will recognize high-frequency words and read grade-level text smoothly and accurately, with expression that connotes comprehension.

FB57533AA70342EAAD3D484EECDE2A35.description: Students will use their combined knowledge of letter-sound correspondences, syllable patterns, morphology and semantics to accurately read unfamiliar words, including multisyllabic words.

AE4EA3BB7A2C454CAB18C848FD8925B7.description: Phonics and Word Study: Students will decode and read words in context and isolation by applying phonics and word analysis skills.

3F4F244F61904E31A9A1E4097D6380B2.description: Students will correctly form letters in print and cursive and use appropriate spacing for letters, words, and sentences.

A99046936DA3458B8414975ABF2E1D9D.description: Print Concepts: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the organization and basic features of print, including book handling skills and the understanding that printed materials provide information and tell stories.

1A7362CBEA1D4CDE9C686A3B812A9A39.description: Reading Foundations - Students will develop foundational skills for future reading success by working with sounds, letters, and text.

D9EAED15364348D4AF80A71D5A0A71A7.description: Students will work effectively and respectfully within diverse groups, share responsibility for collaborative work, and value individual contributions made by each group member.

9D0D14106BB34E3B9F6D7CF88E046466.description: Students will report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences at an appropriate pace.

FEA1B5D29282430BB0D9A6CB6B4EB586.description: Writing: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening to create individual and group projects and presentations.

70FC326DE329477FA264A2A9D2C278A2.description: Students will engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts, expressing their own ideas clearly while building on the ideas of others in pairs, diverse groups, and whole class settings.

E0237D5FD4B3422484CA7583299C791A.description: Students will ask and answer questions to seek help, get information, or clarify information presented orally through text or other media to confirm understanding.

8414D771F19846F3B174353CB33B5CB2.description: Students will actively listen and speak clearly using appropriate discussion rules.

D7B1BED7CAE943AE8CA15D07D3F44726.description: Reading: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening.

D1E3BF862B094A55ABADFC78883F6F12.description: Speaking and Listening - Students will speak and listen effectively in a variety of situations including, but not limited to, responses to reading and writing.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Physical Education

37659499C83243B59DD58452B25AAF25.description: Demonstrates socially acceptable conflict resolution skills.

B0B1D4C10F5A44D5A8DED7DBE17ACC75.description: Compares physical activities that bring confidence and challenge.

119B72CAE4554CFC80D46D89246C698B.description: Recognizes the value of "Good Health Balance".

D87DC97F2707438F9619E268F6C1FC15.description: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction.

A254F6DBF8754383A08C0FC21B60CBBA.description: Works safely with physical education equipment.

109266598B9347F889149A57B2C8A887.description: Works independently and safely in physical education.

774354A62CAA497CB0BC7B27DEA45108.description: Recognizes the role of rules and etiquette in teacher designed physical activities.

C7A7056C9D6D45838B1E0090DA39E1A2.description: Works independently with others in partner environments without regard to differences.

9A534EE159724CFF8F52F67A66898158.description: Accepts specific corrective feedback from the teacher.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for English Language Arts

890B73DBE9474EC0BE465BB65BCEE2BD.description: Students will write independently over extended periods of time (e.g., time for reflection and revision) and for shorter timeframes (e.g., a single sitting or a day or two) to communicate with different audiences for a variety of purposes.

80C0A91132A24C479DAFDFDD9FEE6BE4.description: Writing: Students will write independently for extended periods of time. Students will vary their modes of expression to suit audience and task.

C37A5CF4EAD342ADA0153DCCC62C6546.description: Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes and read independently for extended periods of time.

89964FF5FE9B4263839000DA3FDD273C.description: Reading: Students will read independently for a variety of purposes and for extended periods of time. Students will select appropriate texts for specific purposes.

5D82F2D18FF642EA9145511248D008DF.description: Independent Reading and Writing - Students will read and write for a variety of purposes including, but not limited to, academic and personal.

76E2530A852847888152050AAF7766FE.description: Students will create presentations using video, photos, and other multimedia elements to support communication and clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

4C7A11BB4FF84A6A93E2FBEC5491A3F5.description: Students will create multimodal content that communicates an idea using technology or appropriate media.

B8740CEA6A024C52A6DE3D6BF94823FF.description: Writing: Students will create multimodal texts to communicate knowledge and develop arguments.

CAE090C15C7044989BA46BF750098495.description: Students will compare how ideas and topics are depicted in a variety of media and formats

FA3046758BE3482CA738C90448B913A5.description: Students will locate, organize, and use information from a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts to generate and answer literal questions.

A820CB9D3A9D44A7B25D4D3653523E91.description: Reading: Students will evaluate written, oral, visual, and digital texts in order to draw conclusions and analyze arguments.

B5E457AB17524B68913FF5BC390C9644.description: Multimodal Literacies - Students will acquire, refine, and share knowledge through a variety of written, oral, visual, digital, non-verbal, and interactive texts.

DD12A27E321E4D0B8F391F701631799B.description: Students will summarize and present information in a report.

79646F11FA144C879039BEA560FAC0E3.description: Students will organize information found during group or individual research, using graphic organizers or other aids.

4D98C9005D494DDE81C6B4F900FA41A0.description: Students will generate a list of topics of interest and individual questions about one specific topic of interest.

767E7771D522464DB5B1D1FBED2FF691.description: Writing: Students will summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create reports, projects, papers, texts, and presentations for multiple purposes.

BF77DA0401544449B8FE60EEE7456588.description: Students will determine the relevance and reliability of the information for their specific topic of interest with guidance and support.

7CC54BA85D1C40FCB31B72A5CD6B53D2.description: Students will locate information in visual and text reference sources, electronic resources, and/or interviews.

C4C463897BFB491B8F1600BFE5F990B3.description: Students will use graphic features including photos, illustrations, captions, titles, labels, headings, subheadings, italics, sidebars, charts, graphs, and legends to define a text.

3FED98838D2045A686A4772F5636987A.description: Students will use their own questions to find information on their topic.

822B04F817E245F9A0723A2F4EC6E959.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize resources to acquire and refine knowledge.

907B31125E464A6A94293CFFF8FDAE26.description: Research - Students will engage in inquiry to acquire, refine, and share knowledge.

F3381C31D2BC4A658086AA331DE1AE0C.description: Students will compose simple, compound and complex declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences.

948C3AE3811D4AC2B2DED21AC57E448A.description: Students will compose and expand grammatically correct sentences and questions with appropriate commas, apostrophes, quotation marks, and end marks as needed for dialogue.

4CFBF4C364B14DDDBFEA87265CF8E732.description: Students will use complex contractions (e.g., should've, won't).

17DF0294F0634F5F8705DE9CE7AB0499.description:
Students will capitalize and appropriately punctuate:
  • titles of respect
  • appropriate words in titles
  • geographical names

D3F42B3F20AA46FCA24F34BEE919D5D8.description:
Writing: Students will demonstrate command of Standard English grammar, mechanics, and usage through writing and other modes of communication. These standards begin in Kindergarten. K.5.W.1 Students will capitalize, with guidance and support:
  • their first name
  • the pronoun "I."

DC884819C696460AB645BDEBFA4E8ED5.description: Students will recognize the subject and verb agreement.

183BEBE156194BA495D9C2AE9C00A130.description: Students will recognize prepositions and conjunctions.

8449C239412A44239B05D4B2201DD35B.description: Students will recognize adjectives, articles as adjectives, and adverbs.

27D3928562D7412D9C2D7D059401D585.description: Students will recognize irregular and past participle verbs and verb tense to identify settings, times, and sequences in text.

E505564683FA4D26B6EC45D0C330724B.description: Students will recognize pronouns and possessive nouns.

256F05CBDFFF46508F1C7266E393B4CE.description: Reading: Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to analyze and evaluate a variety of texts.

D59EBDBF7190407B9227AA956855FAA8.description: Language - Students will apply knowledge of grammar and rhetorical style to reading and writing.

BA0C016C02644C039AEB2894AE631BB7.description: Students will select appropriate language according to purpose in writing.

C36C5D2F88CB41E680A2173608863B8F.description: Students will use domain-appropriate vocabulary to communicate ideas in writing.

3D6A725E3F6B40B8822ED6DF3DF6920E.description: Writing: Students will apply knowledge of vocabularies to communicate by using descriptive, academic, and domain-appropriate abstract and concrete words in their writing.

F146F77C38EA4B3281B9D6CB4010192A.description: Students will use a dictionary or glossary (print and/or electronic) to determine or clarify the meanings, syllabication, and pronunciation of words.

24915E15771B465B8B152FB2000542EE.description: Students will infer relationships among words, including synonyms, antonyms, homographs, and homonyms.

B7648D22F5D744268346B9D5370C4BB4.description: Students will use context clues to determine the meaning of words or distinguish among multiple-meaning words.

8189EEBFAEBC441584EB77429C064A8A.description: Students will use word parts (e.g., affixes, roots, stems) to define and determine the meaning of new words.

BE7DDB1C51714E9197CFEB69B3273A8D.description: Students will increase knowledge of academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabulary to infer meaning of grade-level text.

B796E7B701584E8A9A83DEBC42F9F37C.description: Reading: Students will expand academic, domain-appropriate, grade-level vocabularies through reading, word study, and class discussion.

482834E652794D368028491C9DAF3ADC.description: Vocabulary - Students will expand their working vocabularies to effectively communicate and understand texts.

454FBCAB70804F2BA78FF246DC80E34F.description: Opinion: Students will express an opinion about a topic and provide reasons as support.

4858D2240B07448C88CB720BD3AB68E1.description: Informative: Students will write facts about a subject, including a main idea with supporting details, and use transitional and signal words.

D34F6EFCE40240379A1E029A9829A2EB.description: Narrative: Students will write narratives incorporating characters, plot, setting, point of view, and conflict (i.e., solution and resolution).

3DF57B5D83604F1ABDBAC91C72F631D5.description: Writing: Students will write for varied purposes and audiences in all modes, using fully developed ideas, strong organization, well-chosen words, fluent sentences, and appropriate voice.

7AAC8E5F07C247D486E8EBF0E2F28EE2.description: Students will ask and answer inferential questions using the text to support answers with guidance and support.

3843565F89C74692A5AC9C1A2472732D.description: Students will describe the structure of a text (e.g., description, compare/contrast, sequential, problem/solution, cause/effect) with guidance and support.

004BF886BFA94903BC18EB1CF5E65D06.description: Students will distinguish fact from opinion in a text.

321A020A01AE44DAA4985A83583F105B.description:
Students will find examples of literary devices:
  • simile
  • metaphor
  • personification
  • onomatopoeia
  • hyperbole

FAC9F63F214B491DAD3E1A7FE67D2DF8.description:
Students will find textual evidence when provided with examples of literary elements and organization:
  • setting (i.e., time, place)
  • plot
  • characters
  • characterization
  • theme

304B6C59343A400D8A32821052230ABD.description: Students will infer whether a story is narrated in first or third person point of view in grade-level literary and/or informational text.

7405DE418BD349AF8E363E467C2E7965.description: Students determine the author's stated and implied purpose (i.e., entertain, inform, persuade).

CCB2904DD1FE460BB62C773DFAC255BD.description: Reading: Students will comprehend, interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts of all literary and informational genres from a variety of historical, cultural, ethnic, and global perspectives.

809DE4DD806942898C8E96FA4DAF8A93.description: Critical Reading and Writing - Students will apply critical thinking skills to reading and writing.

92348425B5B94B85B5A210829B98B76F.description: Students will use resources to find correct spellings of words (e.g., word wall, vocabulary notebook, print and electronic dictionaries).

3E2BE670F4CB484DA77C56C2063CF87F.description: Students will correctly spell grade-appropriate words while editing.

1B129E4E62FA4BF9906937EF390209B7.description: Students will edit drafts and revise for clarity and organization.

F8BAE966CEC842D0A9D01251621DF808.description: Students will develop drafts by categorizing ideas and organizing them into paragraphs using correct paragraph indentations.

99A21B879C3C4E778C24E23B59D8E45C.description: Writing: Students will develop and strengthen writing by engaging in a recursive process that includes prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, and publishing.

8486155B3255474BA6CCF2CC84FE9265.description: Students will summarize events or plots (i.e., beginning, middle, end, and conflict) of a story or text.

E115B74DF32D49F69726C30A9A3D8AFA.description: Students will compare and contrast details (e.g., plots or events, settings, and characters) to discriminate genres.

A89C2118D6654D27A388F3D4F80D3E6B.description: Students will locate the main idea and key supporting details of a text or section of text.

F153C9C34F7642A09B833618E0E1B5D0.description: Reading: Students will read and comprehend increasingly complex literary and informational texts.

9A5CD20952A1405B87620AC3F97004E4.description: Reading and Writing Process - Students will use a variety of recursive reading and writing processes.

11DB41327AB44064923A0C35325B59E6.description: Students will orally read grade-level text at an appropriate rate, smoothly and accurately, with expression that connotes comprehension.

8316DCA3814B4FDFBCB198880072C11C.description: Students will read high frequency and/or irregularly spelled grade-level words with automaticity in text.

86EA87E4409E469292D48938CA0AD1D8.description: Fluency: Students will recognize high-frequency words and read grade-level text smoothly and accurately, with expression that connotes comprehension.

077CFAC39E6A4ED096FCF11856B364CB.description: Students will use decoding skills and semantics in context when reading new words in a text, including multisyllabic words.

15AABFD185534F64AEB558F973D5EECC.description:
Students will decode multisyllabic words by applying knowledge of structural analysis:
  • all major syllable patterns
  • contractions
  • abbreviations
  • common roots and related prefixes and suffixes

4FAC7D2F52A347BEBC14BEF45A22F0DF.description:
Students will decode multisyllabic words using their knowledge of:
  • "r" controlled vowels (e.g., ar, er, ir or, ur)
  • vowel diphthongs (vowel combinations having two vowel sounds e.g., oi as in boil, oy as in boy]

7B84D47E104A487B94530776A757F84B.description: Phonics and Word Study: Students will decode and read words in context and isolation by applying phonics and word analysis skills.

F497B3A1FD3D46BCA3B5B0D31F678CD8.description: Students will correctly form letters in print and cursive and use appropriate spacing for letters, words, and sentences.

02B29E6FCFC5413BAEB773D01F2CCABC.description: Print Concepts: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the organization and basic features of print, including book handling skills and the understanding that printed materials provide information and tell stories.

2E2C61A6C8614985B9F896DB1BA84672.description: Reading Foundations - Students will develop foundational skills for future reading success by working with sounds, letters, and text.

3613119E1639439A90E7E91D797E92B6.description: Students will work respectfully within diverse groups, share responsibility for collaborative work, and value individual contributions made by each group member.

5B1B8E038C6A473AB87538B3A70051DB.description: Students will report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences at an appropriate pace.

EA5FB10735134409950D9BD7A5479C93.description: Writing: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening to create individual and group projects and presentations.

64CAC65BEA6C4FB2B61217354001ADDE.description: Students will engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts, expressing their own ideas clearly in pairs, diverse groups, and whole class settings.

87D916D8400E4E13B08B86F2DC88B80D.description: Students will ask and answer questions to seek help, get information, or clarify about information presented orally through text or other media to confirm understanding.

9FD1CA961C004275BC75C0D61DB23177.description: Students will actively listen and speak clearly using appropriate discussion rules.

AFA8F55B7FD7402C9A38E9EFD49B3285.description: Reading: Students will develop and apply effective communication skills through speaking and active listening.

F9B1FA1954B3422D95A4D48D4F569973.description: Speaking and Listening - Students will speak and listen effectively in a variety of situations including, but not limited to, responses to reading and writing.

921DB58DD82C4A488613D0AF170F8276.description: Demonstrates warm up and cool down relative to the cardiorespiratory fitness assessment.

C866BE6A76114D259177984627DC6D02.description: Identifies the components of health related fitness.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Mathematics

A46F69AC67984CE8A1F2122029DEE709.description:
Develop the Ability to Communicate Mathematically:
Students will discuss, write, read, interpret and translate ideas and
concepts mathematically. As they progress, students’ ability to
communicate mathematically will include their increased use of
mathematical language and terms and analysis of mathematical
definitions.

D7A9A39D2E8D4DA0A60A5F99252A4616.description:
Develop the Ability to Make Conjectures, Model, and Generalize:
Make predictions and conjectures and draw conclusions throughout the
problem solving process based on patterns and the repeated structures
in mathematics. Students will create, identify, and extend patterns as a
strategy for solving and making sense of problems.

2BFFA980C2E440069DB3727BF5D4188B.description:
Develop a Productive Mathematical Disposition:
Hold the belief that mathematics is sensible, useful and worthwhile.
Students will develop the habit of looking for and making use of
patterns and mathematical structures. They will persevere and become
resilient, effective problem solvers.

7295060FBBA141C889DB1F64BECB6F67.description:
Develop Mathematical Reasoning:
Explore and communicate a variety of reasoning strategies to think
through problems. Students will apply their logic to critique the thinking
and strategies of others to develop and evaluate mathematical
arguments, including making arguments and counterarguments and
making connections to other contexts.

F96B6AB19ED045AE9F0A312A3198DA34.description:
Develop Strategies for Problem Solving:
Analyze the parts of complex mathematical tasks and identify entry
points to begin the search for a solution. Students will select from a
variety of problem solving strategies and use corresponding
multiple representations (verbal, physical, symbolic, pictorial,
graphical, tabular) when appropriate. They will pursue solutions to
various tasks from real-world situations and applications that are
often interdisciplinary in nature. They will find methods to verify
their answers in context and will always question the
reasonableness of solutions.

DF5EFDF2BB8F4D09850CF9F29773FA32.description:
Develop Accurate and Appropriate Procedural Fluency:
Learn efficient procedures and algorithms for computations and
repeated processes based on a strong sense of numbers. Develop
fluency in addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of
numbers and expressions. Students will generate a sophisticated
understanding of the development and application of algorithms
and procedures.

3A89F8C460B840E7ABADD249A291CAF3.description:
Develop a Deep and Flexible Conceptual Understanding:
Demonstrate a deep and flexible conceptual understanding of
mathematical concepts, operations, and relations while making
mathematical and real-world connections. Students will develop an
understanding of how and when to apply and use the mathematics
they know to solve problems.

5458B56AD994476BB06A3FEA9205F8A6.description: Students will understand the principles of government, the benefits of democratic systems, and their responsibilities as citizens.
