2F12AF1D3C3448F0AC6CE79F0F661AFC.description: Analyze the graph of a polynomial function by identifying the domain, range, intercepts, zeros, relative maxima, relative minima, and intervals of increase and decrease.

051611D753F24023BEA861D98A451F8F.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions. Identify the domain, range, asymptotes, and x- and y-intercepts using various methods and tools that may include calculators or other appropriate technology. Recognize exponential decay and growth graphically and algebraically.

B6D1C44F92704CE38E09CFE195D7B401.description: Graph a quadratic function. Identify the domain, range, x- and y-intercepts, maximum or minimum value, axis of symmetry, and vertex using various methods and tools that may include a graphing calculator or appropriate technology.

01E0058FFFDC461E9051F0D479BB50E6.description: Identify the parent forms of exponential, radical (square root and cube root only), quadratic, and logarithmic functions. Predict the effects of transformations [f(x + c), f(x) + c, f(cx), and cf(x)] algebraically and graphically.

AE7B6774605943F8B44C33DC0DAD231C.description: Use algebraic, interval, and set notations to specify the domain and range of various types of functions, and evaluate a function at a given point in its domain.

38A2C126555143C5930D1E2FA8E04D83.description: Understand functions as descriptions of covariation (how related quantities vary together).

A4A40BE7EDD54020841C19CF46095AE1.description: Solve problems that can be modeled using finite geometric sequences and series given the n<sup>th</sup> terms and sum formulas. Graphing calculators or other appropriate technology may be used.

369D220948D64C2B96B7925C79801CA5.description: Solve problems that can be modeled using arithmetic sequences or series given the n^th terms and sum formulas. Graphing calculators or other appropriate technology may be used.

7ED443EAE5364DA599DCAC807A4B8742.description: Recognize that geometric sequences are exponential using equations, tables, graphs, and verbal descriptions. Given the formula f(x) = a(r)<sup>x</sup>, find the next term and define the meaning of a and r within the context of the problem.

6BE73067BCA649D2820C8EA17B27C810.description: Recognize that arithmetic sequences are linear using equations, tables, graphs, and verbal descriptions. Using the pattern, find the next term.

DD14C3D0A7194F67A390EED5881DAFFF.description: Represent and solve mathematical and real-world problems involving arithmetic and geometric sequences and series.

38015E2B6E82424E90119EECA1B5CE85.description: Rewrite algebraic expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

68FE5EA7990241B58D76FABE6DA8F8D8.description: Recognize that a quadratic function has different equivalent representations [f(x) = ax² + bx + c, f(x) = a(x - h)² + k, and f(x) = a(x - p)(x - q)]. Identify and use the mathematical model that is most appropriate to solve problems.

AC49D77645D8462BBCEAE07B699B7095.description: Add, subtract, multiply, divide, and simplify rational expressions.

BDC66D2EFE984AA5B28E8797EB2F372E.description: Add, subtract, multiply, divide, and simplify polynomial expressions.

9F73959E8AD04BA38FE703489A5A990C.description: Factor polynomial expressions including, but not limited to, trinomials, differences of squares, sum and difference of cubes, and factoring by grouping, using a variety of tools and strategies.

F1C10E4E87B444AE9C6C8FE5A9A91A1F.description: Generate and evaluate equivalent algebraic expressions and equations using various strategies.

7C877FE7B56141A09AE8EC7204A3E898.description: Solve systems of linear inequalities in two variables, with a maximum of three inequalities; graph and interpret the solutions on a coordinate plane. Graphing calculators or other appropriate technology may be used.

05E52555B0564D61A9D7D16CA7E76761.description: Use tools to solve systems of equations containing one linear equation and one quadratic equation. Graphing calculators or other appropriate technology may be used.

A22475BD48EE4E24A4A41216C6ACAA41.description: Represent and evaluate mathematical models using systems of linear equations with a maximum of three variables. Graphing calculators or other appropriate technology may be used.

BE24B77DF3F34882BA4A8E9D289C633B.description: Solve common and natural logarithmic equations using the properties of logarithms.

0C5DDA8743B44C53B99C4E185C34CC12.description: Solve square and cube root equations with one variable, and check for extraneous solutions.

E7F1924FC2E14ABE91D52CD5D8FC68F1.description: Solve polynomial equations with real roots using various methods (e.g., polynomial division, synthetic division, using graphing calculators or other appropriate technology).

82B51AC3F6674FBDAF3E89E2A96BCEE3.description: Solve one-variable rational equations and check for extraneous solutions.

CB29AB74DF2C4AE0B0D4A72C80923ADA.description: Use mathematical models to represent exponential relationships, such as compound interest, depreciation, and population growth. Solve these equations algebraically or graphically (including graphing calculator or other appropriate technology).

BEC7644A90374694907A6C0E8FBCC709.description: Use mathematical models to represent quadratic relationships and solve using factoring, completing the square, the quadratic formula, and various methods (including graphing calculator or other appropriate technology). Find non-real roots when they exist.

539BE983D363469EA1E111481577805B.description: Represent and solve mathematical and real-world problems using nonlinear equations, systems of linear equations, and systems of linear inequalities; interpret the solutions in the original context.

E58B8A40CACD4985B2596044FC0F5715.description: Use addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication of matrices to solve problems.

B8D9F0F3814C4F988AA783DAA463C79E.description: Use matrices to organize and represent data. Identify the order (dimension) of a matrix.

1C025056AB08450287B153F8E9A9272E.description: Extend the understanding of numbers and operations to matrices.

E20AC5FE64E1485886CF167E43818DD5.description: Understand and apply the relationship between rational exponents to integer exponents and radicals to solve problems.

ECD2BB51484B44A2989A3FF3C4665EAF.description: Simplify, add, subtract, multiply, and divide complex numbers.

C3D0C1B075294BA9A4BB0B78DCCFDE49.description: Find the value of i^n for any whole number n.

56E4966447B14AA193A4EDC99A5A525F.description: Extend the understanding of numbers and operations to include complex numbers, radical expressions, and expressions written with rational exponents.

FE7671CFE4AE450C95A48958CFA8DDDB.description: Apply the trigonometric functions as ratios (sine, cosine, tangent) to find side lengths in right triangles in mathematical models, including the coordinate plane.

34B333F324D04DAD997FE87D7A9D88FD.description: Use the definition of the trigonometric functions to determine the sine, cosine, and tangent ratio of an acute angle in a right triangle. Apply the inverse trigonometric functions to find the measure of an acute angle in right triangles.

038CE0FBFEA447CD96A832F2CCEA4372.description: Verify and apply properties of right triangles, including properties of 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles, to solve problems using algebraic and logical reasoning.

67D397F04A29494B9D6B3E0EEEEF4AA8.description: Apply the distance formula, the Pythagorean theorem, and the Pythagorean theorem converse (approximate and exact values, including Pythagorean triples) to solve problems, using algebraic and logical reasoning and mathematical models.

3E7C0CBE3124435682C5E9B6A5382174.description: Apply mathematical relationships of right triangles and trigonometric ratios to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

FEB433905AE249B49AC30CFA7BE32373.description: Apply the properties of circles and relationships among angles; arcs; and distances in a circle among radii, chords, secants, and tangents to solve problems using algebraic and logical reasoning.

69A8C3B30F90482F80E543E278AEF4EE.description: Use the distance and midpoint formula, where appropriate, to recognize and write the radius r, center (h,k), and standard form of the equation of a circle (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² with and without graphs.

C28AFCB96A544FBD9D4F375B5CE89C83.description: Apply the properties of circles to solve problems involving circumference and area, using approximate values and in terms of pi, using algebraic and logical reasoning.

26CDCA0A4CD44C029B69CDB9C43AE988.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems using the properties of circles.

6EBB02864A064C328E9293F48C4B271B.description: Use ratios derived from similar three-dimensional figures to make conjectures, generalize, and to solve for unknown values such as angles, side lengths, perimeter, and circumference of a face, area of a face, and volume.

C3B3C16D74E74FB8BB9A90E642C4E6C5.description: Represent, use, and apply mathematical models and other tools (e.g., nets, measuring devices, formulas) to solve problems involving surface area and volume of three-dimensional figures (prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, spheres, composites of these figures).

F2D061D0C7A44422B05DA190A1946E75.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving three-dimensional figures.

DD858AF19C8045C7AE13837DCD1F328F.description: Use numeric, graphic, and algebraic representations of transformations in two dimensions (e.g., reflections, translations, dilations, rotations about the origin by multiples of 90 ̊) to solve problems involving figures on a coordinate plane and identify types of symmetry.

A835650E54F142238918EE0A0D424290.description: Construct logical arguments to prove triangle similarity (AA, SSS, SAS).

D808017DCB7441F68769FD9417B9078E.description: Construct logical arguments to prove triangle congruence (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and HL).

C9A72345D465497698FBA7E0D1DF1BC6.description: Apply the properties of congruent or similar polygons to solve problems using mathematical models and algebraic and logical reasoning.

C107A7C73D564A31ADDB317171262D80.description: Apply the properties of polygons, and use them to represent and apply mathematical models involving perimeter and area (e.g., triangles, special quadrilaterals, regular polygons up to 12 sides, composite figures).

4937DD47E1E84F24A8BD02C32E743738.description: Use coordinate geometry and algebraic reasoning to represent and analyze line segments and polygons, including determining lengths, midpoints, and slopes of line segments.

0D385D993F344C06A19107DEC666FDBB.description: Apply the properties of special quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, trapezoid, isosceles trapezoid, rhombus, kite, parallelogram) to solve problems involving angle measures and segment lengths using mathematical models, algebraic reasoning, and proofs.

48A53875A4674A538AAA411F522E6149.description: Apply theorems involving the interior and exterior angle sums of polygons to solve problems using mathematical models, algebraic reasoning, and proofs.

3BC0941BC8F44DA69756456D8BDFF360.description: Apply the properties of angles (corresponding, exterior, interior, vertical, complementary, supplementary) to solve problems using mathematical models, algebraic reasoning, and proofs.

A3FAA8E8FF014B5CA74F1E593643E173.description: Use the angle relationships formed by lines cut by a transversal to determine if the lines are parallel and verify, using algebraic and deductive proofs.

57D93244881F4B0CB7C9215B88C2D19E.description: Use properties of parallel lines cut by a transversal to determine angle relationships and solve problems.

7DC6C4DA99F54DEE91E893CC20848232.description: Discover, evaluate, and analyze the relationships between lines, angles, and polygons to solve real-world and mathematical problems; express proofs in a form that clearly justifies the reasoning (e.g., two-column proofs, paragraph proofs, flowcharts).

51E04470061D47A4896B50D2E725DD05.description: Assess the validity of a logical argument and give counterexamples to disprove a statement.

A244D2AEEC604385BC247D2B0351ABB7.description: Analyze and draw conclusions based on a set of conditions using inductive and deductive reasoning. Recognize the logical relationships between a conditional statement and its inverse, converse, and contrapositive.

254841C9821A4FA1BF2297ADD37BE325.description: Use undefined terms, definitions, postulates, and theorems in logical arguments/proofs.

86A7C0DD5ACB4F0280E30AFD6976F40A.description: Use appropriate tools and logic, including algebraic methods, to evaluate mathematical arguments.

FDC2A17274EB48EC894C61ADF3167B09.description: Apply probability concepts to real-world situations to make informed decisions.

5162E2CD1FA54A8ABAB3B0128E20E45B.description: Use simulations and experiments to calculate experimental probabilities.

32F77F00F09242F1B2462FBC48D0E4E6.description: Given a Venn diagram, determine the probability of the union of events, the intersection of events, and the complement of an event. Understand the relationships between these concepts and the words "AND," "OR," and "NOT."

DA431EA8E7F54B54870BE2B81766A41E.description: Apply simple counting procedures (factorials, permutations, combinations, and tree diagrams) to determine sample size, sample space, and calculate probabilities.

F7E29CB92E054CCDA510E7796A13971D.description: Calculate probabilities, and apply probability concepts.

5363ADC813EE42ACAE6727A452C7B126.description: Make predictions based upon the linear regression, and use the correlation coefficient to assess the reliability of those predictions using graphing technology.

BA2DE6FDFBA04A278C6F43D06ED57DE0.description: Collect data and analyze scatter plots for patterns, linearity, and outliers.

B850D234148D4F7BB9B081D3FE21A5E8.description: Display, describe, and compare data sets using summary statistics (central tendency and spread (range)). Utilize technology (e.g., spreadsheets, calculators) to display data and calculate summary statistics.

341B4D635F424DC29BC8F19CAEB8409E.description: Display, describe, and compare data. For linear relationships, make predictions, and assess the reliability of those predictions.

10F11D4F07184D09BEF6C7BFE908488D.description: Add, subtract, and multiply functions using function notation.

2ECE6E3FD35E4B5D8E9455CE1A9EAB54.description: Use function notation; evaluate a function, including nonlinear, at a given point in its domain algebraically and graphically. Interpret the results in terms of the original context.

0EA91F73AA564B839F184517F9A7BF1D.description: Identify and generate equivalent representations of linear functions, graphs, tables, and real-world situations.

366758D93BDD42A09D18C5588BBE33AB.description: Represent functions in multiple ways and use the representation to interpret real-world and mathematical problems.

6A5EEF057AE04D5ABCDA95FCC96D97A3.description: Recognize the parent functions f(x) = x and f(x) = |x|. Predict the effects of vertical and horizontal transformations f(x + c) and f(x) + c, algebraically and graphically.

6D37A2F86FDC48B5A593A24D4F1CD5B1.description: Distinguish between linear and nonlinear (including exponential) functions. Understand that linear functions grow by equal intervals (arithmetic) and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals (geometric).

7AF078FDB7F84D7C89E6BEB1D267B7A0.description: Recognize and understand that families of functions are defined by their characteristics.

D74B1D27AC1B4401B1C5773B01977AB0.description: Interpret graphs as being discrete or continuous.

A6136CE2FC8448F1B905692FD9F4AC58.description: Read and interpret the linear piecewise function, given a graph modeling a situation.

1C8B2C2BB5A643B78DB02705588BB702.description: Write linear functions, using function notation, to represent mathematical models.

068582525C194C94BD623175C01DA005.description: Identify the dependent variable, independent variable, domain and range given a function, equation, or graph. Identify restrictions on the domain and range in mathematical models.

1C406228DE234E8BA0AC903975D54699.description: Understand functions as descriptions of covariation (how related quantities vary together) in real-world and mathematical problems.

3F8A7506554E4789BC2045608EBECEF7.description: Analyze and interpret associations between graphical representations and written scenarios.

CE777EC905E344918CB538FF074EA93D.description: Express linear equations in slope-intercept, point-slope, and standard forms. Convert between these forms.

BC1F33B6277D425D9100CE9F035E5E35.description: Write the equation of the line given its slope and y-intercept, slope and one point, two points, x- and y-intercepts, or a set of data points.

D92943043A9A4A48895BEB658BF2C83F.description: Analyze and interpret mathematical models involving lines that are parallel, perpendicular, horizontal, and vertical.

0B4D2ABCF31F476E894DF80CC4C43413.description: Analyze, use and apply mathematical models and other data sets (e.g., graphs, equations, two points, a set of data points) to calculate and interpret slope and the x- and y-intercepts of a line.

837369472842453880736A3A18725D90.description: Analyze real-world and mathematical problems involving linear equations.

FF31085BBA364C9F8B88E4572004D6C1.description: Evaluate linear, absolute value, rational, and radical expressions. Include applying a nonstandard operation such as x ☉ y=2x + y

CF559B74390E42EEB023BE8537936C21.description: Factor common monomial factors from polynomial expressions and factor quadratic expressions with a leading coefficient of 1.

F8A2D58C1DF54040ABE653DC5C4D2452.description: Simplify polynomial expressions by adding, subtracting, or multiplying.

7FAE4A08AC164D40940D0F8255A0E620.description: Solve equations involving several variables for one variable in terms of the others.

051F1206757D4B5A99621564041A613F.description: Create and evaluate equivalent algebraic expressions and equations using algebraic properties.

32E95E89A5384A54B28CE41FCC673515.description: Represent relationships using mathematical models with compound and absolute value inequalities and solve the resulting inequalities by graphing and interpreting the solutions on a number line.

3973C924AC4F4B52BD6E5498BEECF8D3.description: Represent relationships using mathematical models with linear inequalities; solve the resulting inequalities, graph on a coordinate plane, and interpret the solutions.

B3C20A9BDC7F43A0B4BC7D9B66EDF5D3.description: Represent and solve real-world and mathematical problems using linear inequalities and compound inequalities; interpret solutions in the original context.

03516B05456D4AFC93095493BB87EEB4.description: Analyze, use and apply mathematical models to solve problems involving systems of linear equations with a maximum of two variables by graphing, substitution, and elimination. Graphing calculators or other appropriate technology may be utilized. Interpret the solutions in the original context.

57A96C74FF1B4EA2B7BF24842C9459F0.description: Solve absolute value equations and interpret the solutions in the original context.

FF61B7324BDB4769A5D57A69B30C4AA5.description: Use knowledge of solving equations with rational values to represent, use and apply mathematical models (e.g., angle measures, geometric formulas, dimensional analysis, Pythagorean theorem, science, statistics) and interpret the solutions in the original context.

C03DC17C3DA84CCA824BEDDAF84D0824.description: Represent and solve mathematical and real-world problems using linear equations, absolute value equations, and systems of equations; interpret solutions in the original context.

A9E665A078B5477B8C1467441B2AAC95.description: Add, subtract, multiply, divide, and simplify square roots of constants, rationalizing the denominator when necessary.

857A36B59DFD4D559957C59CBD871E6B.description: Write square roots and cube roots of constants and monomial algebraic expressions in simplest radical form.

2698CCFF01A448C8AFD45008A618E944.description: Extend the understanding of exponents to include square roots and cube roots.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards COMPUTER SCIENCE

D5F87094DAE941368B60F02FEFA2141D.description:
Debate laws and regulations that impact the development
and use of software.

1AF505D5695A480DB8367F765DB3183C.description:
Students will continue to apply the standards and practices from the
previous grade levels.

E33F7809D0B94684AA4D24220567DC4D.description:
Design and implement a study that evaluates or predicts how
creating, testing, and refining computational artifacts has revolutionized an
aspect of our culture and how it might evolve (e.g., education, healthcare,
art/entertainment, energy).

B027DC2C5A544AE180C444CAC5C01987.description:
Evaluate the impact of location and user audience on the
distribution of computing resources in a global society.

55C45DB3736A48AEB34365440F67ADC5.description:
Evaluate the beneficial and harmful effects that computational
artifacts and innovations have on society.

45A933CAD33A4D4C8422CBF9A72F3D70.description:
Modify an existing program to add additional functionality
and discuss intended and unintended implications (e.g., breaking other
functionality).

B5ADB6823FBD437382DAFB6DCC46B2DD.description:
Explain security issues that might lead to compromised
computer programs.

9167EF5EFB8E41348530B09C3E1D3042.description:
Develop and use a series of test cases to verify that a
program performs according to its design specifications.

620B323F1EFB4B6BBF6703A26478CBA3.description:
Systematically examine code for correctness, usability,
readability, efficiency, portability, and scalability through peer review.

16673EA9B16342D3AF44939E1F3AFE2B.description: Develop programs for multiple computing platforms.

BADBDB6D89224CF2BD53092E666CA79C.description:
Design software in a project team environment using
integrated development environments (IDEs), versioning systems, and
collaboration systems.

A7985D08DE7E4DCC8C764846EAE73FFE.description:
Create software that will provide solutions to a variety of users
using multiple software development processes.

E0E1D150D1E4495FA33A3F8C73E476B1.description:
Create programming solutions by reusing existing code (e.g.,
libraries, Application Programming Interface (APIs), code repositories).

434195D2EB9C4BCA95625BD3DEAD8713.description:
Design or redesign a solution to a large-scale computational
problem by identifying generalizable patterns.

012300B8CBE54584A644B011D3F102A0.description:
Construct solutions to problems using student-created
components (e.g., procedures, modules, objects).

68D48F2128EE4B0DAE17CBB6D637764F.description:
Model the execution of repetition (e.g., loops, recursion) of an
algorithm illustrating output and changes in values of named variables.

FAADEB74BC424CC7B97C0A6BFA8CD601.description:
Compare and contrast data structures and their uses (e.g., lists,
stacks, queues).

2C0249894963456F81F2A70AB5FF9C1C.description:
Evaluate algorithms (e.g., sorting, searching) in terms of their
efficiency and clarity.

2A11CFE89BEA4B0AA965B13653B636F0.description:
Critically examine and trace classic algorithms (e.g., selection
sort, insertion sort, binary search, linear search).

AE4625673ADD4E7AB840CECDFBDD7778.description:
Develop an artificial intelligence algorithm to play a game
against a human opponent or solve a real-world problem.

7DD5D4FD8B4943ADB2C6FD5B5E95F810.description:
Model and use appropriate terminology to describe how
artificial intelligence algorithms drive many software and physical systems
(e.g., autonomous robots, pattern recognition, text analysis).

DD91988619BC4E52902CC05F3D45C0C0.description:
Use models and simulations to help plan, conduct, and refine
investigations.

469B6995CF414552B8FD9BD9225BA5D9.description:
Generate data sets that use a variety of data collection tools
and analysis techniques to support a claim and/or communicate
information.

329D8293C01F40808C868F3E04007181.description:
Use data analysis tools and techniques to identify patterns
from complex real-world data.

2128071F0B02451A97C185A18DD5066F.description:
Students will continue to apply the standards and practices from the
previous grade levels.

8B516DE3936944F7B22D1C5AA43E8884.description:
Compare and refine ways in which software developers
protect devices and information from unauthorized access.

32057F247883461DB61908E234735688.description:
Describe the issues that impact network functionality (e.g.,
bandwidth, load, latency, topology).

5A6335F90A7A49B8915A05C477D19FC5.description:
Illustrate how understanding the ways hardware components
facilitate logic, input, output, and storage in computing systems will
support troubleshooting.

F9C8A6153E72463EAF0FFE8EA9B49844.description:
Identify and categorize the roles of a variety of operating
system software.

2020186E5D2B4DC199500A46C4BE003B.description:
Students will continue to apply the standards and practices from the
previous grade levels.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards COMPUTER SCIENCE

37F8AFB741C14B9AB1B6DC51A6CC05B1.description:
Evaluate the social and economic consequences of how law
and ethics interact with digital aspects of privacy, data, property,
information, and identity.

838429DF72904208B78BAC7B60D770E9.description:
Describe and discuss the privacy concerns related to the
large-scale collection and analysis of information about individuals (e.g.,
how websites collect and uses data) that may not be evident to users.

E1D15536D79D43EBB28CB64620279EA3.description:
Describe the beneficial and harmful effects that intellectual
property laws can have on innovation.

D474E28AA50641688F21AB71B3771808.description:
Demonstrate and debate how computing increases and
decreases connectivity and communication among people of various
cultures.

6839F325EAF84100ACBE208C1EF6952C.description:
Demonstrate ways a given algorithm can help solve
computational problems across disciplines.

AA6034E0ECE240029FB5BC504733F4B7.description:
Test and refine computational artifacts to ensure access to a
variety of user audiences.

E7A460EEC233495E91F68D4D77D31A99.description:
Evaluate the ways computing impacts personal, ethical, social,
economic, and cultural practices.

EF5B9D0412074FE2AC4716A2383343EE.description:
Additional standards and practices for this subconcept begin in High
School Level 2.

E5F27C48B01344D8876D11E7C1CC004D.description:
Evaluate and refine computational artifacts to make them
more user-friendly, efficient and/or accessible.

5A6D455C4AC049B79A2ECEFDF9EC0289.description:
Using visual aids and documentation, illustrate the design
elements and data flow (e.g., flowcharts, pseudocode) of the development
of a complex program.

2F28B2C6B29348D1BC515890FAD45191.description: While working in a team, develop, test, and refine eventbased programs that solve practical problems or allow self-expression.

FB99022D99A24E7EAE65F3C0289CA5F1.description:
Evaluate a variety of software licensing schemes (e.g., open
source, freeware, commercial) and discuss the advantages and
disadvantages of each scheme in software development.

728465D1FC844C8AABEE1CA5B434A90B.description:
Create software that will provide solutions to a variety of users
using a software development process.

F86CEFA221F442338A5165FCF3B7CF7C.description:
Additional standards and practices for this subconcept begin in High
School Level 2.

D1B648B566C445768E99DA980332A890.description:
Create computational artifacts by systematically organizing,
manipulating and/or processing data.

0B8D28F303AB457989E7466606026946.description:
Decompose problems into procedures using systematic
analysis and design.

BBEBF8CDEEE440D08B94616FD01EE86A.description:
Justify the selection of specific control structures (e.g.,
sequence, conditionals, repetition, procedures) considering program
efficiencies such as readability, performance, and memory usage.

D21A4BB04EAF401ABABAC283C2CDF7BC.description:
Demonstrate the use of lists (e.g., arrays) to simplify solutions,
generalizing computational problems instead of repeatedly using simple
variables.

3FE324BE3FEC4A8BBF25C6C1661F4AB7.description:
Additional standards and practices for this subconcept begin in High
School Level 2.

55568D04AB2D4BB8B48FBDFA90EBD2C0.description:
Create a prototype that uses algorithms (e. g., searching,
sorting, finding shortest distance) to provide a possible solution for a realworld problem.

9874CB7155A749E38D249EE6B957CF6A.description:

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards SOCIAL STUDIES

B427521C263540AEA3F4B9D23450CA44.description: Describe reasons why people and nations trade, providing examples of major imports and exports produced and consumed by Americans.

2EE1AF24DDE34C0A8D38F5284F3AE983.description: Identify the major economic activities in which people of each region work to satisfy their needs and wants (e.g., commercial agriculture, manufacturing, energy production, construction, and services such as healthcare and technology).

7CB60757581A450FB88ABEC15811D57B.description: Describe how production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services are economic decisions made by producers and consumers to satisfy their needs and wants.

70D6DDB50F384CF78DB5396DB6E0FB14.description: Describe the features and advantages of a market economy.

11B02187AB78407EA3DD16AAC2556803.description: The student will examine the American economic system and its economic activities which support human development.

D409111D4A904B0EBD91C7581ACD0C3A.description: Explain interactions between American Indians, Spanish explorations, French fur traders, Catholic missionaries, and early European settlers, comparing different perspectives toward land ownership and use of resources.

810BE6C84D7D46138CBD60523CFDB00E.description: Trace and describe the impact of significant European expeditions (e.g., England: Henry Hudson; France: Jacques Cartier; Portugal: Vasco da Gama; Spain: Christopher Columbus, Hernando de Soto, Ferdinand Magellan, Ponce de Leon).

8A481AA7F66844588804D5238C8068A6.description: Explain how Spain, France, and England were motivated to explore the continent by a desire to expand their wealth and culture, forcibly convert Native peoples to Christianity, acquire natural resources, and develop trade relations.

08D7139EAE4C4655B4772EF444096081.description: Summarize the goals and consequences of European expeditions of North America.

114FDFB94C6B477FB17C49D958BA72DF.description: Analyze how fulfilling one’s civic responsibilities (e.g., jury and military service, paying taxes) is necessary for the functioning and continuity of the representative democracy.

6D55240A4C3D4F2DA1C4CF1B8090B3F0.description: The student will examine and compare the Jamestown and Plymouth settlements as the foundations of American culture and society.

7369FD9FD67B4ADA8B62E438978201C6.description: Create presentations or products which summarize research findings from two or more sources.

8A60170DD1284632ABBD33E229DD9531.description: Organize information from research, quoting accurately from the source and avoiding plagiarism.

236849E3CA664D6898E8DC0978124219.description: Formulate a viable research question related to expanding knowledge of social studies concepts.

B678AF3516F14EDAB2492F4E1B580C2E.description: Engage in authentic research to acquire, refine, and share knowledge through written presentations and products.

F4F4457FDBF9485F92EE400CE6601945.description: Clearly state an opinion through written products, supported by examples, details, and reasoning.

DCEE14DE756046B0900CE812B3FEB472.description: Compose informative written products by introducing and developing a topic, supported by evidence (e.g. facts, examples, details) and maintaining an organized structure.

E3BF70281B0141199FE2ACAB42864510.description: Summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create written products, research projects, and presentations for multiple purposes related to social studies content.

F98E0B0B7F144D93B9A445D20105B2BF.description: The student will develop a variety of evidence-based written products designed for multiple purposes.

9A4E05B2BBDC4FCEBCA2C965DB235C68.description: Engage in collaborative discussions about appropriate topics and texts, expressing ideas clearly to others in group and whole class settings.

6ABBBC878BB146C2A3CD89AA0A06AB62.description: Distinguish fact from opinion in nonfiction text and investigate facts for accuracy.

2F9C4EE1C86E496ABE8EA4605947CC76.description: Determine an author’s purpose and draw conclusions to evaluate how well the author’s purpose was achieved.

705D4800DA8F4CF48A71CCF511E0619B.description: Apply critical reading and thinking skills to interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts and perspectives.

46B8B6BDB7F7402C9850443AAC82A3D6.description: Use information from multiple print or digital sources (e.g., timelines, maps, graphs, political cartoons, images, artwork) to answer a question.

546B030205C74A379FF396379B1BB97C.description: Use information accurately from a text when explaining the text explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

1039B84A802E4059BDD701ECBCEFBF1A.description: Comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize textual sources to acquire and refine knowledge in the social studies.

1C240ABD9AF84D54AE4C9A29682E0DE6.description: The student will engage in critical, active reading of primary and secondary sources related to social studies concepts.

6F2D33D1B24E47C1B77345AC943CF000.description: Analyze the importance of innovation and entrepreneurship in a market economy.

41DEFC635BCC40DDBD05D0F424F56119.description: Explain how the concept of supply and demand operates in a market economy, using historical and contemporary examples.

23335264A1FF47608FB43D24C5A3E754.description: Interpret and draw conclusions from economic data on charts and graphs.

134112408C4E4368B4C763B5535D31DE.description: Identify the principles of economic systems and develop an understanding of the benefits of a market system in local, national, and global settings.

F4FCCC38B43143AAB95B0F4DD70F5638.description: Explain how environmental factors affected historical events and continue to impact contemporary human activities.

AD11C45F0A9B44F08A647F442584CC83.description: Analyze human and physical features of the nation by drawing conclusions and explaining spatial relationships of physical and human places from geographic representations.

41BE259176DD4C1EB6DA4D61B20C6787.description: Answer geographic questions by organizing geographic information from historical as well as contemporary perspectives.

12BB93309332472FB6B3B8A2820960EC.description: Demonstrate a mastery of geographic concepts and the use of geographic tools to understand the impact of geography on the past and present.

F8CDBF2159BB46F1B20F29EFA89AB1A6.description: Explain multiple causes and effects of events and developments of the past or present; create timelines to identify multiple causes and effects from given information.

353B504F9A0B4112B640596B1E6D0BE7.description: Compare perspectives of individuals and groups from different regions and experiences, including the past and present.

977D44394BDB4E418C69F7F8468F819B.description: Compare and analyze primary and secondary sources from the past and present, including the intended audience and author’s purpose.

8592B59F26F94C94AC16011728795990.description: Develop skills which demonstrate an understanding of historical events and the people who shaped our history.

34B684F84EC4401DBF00E68BE72E4144.description: Examine the principles of the Constitution of the United States, including how laws are made in a democratic society and are used to protect individual rights.

8E8853C3981E44F4BB029FCBF4F8A60D.description: Explain the structure, responsibilities, and powers exercised by officials of the national government and describe ways informed citizens can and should participate.

F0E7B33B216A4041ACA748E11498D464.description: Explain democratic principles in historic documents by identifying examples of civic virtues and principles at work in state and national settings.

8F7EA5285BC84E01B854395B176305CF.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of government, the benefits of democratic systems, and their responsibilities as citizens.

B5976B9F866147C6A5C0632A1BBA855E.description: The student will use interdisciplinary tools to acquire, apply, and evaluate content understanding of the four strands of social studies.

201A922E250944809794F2B7E1600722.description: Reinforce understanding of social studies content through collaborative inquiries and the completion of authentic tasks and assessments.

E2FF6B852C344B28B4D1C427F6096AA7.description: Demonstrate critical thinking skills by frequently developing and answering various depth of knowledge questions.

4C9F81AB91014E9DA90932ABF2AF4B75.description: Compare points of agreement from reliable information used to answer supporting questions related to social studies content.

2BDCB64246E54C26AE29E5D363634EDB.description: Ask and examine essential questions that are important to others, as well as enduring across social studies topics.

AB519D201D024C9F826B4BA774C6DEB9.description: Develop practices which demonstrate an understanding that social studies involves the evaluation of evidence.

B7EBDA99844D40AFBC023B87A9E414F6.description: Explain challenges of the past and present and describe strategies used to address local, regional, or national problems.

0884F4DD24A9476BBCD4032A964ACFE8.description: Use a range of democratic procedures to discuss and make decisions about real-world problems in the community, region, and nation.

15811AB13D164ECD8FD964E5C1C98789.description: Explain how human experiences can shape a person’s point of view about civic issues.

10954A29263B4716B1CA54D62D919E77.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the virtue of civil discourse to analyze and address real- world problems.

95B5FA859D614F3CB012C139086DA647.description: The student will apply critical thinking skills to address authentic civic issues.

61CA873490A4495E9690F88F29299FED.description: Explain reasons for conflict between regions of the Western Hemisphere, such as territorial disputes, access to natural resources, and ethnic differences (e.g., boundary and mineral claims of the Arctic, Indigenous sovereignty over oil and gas reserves in Bolivia, immigration across the United States-Mexico border).

514BBA24B8154E4B8C571798E3E2E05F.description: Examine how supranational organizations (e.g., Organization of American States, Arctic Council) create cooperative political, economic, defense, and cultural regions.

53465D48C83A44AC995C340D90FC06C8.description: Describe how the people of different regions cooperate to address common concerns and how such cooperation impacts global interdependence (e.g., the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, Mercosur).

F7B0BA1E166D483089F4EFE36F6FD571.description: Explain reasons for cooperation among nations of the Western Hemisphere.

4BF17559BA884C4C8212AD7DE5B35E2F.description: Explain economic interdependence as it relates to the outsourcing of jobs to developing regions.

F1D099DE85FE41E1903DF75C44E5B770.description: Define basic concepts related to trade, including exports and imports, tariffs, free trade, and balance of trade.

F8A37F2C511540858EA73B1D8FECEE21.description: Describe patterns of economic interdependence and trade linking regions of the Western Hemisphere.

EF4FC305F1E84A738CB6B6359D50C0CD.description: Identify examples of man-made regions sharing common characteristics related to culture, human settlement, history, economic activities, and governments (e.g., Latin America, corn belt, Northeast megalopolis, Silicon Valley, British Commonwealth, barrio, suburb).

D8BB505CDD9D4539832F6CE9C5E0B045.description: Identify examples of physical (natural) regions sharing common features of landforms, climate, vegetation, and natural resources (e.g., Great Plains, New England, Amazonia, Canadian Shield, Altiplano, sun belt, tornado alley).

0E5184012D8348E081FB62C1DE95B1D8.description: Define the concept of region as an area sharing common characteristics and explain how regions can be categorized in many ways, such as political, physical, cultural, and economic.

1F4D4B233D3B419C9250037310BC9F34.description: The student will analyze the common characteristics of regions which create a sense of identity and unity, influencing the interactions among people and nations of the Western Hemisphere.

EE97EFD9440F47018A3AD9A4EC949392.description: Identify and compare the characteristics of developed and developing countries by analyzing data (e.g., literacy rate, life expectancy, per capita income, and infant mortality) used by geographers to measure development.

577A4D1CF0EE4DFD84E2EC0E4130F0E4.description: Quaternary Sector: Research and intellectual services such as technological advancement and innovation (e.g., Silicon Valley and Sao Paulo’s technology centers, Massachusetts Institute of Technology).

92F01F0DE3B343BEBE29D812205FFDFF.description: Tertiary Sector: Businesses that provide services to consumers (e.g., ecotourism of Costa Rica, New York Stock Exchange, Houston’s MD Anderson Cancer Center)

DB1BFABBE54B41679B1EA9D9599DA1A6.description: Secondary Sector: Production of goods through manufacturing and construction (e.g., United States steel industry, Argentina’s meat-processing, Mexico’s automotive exports)

86983ADC2C924E9CA8BF5F51E20A5347.description: Primary Sector: Extraction and harvesting of natural products (e.g., Venezuela’s Orinoco Belt, Chile’s artisanal fishing, logging of Canada’s boreal forests)

C7632F2A5872412F8BD1BA37CB0D1761.description: Explain how different sectors of a nation’s economy contribute to the development of a nation.

8BA758F19FA544D48FCCD358110395D4.description: Compare the outcomes of different economic systems for human prosperity, equality, and freedom.

C6123F0BDDBE472A88ACB12E72555B81.description: Describe how government policies affect economic activities within a nation, as well as determine trade relationships.

08BB324C6EA648DB96E5D78E1CE9982A.description: Define the characteristics of traditional, market, and command economic systems.

8B1489C88F654B89B407AC84234B9957.description: Analyze the benefits and limitations of various economic systems.

A3DDD70FC0F24AB393E61180AD9E0E46.description: Explain how people organize economic systems to address basic economic questions regarding which goods and services will be produced, how they will be distributed, and who will consume them.

37948EF339014D1E9C9FE67FAA5D1673.description: Analyze economic systems of the world and how they impact the development of a nation and region.

7BF1B7F2FEFB4D7CA89860B4F1C44A92.description: Compare common features of the Constitution of the United States to other representative governments of the Western Hemisphere, focusing on the principles of limited government, individual rights and liberties, and the role of the citizen in the selection of government officials.

585C8949CCA748319502E8FEEF2895D2.description: Describe challenges for several Latin American governments and economies, due to a history of political and economic instability.

6B2EA9BEDCF54882A0DABBB65218FC57.description: Describe how historic struggles for independence in Latin America and the Caribbean were influenced by the American revolution and Constitution, leading to the creation of modern republics.

E4C4FE76576740FDB397C66AC8FF8711.description: Explain the concept of sovereignty with regards to American Indian Tribal governments, as well as other Indigenous people of the Western Hemisphere, and examine issues related to rights of self- determination over lands and resources.

22BC0E23D6424BDD9E5522F889E04CBC.description: Differentiate between a representative democracy and a constitutional monarchy/parliamentary democracy by comparing the governments of the United States and Canada.

676D91AD77AE4B20925ACEC7B6C9F916.description: Define and describe the characteristics of limited governments (democracy, republic, constitutional monarchy) and authoritarian systems (dictatorship, oligarchy, absolute monarchy).

793708A9ED234D6D92146CB9578A6830.description: Analyze why and how humans develop rules, laws, and governments, including the role of citizens in government.

212D3E97E6F846829CFA45E5BE90D8BF.description: Describe the role of citizens as responsible stewards of natural resources and the environment (e.g., recycling campaigns, water conservation, national parks, protection of wildlife preserves).

B31EF16515134724984D85FC70529426.description: Evaluate the need to preserve resources, climate, and wildlife by creating public awareness, including the efforts of eco-tourism.

EB37D7AE6D1B490BAB020CF1FF106DBD.description: Identify environmental challenges (e.g., air pollution, acid rain, deforestation) and explain how they can impact a region (e.g., oil spills in the Gulf of America, ranching and logging operations in Amazonia, urban sprawl of Mexico City).

FA11A169F39440368C855F1727059EB6.description: Describe how humans modify the natural environment to support human development, such as subsistence and commercial agriculture, extraction of fossil fuels and minerals, development of industry, and urbanization.

491B148C84AF49479BD3856F947975F7.description: Analyze the impact of natural disasters on human populations, including displacement, scarcity of consumer goods, economic activities, and loss of life.

7F4F3F163D64490C943A13777AEC7D26.description: Explain how humans adapt to the environment (e.g., types and location of housing, clothing and food choices, methods of transportation, and options for economic activities) using historic or contemporary examples.

7BDC520DC0524EE3A2ECEE3438713E9D.description: The student will analyze the interactions of humans and their environment in the Western Hemisphere.

9342E340B19A4676AF6DD3E02C625DEA.description: Explain the effects of plantation agriculture and the importation of enslaved labor on the economic development and cultural heritage of regions (e.g., Brazil and the Caribbean).

9372E11975524FE79E7BE598974075EF.description: Identify the distribution of enslaved persons between different areas of the Western Hemisphere and explain how overseas expansion and commerce led to the development of the trans-Atlantic slave trade.

1CB80E448D554FBB96869896EED2E14D.description: Examine Spanish colonialism of Latin America and its influence on language, religion, and customs, including the practices of privateering and mercantilism.

0455211A684A44B7BF15A2AED7EAF06B.description: Describe the impact of English and French settlement of North America on cultural characteristics such as language, customs, and principles of self-government.

64BF6ADC16104C36993F949839913F49.description: Identify examples of cultural diffusion (e.g., Columbian Exchange: availability of new commodities and technology; assimilation of Indigenous peoples into colonial societies).

CB1FB4990B954D14807B791682B2A601.description: Describe the cultural interactions between Indigenous cultures and European settlers which impacted the heritage and history of major regions of the Western Hemisphere.

F1B30BEBA4D643E3857798FAB6C3FE76.description: Explain how the Inca were able to control an expansive empire in the Andes, developing a strong central government and innovations in agriculture.

1D1AC8106351411B96597A75069BC4C1.description: Describe how the Aztec conquest of other Indigenous peoples created extensive trade networks and wealth.

1F3F2051B5CC49B2AFD8966CD4E1EBFE.description: Explain how the Olmec and Maya adapted to and modified their environment to develop advanced civilizations in Mesoamerica, featuring advancements in science, architecture, the development of a writing system, and regional trade.

89CFF6EC2E984D7AAF2E6D8E28532FD3.description: Explain that various complex societies, economic, and political systems developed on the North and South American continents, each known for unique achievements and contributions prior to the arrival of Europeans.

929E1A85FE434D3BB629A138E94D15DE.description: Describe the ethnic heritage of Indigenous cultures of the Western Hemisphere.

DF01ABF574DB4E21B915F63D799B48A2.description: Identify and provide examples of pull factors of migration (e.g., economic opportunity, religious freedom, family ties, education).

BD1DE2ADEB08410E884E4E0B2AB234D0.description: Define push factors of migration (e.g., instability, conflict, natural disasters) using historic or contemporary examples (e.g., European colonization, asylum seekers from political unrest or religious persecution, and examples from different waves of migration in American history).

656933B8F5374F8CA2D4FF85B94E4577.description: Examine the impact of geography on migration and population distribution.

25600AF5DCD94D6E878EC5C1E3CE5441.description: Define cultural diffusion and describe how cultural characteristics spread and impact contemporary regions (e.g., entertainment, fast foods, social media’s rapid spread of ideas, wide use of the smartphone).

108348F177FB4FF9972B4DC71B8815C0.description: Compare major cultural groups of the Western Hemisphere (e.g., American Indian, Indigenous peoples of Canada and Amazonia, French-speaking Canadians, Hispanic Latin America, Caribbean citizens of African descent).

B2D0D6DFF7F1438DBE3AC5C638150D40.description: Explain how culture provides individuals with a sense of identity and how it is transferred from one generation to the next.

50619E1DE615420985D5D867A64F1896.description: Identify and describe cultural traits (e.g., language, ethnic heritage, religion, traditions, the arts) which are unique to a people and region.

F931E91363B6449EA0632336ED2EBA49.description: Analyze how the characteristics of culture impact people and places.

8F5D78E3658649388A5719FE72C0C9C6.description: Identify on a political map the major countries and population centers of each region, describing urban, rural, suburban, and metropolitan settlement patterns.

06A6FE40554A4C958F445DF859E3E812.description: The student will identify the characteristics, distribution, and demographic patterns of human populations and systems of the Western Hemisphere.

3B4032B08098475F9D7A4107030C1766.description: Describe the distribution of natural resources found in each region, delineating between renewable and nonrenewable resources, and explaining how the relative location to such resources can influence the economic development of a region.

B13739399B1E43D3B263F0378573E75A.description: Explain how the factors of latitude, elevation, and proximity to bodies of water influence climate and human activities.

398411FBD01B4EDCA6943E4072842144.description: Use visual information to describe on a physical map the major climate and vegetation zones, drawing conclusions about their impact on human development.

192BC95FD22C4A7B9615B7B90FC5E25D.description: Identify and describe on a physical map the major landforms and bodies of water important to each region of the Western Hemisphere.

DAC1046DFC3A432DB4613488808F044D.description: The student will analyze the physical systems of the major regions of the Western Hemisphere.

5E7EEDBB65A64B87B3AC9E58DC1E7307.description: Describe and analyze the role of geographic factors on events which impact the people and places of the Western Hemisphere, using both primary and secondary sources.

087152B360B849EF9DB83E03182D79E3.description: Compare characteristics of major regions of the Western Hemisphere through the regular use of strategies, such as the Five Themes of Geography (location, place, human-environment- interaction, movement, regions) which utilize critical thinking about geographic concepts.

099BE1E2F8324AA9B1B7990B1A04BA6D.description: Use different types of maps, graphs, charts, and geographic tools, such as satellite imagery and Geographic Information System (GIS) technology, in order to draw conclusions and make predictions from geographic data.

1A44CD7F3A504AB5ACB3EE460EB16B9E.description: Use the system of latitude and longitude to identify the absolute location of a place on maps and globes, explaining how various map projections distort the surface of the Earth.

0274C60669E5401987E138D7FB631921.description: Apply the concepts of scale, distance, and direction to explain the relative location of physical and human places.

D7EA51BDD5CB47B0AC1D4248EB0BB5BD.description: Integrate visual information to organize understandings about the people and environments of the Western Hemisphere.

55E5D30A7B0A43C5AEFA05DDAC615FD8.description: Explain geography as a field of inquiry which answers “the why of where” by examining both physical and human geography using spatial thinking skills.

D37293F80DBB4B4597422678A98D9B66.description: The student will analyze data from a geographic perspective using the skills and tools of geography.

673FF9CAAAA84920BDA8483A32DC8D6E.description: Organize and create presentations or products using research from a variety of formats and encompassing different points of view.

64132FE48E8340BEAB0DE0C0AF278D35.description: Quote, paraphrase, and summarize findings, avoiding plagiarism.

D7BA278D9AF3463FABE8EA75C10D71CF.description: Refine and formulate viable research questions related to social studies investigations, using well- developed theses or claims.

5EE0028CC4E944F2B747C8A99D07E068.description: Engage in authentic research to acquire, refine, and share knowledge through written presentations and products.

5C21362C6FD14761AAD8083968AD1F33.description: Compose argumentative written products by introducing a claim, recognizing an opposing viewpoint, and organizing evidence and reasoning from credible sources.

85EFACA88B4F43C4935614AC35BE3134.description: Compose informative essays and other written products using and citing evidence (e.g. facts, examples, details) from multiple sources and maintaining an organized structure.

B8986A04C40F4876AC21EBF78CDD76E8.description: Summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create written products, research projects, and presentations for multiple purposes related to social studies content.

1E844F0A5D4346C2B08BAC90255E4920.description: The student will develop a variety of evidence-based written products designed for multiple purposes.

512DA6BAD6CA4D70818A931E271B6605.description: Engage in collaborative discussions about information presented in social studies texts, expressing ideas clearly while building on the ideas of others.

40EE82ED3738417E97DF00BC462210F3.description: Evaluate textual evidence to determine whether a claim is substantiated.

A0F818ED3B844070845E0DE1F1C97FB7.description: Analyze works written on the same topic and compare methods the authors use to achieve similar or different purposes.

ECED0C9D0E074094870C42F17DE79373.description: Apply critical reading and thinking skills to interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts and perspectives.

8E86A4721E8C48469784C171D01F9CF6.description: Integrate the use of visual information (e.g., maps, charts, photographs, videos, political cartoons, artwork) with textual information from primary and secondary sources to draw conclusions.

98334F2542B347FB82D8A3DBC916AFF7.description: Paraphrase the main idea and cite evidence from primary and secondary sources; provide an accurate summary of a source distinct from prior knowledge or opinion.

147EA914B68B4BBAAFDFCE889B7DDFC4.description: Comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize textual sources to acquire and refine knowledge in the social studies.

DF8DB84F8BB14A7DA7F24E535F334559.description: The student will engage in critical, active reading of primary and secondary sources related to social studies concepts.

C478FF2ABF6E4562BF02A47E291245E1.description: Explain how technology and trade impact standard of living and economic interdependence, using historical or contemporary examples.

DBA5C10C0C26440DAD34F7BDDAC9BFC7.description: Identify different types of economic systems, comparing advantages and disadvantages for citizens and the growth of a nation’s economy.

A9CBBC18F4734550AC21A69D2023614C.description: Analyze, interpret, and compare economic data from multiple charts and graphs.

9F590690F0F04174A827CB3D98AC63B1.description: Identify the principles of economic systems and develop an understanding of the benefits of a market system in local, national, and global settings.

DACB3FBAAB3946529A848BA94BB26B25.description: Explain how the environment affects cultural patterns and historical events, providing opportunities and challenges for human development.

4BC31332FB2C4DF39300D66A68785D9D.description: Use multiple mapping techniques, data visuals, satellite images, and geographic technology to analyze spatial patterns of physical and human characteristics, making connections between regions.

3EE8BE45189D445EB831697A897C3844.description: Answer geographic questions and conduct investigations by acquiring, organizing, and interpreting information about the modern world and historical events.

35BA0E2FE98844CAB88D06DB34553D4E.description: Demonstrate a mastery of geographic concepts and the use of geographic tools to understand the impact of geography on the past and present.

2D6ED35C21E840F5A545C7F639417383.description: Distinguish multiple causation, including immediate versus long-term cause-effect relationships; construct timelines of related events.

B5B1BF685A5041D08C0E3D7F33F1BBDC.description: Describe multiple factors and explain how they can influence the perspectives of individuals and groups on events from history and the modern era.

B371632CF98C4D0599FE1D5627535B5E.description: Gather and draw conclusions from sources of evidence, identifying plausible author, occasion, audience, purpose, and possible bias.

AC4A88CBAF884E399C3257660F31BA45.description: Develop skills which demonstrate an understanding of historical events and the people who shaped our history.

53A466736F9C4A20AE3F534C3A69D061.description: Examine the impact of constitutions, laws, treaties, and international agreements on the limits of government, including the concepts of sovereignty and the rule of law.

C290DBFFB8AE4984B8DEB84B114BD1FE.description: Compare the powers and responsibilities of the United States government to other forms of government, including the roles and rights of citizens.

030A629586F34CF397349C0C52E2A8D4.description: Compare and analyze civic virtues and democratic principles in historic and global settings, explaining how they influence political institutions.

B4627785238E43CE93715C5B3F46576B.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of government, the benefits of democratic systems, and their responsibilities as citizens.

7DDCA82B1F55426E99C2E471E7E8117D.description: Develop deeper critical thinking skills by questioning assumptions and identifying inconsistencies or errors in reasoning.

B12A0DB273EE4358AC3D3E72984C808F.description: Answer supporting questions related to social studies content knowledge and make connections to different interpretations.

1E58CD1185EB455BA8E55C2E3A852455.description: Investigate and propose answers to essential questions representing complex enduring issues across the social studies disciplines.

50B2EEB0816F43EBBEA77C152686A116.description: Apply a range of deliberative and democratic procedures to discuss, make decisions, and propose action about real-world problems in and out of school.

8DD88E05B8AB417EB976C5022A2FEAD3.description: Analyze why the acknowledgement of different perspectives can contribute to civil discourse and solutions to civic issues.
