1CA4BE950B1A4BC4B7B16FDE0E1222C2.description: The student will apply critical thinking skills to address authentic civic issues.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards SOCIAL STUDIES

5746524314D54DD383256C33EA604FAC.description: Analyze reasons for conflict and cooperation among regions, evaluating the advantages and disadvantages of international organizations and alliances (e.g., European Union, North Atlantic Treaty Organization, International Red Cross) as they relate to mutual defense, the resolution of disputes, and the response to humanitarian needs.

3B0C8DF791044F41B0F1FB784FD0523B.description: Describe how political, economic, and cultural forces (e.g., civil wars, terrorism, genocide, ethnic separatism) have challenged political arrangements (e.g., political status of Taiwan to China, the Shoah [Jewish Holocaust], the division of Sudan and South Sudan).

9CDBC405E791494A9A2AC3785F21DF53.description: Explain why countries enter into global trade agreements (e.g., Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries [OPEC], the Association of Southeast Asian Nations [ASEAN] and the African Continental Free Trade Area [AfCFTA]).

ECEF11631C12461EA2AEDCF7D8425A15.description: Examine indicators of economic interdependence and world trade, including why nations are concerned with the balance of trade, and explain major trade patterns among regions of the Eastern Hemisphere.

AE0B516CDAAB4F54A57B4DFBB3513F75.description: Explain patterns of global interdependence, including the impact of changing technology on trade routes, dependence on resources, use of low-cost labor, and the outsourcing of technological and manufacturing jobs to developing regions.

14EBFE0503344BF09B2F19D300CAF1CA.description: Explain and summarize how common physical or human characteristics can link as well as divide regions (e.g., manmade canals linking European trading centers, the Sahara Desert as both a physical and cultural division of the African continent, religious and political differences leading to armed conflict in Southwest Asia).

96B01BBC2FCA45D29055E3407AC70BA3.description: Define the concept of region and explain how regions change over time through physical and human processes, such as land use, urban growth, population, natural disasters, and trade.

792090DF4E3740A09BCCAD6A0025730D.description: The student will analyze the physical and human characteristics of regions which create uniqueness and influence people’s perceptions of the Eastern Hemisphere.

F91DCCB0DF194D1C875BBB0DA3479E12.description: Analyze the role of government to finance a nation’s development (e.g., infrastructure, enforcement of contracts, law and safety, social programs, and education).

6902183F72DA4D8585B88136505D73BD.description: Distinguish between developed and developing regions by analyzing data used by geographers (e.g., the Human Development Index data, literacy rate, life expectancy, infant mortality, per capita income).

36249D377FA44CD5933A6EF19CFCE672.description: Compare the economic measurements of productivity which inform nations of their economic health and growth (e.g., Gross Domestic Product and Gross National Product).

05FED49D224D4588BCFDB8F74E4258C0.description: Research and intellectual services such as technological advancement and innovation (Quaternary Sector).

2630B4173C6C4FE09D0B4F72D7D70A70.description: Businesses that provide services to consumers (Tertiary Sector)

5B45FC1193E043D9AB585BBC3F4C3CA3.description: Production of goods through manufacturing and construction (Secondary Sector)

29011B04E8F54AC8A7713E2E3068F5AF.description: Extraction and harvesting of natural products (Primary Sector)

77276DE9AECA4C72875C4E4A7A8CF196.description: Evaluate how the major sectors of economic activities contribute to the development of a country or region:

E10763763F0E4BF5B55FA94DFF1ECE4B.description: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of the traditional, market, and command economic systems, including how government policies affect economic activities and trade relationships among nations.

ABB253BD5C534366976B359CBE58E6AE.description: Explain how people organize economic systems to address basic economic questions regarding which goods and services will be produced, how they will be distributed, and who will consume them.

FF583D7685A948EFA3EB13ABDE959B7D.description: The student will examine and compare economic systems as means by which governments organize and distribute available resources, services, and goods.

803DAB3C7ED4421B9D5EBA8237A4E2C7.description: Analyze issues related to Indigenous sovereignty, including the management of natural resources and the preservation of Indigenous cultures (e.g., Scandinavia’s Saami, the Rohingya people of Myanmar, the Uyghur ethnic group of China, New Zealand’s Māori).

709910851DA44E94A03A0114948C08B1.description: Describe how contemporary authoritarian governments maintain power over citizens (e.g., denial of natural and civil rights, illegitimate elections, restrictions on free speech and the free exercise of religion, refusal of due process protections, corruption among government officials, unequal application of the law, and use of mob intimidation).

286E4382D4E447A6B3EC46CFDC184BDE.description: Compare civil liberties in representative to authoritarian systems of government, referencing the United States Bill of Rights.

3CD61C1BAAB847FE845046C4C260E858.description: Describe the involvement of citizens in the selection of government officials and the lawmaking process in different systems of government.

3C82EC4000A045088A20E50B4432EEEA.description: Compare the role of the citizen in modern representative governments to authoritarian systems (e.g., United Kingdom to Russia; India to Saudi Arabia; South Africa to China; United States to Iran).

AEBA250591C54E49913F256B2C55960D.description: Describe influences of early English tradition related to the principles of limited government and individual rights, such as found in the Magna Carta and established by the English Bill of Rights.

06EFC56EDDB549C68602CA7B8C8AA43A.description: Describe the government of the Roman Republic and its contribution to the development of representative self-government, including separation of powers, liberty, the rule of law, and the concept of civic duty.

F5E21B5E4A2343B6BDD0044E80BEEC11.description: Explain why the government of ancient Athens is considered the beginning of democratic government and examine Greek political concepts, including the “polis” or city-state, rule of law, liberty, civic participation and voting rights, legislative bodies, and written Constitutions.

253BEAAF535D4CFAA60783ECFEA953F4.description: Trace the historic roots of representative democracy.

676CAAEAB3974945BE9E55CB09474F45.description: Compare the source of authority and power of representative governments (republic, Constitutional monarchy) versus authoritarian systems (dictatorship, monarchy, totalitarian regime, oligarchy, theocracy) using contemporary or historical examples (e.g., the symbolic role of the British crown versus the authority of Saudi Arabia’s monarchy, the republics of western Europe to the Chinese Communist system).

5C3EE207387148D7B3511D7C834A0304.description: Analyze systems of government by examining their source of authority, principles, structures, and processes.

956A942F6462473AB44CAE56100B0A05.description: Explain the origins and central features of Islam, including its sacred text, basic beliefs (e.g., monotheism, Five Pillars) and describe its expansion and influence into Europe and North Africa.

A091785AF5284F5A9974C918AC7E4A74.description: Describe the origins and central features of Buddhism, including its basic beliefs (e.g., Four Noble Truths, Nirvana) and how its philosophy influenced other regions.

5C0DC20DB1624D46A7A007C8745A4AFA.description: Describe the origins and central features of Hinduism, including its basic beliefs (e.g., karma, reincarnation) and its influence on society of the Indian subcontinent.

67A5AB69473348159D6A5965AAAAC320.description: Explain the origins and central features of Christianity, by identifying its sacred texts and teachings, explaining its basic beliefs (e.g., monotheism, eternal life, Jesus of Nazareth as the messiah), its relationship to Judaism, and its impact on modern societies and contemporary culture.

DBD1501FF5BE49B3B83340E753288593.description: Describe the origins and central features of Judaism, identifying its sacred texts (e.g., the Torah, Ten Commandments) and explaining its central features and teachings (e.g., monotheism, emphasis on individual worth, personal responsibility, and adherence to moral obligations) and its impact on modern and contemporary Western societies and culture.

6FA8CC1D46094DBD8FE1ECB3C90C8424.description: Examine major religions of the world, including their belief systems and influence on contemporary societies.

4619C4AB4188465CB680EAC672D6CFA6.description: Explain that complex societies and civilizations in different regions share common characteristics (e.g., agricultural innovations, written language, and early systems of law and government).

340EC95D70614F0A931888C676912D0F.description: Examine how and why major cultural hearths developed along major river valleys and crossroads of trade (e.g., Mesopotamia's Fertile Crescent; the Nile, Indus, Huang He and Yangtze River Valleys; the kingdoms of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai).

9FF6EE04A20C4AFDA416D92AD40F2C97.description: Define and describe the legacy of the world’s major cultural hearths on a region’s ethnic heritage and history.

A7454D45EFC24D5D8BDB79A56E92442E.description: Compare cultural traits of major cultural regions and explain how culture can change over time through the process of cultural diffusion.

AB31FA394CB2451193466024F6411297.description: The student will evaluate the development and impact of culture on the major regions and peoples of the Eastern Hemisphere.

D681E1DD353A4A49AA5EA8C0EA24EF0F.description: Describe contemporary reasons and examples of migration (e.g., drought in agricultural eastern Africa resulting in urbanization, overpopulation of India’s cities due to employment options in high-tech industries).

C050F1B6FFA74B5C8FF4CD693F4F918D.description: Examine the role of pull factors (e.g., economic opportunity, education, family) and the role of push factors (e.g., political unrest, religious persecution, war, famine, natural disasters) which motivate both emigration and immigration, differentiating between involuntary and voluntary migration.

F6A9B651316442A28D77639ADB25DD0E.description: Describe the reasons for emigration and immigration.

8A87980CBB9B42D8A1F8A32DBBD55DAA.description: Examine how nations address population changes through government policies (e.g., education, health care, immigration).

DAB5BA4E148E422BB666288CDD8D64E1.description: Describe the challenges of urbanization and urban sprawl (e.g., access to public services, affordability of housing, gentrification, pollution, transportation).

147C08A385D54C8A9D50BAB2B2A0BDDE.description: Identify on a political map the major countries and population centers of each region, describing urban, rural, suburban, and metropolitan settlement patterns.

4D544D678F7E4F54953FF68A70D16B70.description: The student will identify the distribution and demographic patterns of human populations of the Eastern Hemisphere.

A877FE6EF7B740D1B1013E018CCEE36F.description: Describe the role of citizens as responsible stewards of natural resources and the environment, through sound resource use and conservation.

59EB90FE319448799482B77612DA2ABC.description: Examine how the development of technology meets energy demands, as well as modifies the environment (e.g., extraction of raw materials, offshore drilling, nuclear power plants, water diversion, hydroelectric power plants).

EDDA2D2861AB40B6AB1E63C2E7F31502.description: Describe the importance of transportation infrastructure and its direct impact on people's access to resources and consumer goods.

99A400C9960849C4A8BDFA7107D3FF7A.description: Explain why places become major hubs of industrial activity by analyzing the relationship between the location of natural resources to various manufacturing industries.

F70BC6BDA47343C1ADAE48FE0E9F8519.description: Evaluate the effects of human modification of the natural environment through processes related to industrialization.

E1609491728D49E794A5A20970389D90.description: Examine how agricultural practices in a region imprint the physical environment (e.g., desertification of the Aral Sea, terraced construction for rice farming, modern irrigation methods utilized in the Arabian Peninsula).

B4528CE50EE9441A8DD5BB6E5311663C.description: Explain how agricultural innovations, such as the Green Revolution and modern irrigation systems, increase food production in developing countries.

EAC686C8E9D0426D8837E71BA44CD794.description: Describe the differences among subsistence, cash crop, and commercial agriculture, including their impact on the economic development of a region.

F01EF45B978542C7851B177B346F6881.description: Describe how humans adapt to and modify their environment for the purpose of food production.

B2C81679801244F489BC971026A6ABB6.description: Analyze how humans adapt to their environment, including the impact of weather patterns and natural disasters on human populations, resulting in displacement, scarcity of consumer goods, and loss of life.

E1CE3DD8A9884B30B4AAFDD631DB19B6.description: The student will analyze the interactions of humans and their environment.

8A9DA8603BD84D23B84FF857BD005B4B.description: Identify examples of scarcity and how the availability of natural resources impacts regional economies, which can contribute to conflict and cooperation.

1822448CA38B4589A016135B2EBBF84F.description: Compare the characteristics and distribution of major renewable and nonrenewable resources of each region, identifying major nations in which natural resources (e.g., fossil fuels, minerals, agricultural crops) are the primary source of economic activities.

0A651E260C9344639E4433FBE99507A2.description: Describe how the physical environment can influence human population distribution, population growth, settlement patterns, land use, and economic activities.

72E4A1259E6044889E2FB982E87864A7.description: Identify on a physical map the major landforms and bodies of water of each region and compare climatic conditions, vegetation, and biomes using thematic maps and other geographic tools.

7CFBACCBEFB249E794BD9285B3D8B8F0.description: The student will analyze the physical systems of the major regions of the Eastern Hemisphere.

30BCC56BCB68479195DDB6CF678BE7F3.description: Reinforce geographic skills through the routine practice and use of geographic tools (e.g., thematic maps, graphs, charts, satellite imagery, GIS technologies) in order to draw conclusions and make predictions from geographic data.

B27193A83BBA41959DE875BA57AF4330.description: Describe the role of geographic factors on events, explaining the importance of spatial perspective and integrating specific geographic information to support analysis from primary and secondary sources.

6B80B1CFFAE04133AEF4B55C4588CE7A.description: The student will analyze data from a geographic perspective using the skills and tools of geography.

36146506BB6C473EAE27C982077492FF.description: Organize and create presentations or products using research from a variety of formats and encompassing different points of view.

871DF68307D94F24918EC21F386A02E2.description: Quote, paraphrase, and summarize findings, avoiding plagiarism.

B84C7D3C43C34EF0967C7E6EFA34A720.description: Refine and formulate viable research questions related to social studies investigations, using well- developed theses or claims.

54E06166C713450BA1C4ED36CE1F3287.description: Engage in authentic research to acquire, refine, and share knowledge through written presentations and products.

8864312E763C405F96F06F1F4B160595.description: Compose argumentative written products by introducing a claim, recognizing an opposing viewpoint, and organizing evidence and reasoning from credible sources.

00463E36BBA24DC3B1629ECD8F85F3EF.description: Compose informative essays and other written products using and citing evidence (e.g. facts, examples, details) from multiple sources and maintaining an organized structure.

9E43BED6D6CF4D95BBD362BACB2B4C00.description: Summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create written products, research projects, and presentations for multiple purposes related to social studies content.

E4D4B7BF72E84A5F96DA0C91F7B1AA70.description: The student will develop a variety of evidence-based written products designed for multiple purposes.

7234B0E4ED534EA2AC63097323E2777B.description: Engage in collaborative discussions about information presented in social studies texts, expressing ideas clearly while building on the ideas of others.

3F09B0327824439D85697E37596EF9C6.description: Evaluate textual evidence to determine whether a claim is substantiated.

FB07F6BC6D5C4C348DD00E9BE6B06ADE.description: Analyze works written on the same topic and compare methods the authors use to achieve similar or different purposes.

CFFCA6CF786748F89AFD62BF475DD2D4.description: Apply critical reading and thinking skills to interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts and perspectives.

03C15F1A8E5E4602BB291CF631299586.description: Integrate the use of visual information (e.g., maps, charts, photographs, videos, political cartoons, artwork) with textual information from primary and secondary sources to draw conclusions.

3B98BC39DC5A46038FA62394AB911243.description: Paraphrase the main idea and cite evidence from primary and secondary sources; provide an accurate summary of a source distinct from prior knowledge or opinion.

E81780B7E6C54CA991DD4520977363D7.description: Comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize textual sources to acquire and refine knowledge in the social studies.

19F91B0BF4EC4057B2346CC2199B1E8B.description: The student will engage in critical, active reading of primary and secondary sources related to social studies concepts.

15949F781E884A98956EE40FE0545111.description: Explain how technology and trade impact standard of living and economic interdependence, using historical or contemporary examples.

5275A4154D4C4B28B5D1B0D068F3B0EC.description: Identify different types of economic systems, comparing advantages and disadvantages for citizens and the growth of a nation’s economy.

8910EAC915E8418A9AA584712A4D26C6.description: Analyze, interpret, and compare economic data from multiple charts and graphs.

1E19D576D3D64C2186139C3FD2C4E890.description: Identify the principles of economic systems and develop an understanding of the benefits of a market system in local, national, and global settings.

0DF47B997B734B72945FB85D0B10ED8D.description: Explain how the environment affects cultural patterns and historical events, providing opportunities and challenges for human development.

6DCDD048376E4967A8CDFC7C8C3392F1.description: Use multiple mapping techniques, data visuals, satellite images, and geographic technology to analyze spatial patterns of physical and human characteristics, making connections between regions.

9373D9FA6FE94EA4A04F19F51BA1FC7F.description: Answer geographic questions and conduct investigations by acquiring, organizing, and interpreting information about the modern world and historical events.

01791029FD9840CEB7C8327804022A4C.description: Demonstrate a mastery of geographic concepts and the use of geographic tools to understand the impact of geography on the past and present.

A6F3C488D83746DB8F78F320EA62F926.description: Distinguish multiple causation, including immediate versus long-term cause-effect relationships; construct timelines of related events.

D8CCC749C5C746B48F2D1F91BC49D8C4.description: Describe multiple factors and explain how they can influence the perspectives of individuals and groups on events from history and the modern era.

D0C3A49AA9C24AC7A4B021C76637BEC5.description: Gather and draw conclusions from sources of evidence, identifying plausible author, occasion, audience, purpose, and possible bias.

76EC0BB201A340F8A16DBFB29086CB12.description: Develop skills which demonstrate an understanding of historical events and the people who shaped our history.

DD20BA98C1E14314B93D4712056309C9.description: Examine the impact of constitutions, laws, treaties, and international agreements on the limits of government, including the concepts of sovereignty and the rule of law.

33E364CACC484885A057EE3D0A45D541.description: Compare the powers and responsibilities of the United States government to other forms of government, including the roles and rights of citizens.

311DEA1D8916480A9DBA6A7D9363EB35.description: Compare and analyze civic virtues and democratic principles in historic and global settings, explaining how they influence political institutions.

A46EFF276C3A4728915FFA38DDF82334.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of government, the benefits of democratic systems, and their responsibilities as citizens.

13155E368504448AAC735D421D0C9F38.description: The student will use interdisciplinary tools to acquire, apply, and evaluate content understanding of the four strands of social studies.

864447687D9F48F0920AFA721E7B96E1.description: Demonstrate understanding of social studies content through the development of self-driven inquiries and the completion of authentic tasks and assessments.

D92AAE3D580E43E9B88631639790AE33.description: Develop deeper critical thinking skills by questioning assumptions and identifying inconsistencies or errors in reasoning.

379391CD3CE64608A3870E1DE369357E.description: Answer supporting questions related to social studies content knowledge and make connections to different interpretations.

AE88F3C26ED84C768F1B6DC1B62607C2.description: Investigate and propose answers to essential questions representing complex enduring issues across the social studies disciplines.

DAB50775347D478F8376A081CD99FAF9.description: Develop practices which demonstrate an understanding that social studies involves the evaluation of evidence.

6E873EA600DE4E8AA753894E6E213D12.description: Use information to analyze how a specific problem can manifest itself in regional and global issues, describing options for solutions.

36B1AB7B671E4629BD881C9E4C151534.description: Apply a range of deliberative and democratic procedures to discuss, make decisions, and propose action about real-world problems in and out of school.

58EF148AEDA2451A82C2BEA0CF59E97A.description: Analyze why the acknowledgement of different perspectives can contribute to civil discourse and solutions to civic issues.

AF1608083FEE44A599ED28F5065B88A9.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the virtue of civil discourse to analyze and address real- world problems.

7F1C570D5B5342089CD48F103A7516B7.description: The student will apply critical thinking skills to address authentic civic issues.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards SOCIAL STUDIES

50772480EB124EEFA559067E2883DABC.description: Describe escalating conflict between American Indians, military forces, and civilians (e.g., Whitman Mission and Sand Creek Massacres).

33E286ACCE064CD7BA4332C9C05D8363.description: Describe the impact of Grant’s policy of government-run boarding schools and missions directed to assimilate Tribal members.

6FC0BD74F3C94E79B6CF817E4D81E97D.description: Summarize the intent of President Grant’s Peace Policy on the displacement of American Indians from their homelands.

387046DA54E44381ACBC7D933E076E4A.description: Analyze the impact of the development of the Transcontinental Railroad on connecting agricultural goods and products to population centers and markets.

222F0FEC0E5E4BF0AAE2D5BB20D43EE5.description: Describe how the Homestead Act of 1862 enabled more individuals to obtain land and partake in economic opportunities following the war.

6DEC8FD95F274BB39EC0DEAC63021B18.description: Evaluate the impact of federal policies related to the on-going migration and settlement of the West.

BFA65561F8F846DCB71CE7344B90DCD4.description: Explain the effects of the presidential election of 1876 and the Compromise of 1877 on Reconstruction.

AE56BA7C73254272BBDBE622B17B776A.description: Examine the development of segregated societies in the South.

704D4C1F7A1E4A06B0928B3C300B2AD3.description: Describe the impact of the lack of enforcement of the 14th and 15th amendments.

306DF4DC35784B0E8A103B304556B0C9.description: Assess the factors leading to the end of Reconstruction.

7AC8632D4F234E2FB5815A1D4E301D16.description: Describe the migration of African Americans (Exodusters) from the oppressive conditions of the South to opportunities in the north and west.

1957531B3829474D8854AF0A6E9CD91C.description: Examine the political and social goals of the Ku Klux Klan, including its intimidation of African American voters.

2518BE96F60E4D4B8952344A69A10735.description: Describe the expansion of the tenant and sharecropper systems which enabled landowners to reestablish a labor force severely restricting economic mobility.

ADF054FC6E1F446AA81F00568BB67537.description: Identify the various motives of carpetbaggers including economic gain, exploitative aims, and genuine concern for the civil and political rights of freed Blacks.

F87D31E12799440DAC7EBB2026BD33BC.description: Analyze the emerging social structure of the post-war South.

621BD0E300D541309367CCE77001ED11.description: Describe how the adoption of Black Codes by many southern state legislatures restricted employment and property rights of Freedmen.

37FD10D9910A449699F9BDB3535CF79D.description: Evaluate the efforts of the Freedmen’s Bureau to assist freed persons with economic, educational, and political opportunities.

2F248E05DC0447128C39B03D7347C00A.description: Assess the impact of the Civil War Amendments in securing political rights for African Americans, resulting in their election to state and national government positions.

300A4CC93A674FE5A36B524F7DB83EEC.description: Explain the impact of the 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments on the status of formerly enslaved persons, as well as the relationship of the federal government to the states.

879488FEC5524042A08FB86B3171E9B4.description: Analyze the impact of state and federal legislation following the Civil War.

C56BB2AF5B6743D592CFFBA5119A4078.description: Compare the plans and policies proposed for Reconstruction (e.g., President Andrew Johnson, the Congressional Republicans) assessing their intended goals and possible outcomes.

D33D34F8EBC541719247BD8712AC278B.description: Evaluate Lincoln’s plans for reconciliation, as expressed in his Second Inaugural Address, and the impact of his assassination on Reconstruction.

F6A0D2062513470AAFA47C84F9A20818.description: Examine the challenges of rebuilding the nation following the end of the Civil War.

4029B3D0E1CA4C3CAC731E07DFDF3EA2.description: The student will analyze the political, social, and economic transformations during the Reconstruction Era.

D853F091319D46A1BAA0B9020C09101A.description: Describe Lee’s surrender at Appomattox Courthouse and the conditions of Grant’s surrender terms.

F0CD02223A6D46C8B5C77055460EE6BB.description: Explain how the Confederate loss of Vicksburg opened the way for the North to seize control of the Mississippi River, dividing the Confederate forces.

83B3896858EF447C8F9B05DE45C504B4.description: Describe how the Battle of Gettysburg ended the Confederate attempt to invade the North and analyze Lincoln’s Gettysburg Address which clarified the Union’s motivation for winning the war.

EBCFFF2BC81D4EAFBECC9BA5C6CA3B30.description: Analyze the Emancipation Proclamation’s role in expanding the goals of the war and its impact on slavery, including the significance of Juneteenth in relation to emancipation.

81265CAEE0CF48F1A33F2AFB075BE4F1.description: Explain how the Battle of Antietam proved that the Union could withstand the Confederate Army, providing Lincoln the confidence to issue the Emancipation Proclamation.

F7EA4E16D18E413493DE19201BA670CF.description: Summarize the significance of key battles and turning points of the Civil War.

5A5FB204FCF54820971B48D85D7FDE46.description: Examine the lasting impact of the Civil War, focusing on its devastation of property and the national economy, unrestricted use of weaponry, and the involvement of civilians.

9B504B30A7F84FEAB8C4FFFB9E315D91.description: Describe how the Southern military strategy focused on holding Confederate territory in hopes the North would eventually abandon the war effort.

BB54DF32E6734B03AA3B937B29BA8B75.description: Compare the goal of the Union’s Anaconda Plan to blockade and surround Confederate forces to the intent of Sherman’s total war strategy.

EFA8982EC491424D9E3A91867506BD15.description: Identify the key strategies used during the war and evaluate their effectiveness in determining the war’s outcome.

E76F486668C94337BC4CBD4A233278F5.description: Describe the value of immigrant troops used to fill Union ranks.

31ED49DE05ED489EB2B67A7BD8B3C078.description: Examine the contributions of free and enslaved persons, such as the 54th Massachusetts Regiment.

A86BBA03C2504C94A3D1FF2F1EA3D54C.description: Describe the significance of military leadership and experience (e.g., Robert E. Lee, Ulysses S. Grant).

CB06DB63153846D4B2D368D8756F552D.description: Compare natural resources, population, and industrialization.

0319FE19F3AC4E3E9B846D42E66843FE.description: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of the Union and the Confederacy.

3477C40DC32346C1AC7D56A511AB3070.description: Describe how the Confederate attack on Fort Sumter ignited armed civil conflict.

784A0B39460B49638CF35BC025638550.description: Trace the formation of the Confederate States of America under the leadership of Jefferson Davis.

7319F5FF68434859BF8A9EF0FAF3DE9C.description: Describe tensions over the strategic and internally divided border states.

668F26B5A23C458FAAD2881410BC049E.description: Explain slavery as the central factor for the secession of southern states by examining passages from state secession declarations.

217AE840F0274A8AA15D258C7DE586C0.description: Identify President Lincoln’s stance on slavery and intention of preserving the Union, as stated in his Cooper Union Address.

B12D939B744644A59F71761A93ECEDB6.description: Describe the emergence of the third-party system.

FB1B5535A0DB4CBBB8FB32D4A7098001.description: Analyze the immediate impact of the presidential election of 1860.

2FDA73CB3904460F80C8FEF5D3EEE864.description: The student will analyze the course and consequences of the Civil War.

0B12CC1C21A84C1B8394DD61706B5D01.description: Examine the motives for John Brown’s Raid on the federal arsenal at Harpers Ferry.

A282FB65788646A8A1842C51EDD6CC98.description: Evaluate the impact of the Dred Scott v. Sandford decision, which denied citizenship to African Americans and ruled enslaved persons as property.

05CCA27F359A471A8E20BF61AAF9D4C3.description: The student will evaluate the major political and economic events that transformed the land and its people from early contact through Indian Removal and its aftermath.

E502476A6DDB44B8B7C2E6C0B119C4C4.description: Compare cultural perspectives of American Indians and settlers regarding land ownership, social structures (e.g., matrilineal vs. patrilineal), religion, spirituality, and concepts of government.

5EA8628C578648BF8982D53E29D291EF.description: Compare the goals and significance of early European interactions with Native cultures, such as the benefits of trade, the impact of disease, the transformation of Native life brought about by the arrival of the horse, and new technologies.

FE20EB2BD2A74D799B74294FB17EA422.description: Examine the Caddo and Wichita cultures, active in the production and trading of goods using extensive transcontinental, intertribal trade routes prior to European contact.

D55F703908624133B4AA4B03CF894123.description: Describe the region as home to well-developed and complex pre-contact societies, such as the Spiro Mound Builders.

5F53118C93494BE7BC8260A085D31E82.description: Explain the significance of the Cooper Bison Kill Site as credible evidence of the early presence of prehistoric Native cultures.

0D42EB2ACB4E4CBC9B5D50C4D484B5D0.description: Describe the various physical features of Oklahoma and how the environment, ecological regions, and natural resources can affect human activity, comparing information on historical and contemporary thematic maps.

016DB5A2C3E94FC3931F550D10B4F1DE.description: The student will describe the state’s geography and the historic foundations laid by American Indian, European, and American cultures.

C73FD4A824C74205BA38EA9A354D1C31.description: Construct presentations or products for a designated audience, using research and reasoning to enhance understanding of a topic or issue.

E33FCFB00F8243F3B4DA1CE6C8F7D766.description: Integrate quotes and summaries of research findings into written products while avoiding plagiarism.

D0CCEA4FE66E4194825F07A0E33A9A1A.description: Develop self-generated theses or claims related to independent research and investigations using credible and relevant sources.

C6222C445C924C51A47678B1F2EA0113.description: Engage in authentic research to acquire, refine, and share knowledge through written presentations and products.

E3B70A3F236A49B289EC53A1BF02D06C.description: Compose argumentative written products, including a precise claim as distinguished from opposing claims, organizing logical reasoning, and providing credible evidence to develop an argument.

44AF3B71045B436CB653DEDC3760351F.description: Compose informative essays and written products, developing a thesis, citing and incorporating evidence from multiple sources and maintaining an organized, formal structure.

CA9F309945CB47A4908E7815B389995E.description: Summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create written products, research projects, and presentations for multiple purposes related to social studies content.

053F08B3D44342B8ADFC6C826B88B2DE.description: The student will develop a variety of evidence- based written products designed for multiple purposes.

B79D32C748C341DDA09FBF13E5988D86.description: Actively listen, evaluate, and analyze a speaker’s message, asking questions while engaged in collaborative discussions about social studies topics and texts.

CEB55EC70F764FD2A46450FC8731AC3D.description: Evaluate the author’s point of view, potential bias, and how authors can reach different conclusions regarding the same issue.

627574F4AC654C6F99791A3ECA7D9C6F.description: Evaluate the extent to which historical or cultural perspectives affect an author’s stated or implied purpose.

234CC25E2E2249FCA218FADB994CED6C.description: Apply critical reading and thinking skills to interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts and perspectives.

E35A8E58EEB84F20B750DFE35AA8B3B4.description: Analyze information from visual, oral, digital, and interactive texts (e.g., maps, charts, images, political cartoons, videos, artwork) in order to draw conclusions and defend arguments.

39E7A93EAF65411CB96CA969DDF71510.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, evaluating features such as author, date, and origin of information.

B3899BEF8498493F9EE1CE759930533B.description: Comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize textual sources to acquire and refine knowledge in the social studies.

AA8D21256AD44B9AAC3D42A1EC4868A5.description: The student will engage in critical, active reading of primary and secondary sources related to social studies concepts.

4CC7EA688C584A609748FBBA8FC94A56.description: Evaluate the impact, both intended and unintended, of government policies on market outcomes at national and global levels, past and present.

941088575A1A4DF8A9EC49AFDC2215C0.description: Construct arguments using a combination of evidence regarding solutions used by nations to address historical or contemporary economic issues.

944E79C7666A485BA733911820DADD80.description: Evaluate economic data from charts and graphs, noting trends and making predictions.

3AE73C8FD05A415FA1F81E9F82758C71.description: Identify the principles of economic systems and develop an understanding of the benefits of a market system in local, national, and global settings.

CCE1385B1D55491D96CA2BBDAF8C9D3F.description: Evaluate the extent to which political and economic decisions have had significant impact on human and physical environments of various places and regions.

5249744CDFCC473FB6B5E1FDCC4D1D8F.description: Compare and analyze complex maps and mapping technologies to analyze spatial patterns of human and physical environments, explaining relationships between the environment and events, past and present.

8E00924F1DA442CF929873F7C012E94E.description: Actively engage in asking and answering geographic questions by acquiring, organizing, and analyzing multiple sources of data and information about the world’s past and present.

0890B3544D7945EEA79A52F5CE4CFCE2.description: Demonstrate a mastery of geographic concepts and the use of geographic tools to understand the impact of geography on the past and present.

5031ED4801934428BE7CFCFF41D8DD70.description: Evaluate how multiple, complex events are shaped by unique circumstances of time and place; construct and interpret parallel timelines.

35A8BAC938A843B88407CCD02674225A.description: Analyze complex and interacting factors that influence multiple perspectives during different historical eras and contemporary events.

8581CC393E314B47AF6DDB0CAEE73571.description: Gather and evaluate the usefulness of various formats of evidence for specific inquiry, analyzing the broader historical context, and assessing potential bias and credibility of sources.

04E90ED10AC94ADB891169C45C29E586.description: Develop skills which demonstrate an understanding of historical events and the people who shaped our history.

2C97C8D37FAC4A06B79548FC1AD49089.description: Analyze the impact of constitutions, laws, treaties, and international agreements, by comparing how various governmental powers and responsibilities have changed over time.

5B8EA1699A8B4739956C25A42D500A05.description: Evaluate the impact of the structure and powers exercised by governmental systems on public policy, using historical and contemporary examples.

EEC45BAD9B50400696E386D7448AC48C.description: Evaluate various significant documents from the United States and other nations to compare civic virtues and principles of political systems.

7ED2AF123A2C4C07AF926351C25A66B9.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of government, the benefits of democratic systems, and their responsibilities as citizens.

58605213DE094D949D0987C7888F9DB0.description: The student will use interdisciplinary tools to acquire, apply, and evaluate content understanding of the four strands of social studies.

2F81C6624B1B4AB19A92CF594AAE8EF0.description: Demonstrate understanding of content through the development of self-driven inquiries and the completion of multi-staged, authentic tasks and assessments.

DCAF65A6811D420CAD1456E5B35C55ED.description: Reinforce critical thinking by evaluating and challenging ideas and assumptions, analyzing and explaining inconsistencies in reasoning.

7691627C633845388ED13446A466861C.description: Evaluate points of agreement and disagreement from reliable information and expert interpretations used to answer supporting questions related to content knowledge.

C06DF1BB412B4379B553D13B04E25028.description: Develop, investigate, and evaluate plausible answers to essential questions that reflect enduring understandings across time, real world circumstances, and social studies disciplines.

87F19D33464442809B52A8ED0162D88C.description: Develop practices which demonstrate an understanding that social studies involves the evaluation of evidence.

F6DA4DD524874430A1F111F6814CE37D.description: Gather and evaluate information regarding complex problems, assessing individual and collective actions taken to address them.

29F9992554A143E5A03CCBA76983B654.description: Engage in a range of deliberative and democratic processes to develop strategies to address authentic, real-world problems in community and out-of-school contexts.

603ADE4208D04CCCBCC5093487D144E1.description: Evaluate the impact of perspectives, civil discourse, and democratic principles on addressing civic issues.

5E15400A216F492CA5FB79849AF1BA74.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the virtue of civil discourse to analyze and address real- world problems.

B088CF17C9104F4DACF1BF0749C3ED91.description: The student will apply critical thinking skills to address authentic civic issues.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards SOCIAL STUDIES

CD773C45E4AD42FD8B560F89C4A95249.description: Describe recent contributions affecting significant changes in contemporary societies in the fields of literature and the arts, as well as in science and technology.

686E3C14468E49A1B913A3A275C4F6E6.description: Describe the challenges and impact of trade and economic interdependence on modern economies.

57E25345CA6A4C2CA2EC22617D85F46D.description: Identify conditions that have given rise to international terrorism and the risk of weapons of mass destruction, evaluating responses by governments and societies to such threats.

427340E41433494DB01948A8A30C49B0.description: Examine the religious, ethnic, and political origins and the lasting effects of ethnic conflict, modern genocide, and atrocities (e.g., Cambodia’s Khmer Rouge, Northern Ireland’s “Troubles”, Rwanda’s civil war, the Balkan’s ethnic cleansing).

BE02F35CF93543669070214C0E34FF28.description: Analyze recent threats to global security and regional stability.

8DC46B77ADAE47BB9EA6136D3DA91827.description: Describe the establishment of the European Union and the continued strength of national loyalties.

4F2042427EFE4B1B8B4FC347C2C0792D.description: Explain and describe the components of Western Europe’s postwar rise to modern prosperity (e.g., American-led free trade system, scientific, technological, and medical advances, welfare states, the economic recovery and development of Germany, and the mass rise in living standards).

3808CC4A30C44387A4017F967942BA56.description: Describe European politics since the fall of the Soviet Union, including Eastern Europe’s transitions, the expansion of the European Union and NATO, Brexit, and the re-emergence of Russia as an independent power.

2CC126896ECE45D0BBA0A0C0D0D4CD78.description: Assess the effect of anticommunist policies of President Reagan, Margaret Thatcher, and Pope John Paul II, as well as Western diplomacy initiated by individuals, such as Willy Brandt, and resistance movements led by individuals, such as Vaclav Havel and Lech Walesa.

D3E0AA1B635346E6820FE2BCD8FC4877.description: Explain how the policies of rapid political and economic restructuring under Mikhail Gorbachev, known as perestroika and glasnost, further contributed to the destabilization of the Soviet system and to the eventual breakup of the Soviet Union.

A53E48BD8CEE4C94ADE49FB99BE17D22.description: Explain the effect of the burdens of Soviet military commitments resulted in the collapse of the Soviet Union.

5D462FDDD7B741EDA2923ED27D1A531A.description: Examine the goals of Poland’s Solidarity Movement as a broad anti-authoritarian civil resistance which advanced the causes of workers' rights and social change.

ED56A0A30D1F48EB84FD6FB8D8EF2DD9.description: Analyze the effect of the collapse of the Soviet Union on global power dynamics, including the emergence of new democracies in Eastern Europe.

F6CCE1BFACB74C0F88792C670B8D9ACB.description: Evaluate the conditions leading to the end of the Cold War.

D8440A06928E4BD59FC1D1C62DFE37FA.description: Analyze the political, economic, and social context of South Africa’s apartheid system, assessing the role of international pressure and internal resistance in dismantling it, and describing the influence of Nelson Mandela and Desmond Tutu.

EC0D294C0F234BA98646BF9623CC728C.description: Describe the struggle for self-government in Ghana, including the influence of Kwame Nkrumah.

11A7A4BE9FDF4DAA89F44D8AC38E5D0F.description: Explain the effects of Pan-Africanism on changing political boundaries.

1FD0B4E51DA14AF8922C68260BBDA521.description: Assess the impact of African independence movements on human rights and self-government.

DF232A1CA8BD4138A23565A17F5913B6.description: Explain the significance of pro-democracy movements (e.g., student protest at Tiananmen Square) and economic reforms under Deng Xiaoping, including China’s economic and technological modernization, its growing involvement in world trade, rise in power status, and rivalry with the United States.

9C87D7C6AE3C4319BDD39C8B7C571118.description: Describe the effects of the Chinese Communist Revolution characterized by the repressive economic and social policies of Mao Tse-tung (e.g., Great Leap Forward and mass famine, Cultural Revolution and the terror of the Red Guards).

32EC9249014C4C9186B00AF3930C4229.description: Describe significant political and economic change in China, including the influence of Sun Yat-Sen and the 1911 nationalist revolution, and examine the consequences of the Chinese Civil War, which resulted in the establishment of a communist regime and the emergence of a free, prosperous, and democratic Taiwan.

B499C5F0F4F642B8843E2D79D8D19D50.description: Explain how civil conflicts in Korea and French Indochina became proxy wars between superpowers over the spread of communism.

FB93F32F4E194736888EC7684C96284C.description: Analyze political and cultural transformations occurring in East and Southeast Asia during the postwar era.

6D7F471FD9C240799DF1C92DD5857277.description: Describe the partitioning of India and subsequent international relations (e.g., Indo-Pakistani wars, the Non-Aligned Movement, India’s secular constitution, experiences with socialism, and free-market reforms).

576F70501D9042BE9383E9D08F3DA822.description: Describe the fall of the British Raj and the emergence of an independent India and Pakistan, including the influence and ideas of Mohandas Gandhi.

E18D56139003481D9102204889340AF4.description: Assess the impact of independence movements on self-government in South Asia.

780E64F1968742A4A30FAD5241D9F6AD.description: Examine the roots of the ongoing regional instability of the Middle East, including the rise of Islamic fundamentalism, the Iranian Revolution and its establishment of a theocracy, the Iran-Iraq conflict, and the invasion of Kuwait.

BB5C317CC35E4236B8607646FAB3C1E0.description: Explain how the attack by Arab states on Israel in 1948 unfolded and how the United Nations’ partitioning of the Palestine Mandate created refugees and contributed to ongoing growing tensions (e.g., Six Day War, Yom Kippur War).

6577B4908A0846D29C510F54D2AE1B86.description: Describe the creation of the modern State of Israel, including the rationale for its establishment, the Zionist movement, and increased migration of European Jews to the British Mandate for Palestine.

9B8C5FA2628D477B8AF3343823F3F281.description: Evaluate ongoing regional disputes of the Middle East.

2DC28EB467034306820A631CB23C3298.description: Compare military power shifts caused by the war and a proliferation of nuclear armaments, describing the impact of transnational organizations and alliances (e.g., United Nations, North Atlantic Treaty Organization, Warsaw Pact) and explaining the goals of the non-alignment movement.

1B8B5BF41E6144A8B92145C20568B0D5.description: Explain how tensions escalated, fueled by the Berlin Blockade, Suez Canal Crisis, and subsequent uprisings by people in Soviet-dominated satellites (e.g., Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia).

0A7A59803016432ABD50C9DB19A39AA0.description: Compare the ideological, political, and economic distinctions between the United States and Western bloc versus the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) and the Eastern bloc, leading to the division of Europe, separation by an Iron Curtain, and adoption of a policy of containment.

BD886C4510674180A81F7CC9DE8DD1F2.description: Explain the major consequences of World War II, including physical and economic destruction, the loss of life, including millions of civilians, the mass expulsion of ethnic minorities, and the devolution of colonial empires.

E1CB90317FA34226A0DD82415D7F1854.description: Evaluate the effects of World War II including the origins and escalation of the Cold War.

28AD87C6EF614D929E75E261B461AE5A.description: The student will evaluate post-World War II regional events leading to the transformations of the modern world.

F50FCE9E6106428880889E4F001BE9EC.description: Describe efforts to avoid the abuse of human rights by examining the intent of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the expansion of the Geneva Conventions.

352571212FE949E693BE967FA0793109.description: Summarize world responses to the Holocaust, including Christian opposition, the Nuremberg Trials, and the move to establish a Jewish homeland.

CB0472BF4F15420B830D63055E601ECA.description: Examine the effects of the Shoah (Jewish Holocaust) through eyewitnesses such as inmates, survivors, liberators, and perpetrators.

9C8864A494AD490DB5AF74A7F67F5394.description: Describe the National Socialist Party’s (Nazi) seizure of unchecked power, its dehumanization of the Jews and the mass genocide of other victims (e.g., physically disabled, the Roma, homosexuals).

A53EBC9EE96246A585CD5DDF050458B3.description: Trace the roots and long tradition of antisemitism among Christians and 19th century ideas about race and nation.

AD539AB7B6CB4B6C8CDAF695D0C5CC13.description: Examine the background, causes, series of events, and effects of the Holocaust.

712484D9E6784D8B9339240732C56493.description: Compare military campaigns in Africa, Asia, and the Pacific (e.g., Battle of the Atlantic, Battle of Britain, siege of Leningrad, Operation Torch, Operation Overlord), identifying Allied military leadership, major strategies, and sacrifices made by soldiers, as well as civilians.

B461A3FB81064C91B551749112973358.description: Describe aggression by the Axis powers (e.g., Italy's invasion of Ethiopia; Germany’s militarization, the Stalin-Hitler Pact of 1939, annexation of Austria, and attack on Poland; Japanese invasion of China, the Nanking Massacre) and the initial responses by the Allied nations.

2B383D7C827F4F77B3EF961B0BB21356.description: Examine the significant events of World War II from a global perspective.

84BA7FF1473040D8AAF639BFBFD1B2F6.description: Identify the characteristics of fascism, including how such totalitarian regimes utilized propaganda, repressed dissention, and instigated antisemitism (e.g., Nuremberg Laws in Germany).

25CDF889CE284F22A005060D8821C085.description: Describe the drives for empire in the 1930s by evaluating the economic, social, and political conditions that allowed the rise of fascist militarist regimes in Germany, Italy, Spain, and Japan.

FB656A160FF94E239A3909100EC336D8.description: Explain how violations of the Treaty of Versailles and failure of the League of Nations, including attempts at disarmament and unrealistic expectations of massive reparations, fueled a second global conflict.

A3BDC0C2C9064E8086687A73B0837F1F.description: Describe the various causes and consequences of the global economic collapse and evaluate how governments responded to the Great Depression, including English and French social welfare legislation, the growth of the mixed economy, and the welfare state.

37EB03B8D5DA4E0A9A203279CA699778.description: Analyze the economic, social, and political conditions that resulted in World War II.

9F93CD38A967426199FA86FE224ABD99.description: Describe Stalin’s rise to power and establishment of a totalitarian regime resulting in the destruction of civil society (e.g., Great Purge’s oppression of political opposition, the destruction of individual rights, use of mass terror against internal enemies, genocidal starvation of the Ukrainians known as the Holodomor).

AEF0EF15AAD24A3D86AF1C18EE558BBA.description: Summarize the consequences of Soviet communism, including the establishment of a one-party dictatorship under Lenin, government seizure of private property, and the persecution of religious believers.

AA89225B771845FF9DD7691F4BF5068F.description: Describe the growing political and social unrest under Czar Nicholas II, collapse of the Romanov dynasty, the emergence of the Bolshevik movement, and the Russian Civil War.

079D5C00BA8145678400F607555A0933.description: Analyze the causes, consequences, and impact of the Russian Revolution on global politics, social structures, human rights, and economic systems.

4450C35B193847C8BEF0CFB4201FA7DE.description: Examine the immediate consequences of the Treaty of Versailles, including the “war guilt” clause, the establishment of European mandates and the rise of Zionism, as well as the subsequent rise of regional nationalist movements.

2C8ED606E09C4DD2B5C9C019E61A88BB.description: Explain post-war political instability (e.g., collapse of the Russian, Ottoman, and Austrian Empires).

3FCD429A273C4AB4A8AD38BBADDEAD3E.description: Describe the economic destruction and unprecedented loss of life, including the Armenian genocide.

37B92EE946E149458320732C82441711.description: Evaluate the lasting effects of World War I.

156D2459FDF74AC89683D5EBA65D1575.description: Summarize the significant events of World War I and why the conflict was considered a total war (e.g., use of industrial and chemical weapons, prolonged trench warfare, expansion into a global conflict) with a focus on the war’s significant turning points (e.g., Battles of the Marne, Verdun, the Somme).

790ABF3F15364905A4CB405435E64C6A.description: Describe the complex and multiple causes of World War I (e.g., German militarism and arms race, nationalism, industrial and colonial competition) and examine Europe’s alliances affected by the declining power of the Austro-Hungarian and Ottoman Empires.

D58E14D4B7914B609C22053738D2203F.description: Analyze the underlying causes and significant events of World War I.

D5D66B1D0BDE492089AAA8321BC040E1.description: The student will evaluate the global transformation created by the World Wars.

BC30340C8819493EA3CAC467EBA97BC2.description: Describe important political, economic, and cultural aspects of the decay of the Qing dynasty, including growing Western influence and the Boxer Rebellion.

528A83CA2AAE4095938121F38777F470.description: Assess the political, economic, and cultural impact of the British Raj, Britain’s subordination of India, characterized by economic, educational, and infrastructure investments, at the costs of exploitation and self-rule.

663F614EEB7D496D8CB5AA3E2D14662C.description: Describe the outcomes of the Berlin Conference on Africa’s Indigenous populations and the impact of superimposed boundaries, establishing spheres of influence.

E04B0358C7E4498BB0A2B476F08113C4.description: Describe the consequences of imperialism and the growth of national rivalry in Asia, Africa, and the Americas (e.g., territorial conquests and the development of settler colonies, European investments abroad and imperial reshaping of colonial economies, the exploitation of natural resources, changes in life expectancy, inhumane treatment of Indigenous populations, and the spread of Christianity in Africa and Asia).

6A25121DAD10431AB675E82B7FD6E105.description: Explain the economic, political, and social justifications supporting imperialist ideology and colonialism (e.g., Social Darwinism, economic gain and resources, Christian missions, strategic advantage, and Nationalism).

1862DBBC3D104AEEB522DEB85E569596.description: Evaluate the impact of industrialization on global imperialism.

F242A7AF0CD44350BED754BE9CB30D29.description: Describe the European intellectual revolution and the ideal of academic freedom, including leading figures (e.g., Marie Curie, Charles Darwin, Gregor Mendel).

8C6D57A3307B48A5A3CDE206EEC6D7C6.description: Describe the rise of socialism, including the ideas and influence of Robert Owen and Karl Marx, as well as the major ideas of Marx and Engels’ The Communist Manifesto.

4130FF911C9C4428930E0E94DB1F7E67.description: Examine the concept of economic interventionism (e.g., economic protectionism, child labor laws, legislation for old age pensions, health insurance).

BB9D6C14BEF7482ABB4C9B3C7F0441A5.description: Explain the rise of trade unionism and the birth of the Labour Party, including the effects of various social and political reforms, such as Liberalism (John Stuart Mill) and modern conservatism (school of Edmund Burke).

FF6D2F21FBFB4BC7BDEBEF43F79F9A70.description: Examine how the abolition of slavery within the British Empire was influenced by Christian humanitarianism and examine the role of various antislavery societies, including the work of William Wilberforce.

769218E6C8144EA0B659B0EC05106E7C.description: Analyze responses to and the legacy of the Industrial Revolution.

278B205D7EFA4A1DB1FC15E78303707B.description: Describe the social and economic consequences of industrialization, such as population growth, increased life expectancy, rural to urban migration, harsh living conditions for the urban poor, and growth of the middle class.

08009C6B286A445C9003AEA4174D1600.description: Explain how an entrepreneurial culture led to technological innovations such as the steam engine, railroad, and the application of scientific research to industrial innovation.

5EA362D30A1246118CB0B6EDDD65C320.description: Evaluate the extent to which the Second Agricultural Revolution and innovations in energy, mechanization, and transportation enabled industrialization.

5680A1BA613044989FCC3A767F280A93.description: Explain how the Industrial Revolution began in England due to its natural resources, entrepreneurship, labor, and access to capital.

03BA5629DA784C8A8B2641930453B2DA.description: Examine the causes and characteristics of the Industrial Revolution.

7BC067087A3041858DC6E6AA4FFD2113.description: The student will analyze the massive social, economic, and cultural change brought about by the Industrial Revolution.

47DC2AB693F343B78C4F48A9ADCA48C0.description: Describe the common conditions (widespread protests and demands of working class; poverty and mass starvation) and democratic ideals (e.g., removal of monarchial power, universal suffrage, free press) contributing to the wave of revolutions of 1848, explaining how they set the stage for the emergence of modern nation-states.

606162BE31744283AC545FA17A7AB16A.description: Describe the legacy of the Napoleonic Wars including an accelerated rise of nationalism across Europe, Britain’s role in maintaining a balance-of-power, and how the Congress of Vienna attempted to establish a new political order in Europe.

DBD328F8C82A4AA2816A8202D0E535B1.description: Explain how the intellectual thoughts of the American and French Revolutions regarding self-rule inspired revolutionary movements globally, such as democratic revolutions in Haiti, Mexico, and South America.

DB55B45A74494F6698BA687BCD98A266.description: Explain the major effects of the French Revolution (e.g., contribution to modern nationalism, political, economic, and cultural debilitation of the Catholic church) and analyze how its support for ideas of popular sovereignty and legal equality served as a model for later revolutions.

E5F747F6ED75449D92FE66538F1E6842.description: Trace the significant events of the French Revolution (e.g., convening of the Estates General, Tennis Court Oath, storming of the Bastille, execution of Louis XVI, Reign of Terror) and analyze the political concepts presented in Declaration of the Rights of Man and the Citizen.

1D7FD8033BF94393AB355540178F3C62.description: Examine the influence of Enlightenment philosophy, economic conditions, the rising influence of the middle class, and the excesses and corruption of the French monarchy on demands for reform.

D3074CE262024D3BACA1DA219793AF60.description: Analyze the complex political, social, and economic causes culminating in the French Revolution.

CFDA425623774F88BDFCAF2C1D3D427E.description: The student will analyze the political, economic, and social transformations brought about by the events of the age of revolutions.

CAE82BDAA9E143E4AEDD124A315EC907.description: Examine the impact of Adam Smith’s theories, as presented in The Wealth of Nations, on modern economic thought and free enterprise.

545D8322153D4578A340137B41B6A270.description: Examine the origins, meanings, and effects of John Locke’s Second Treatise of Government.

C026040EE41D4C7681AD69F0FC58C7DC.description: Describe the contributions of major Enlightenment thinkers (e.g., Locke, Montesquieu, Voltaire, Rousseau), contrasting the views of Thomas Hobbes regarding the divine right theory.

6119122526864BE6AE3856508FB0B060.description: Explain how the major ideas of enlightened philosophy influenced the concepts of natural rights and consent of the governed.

12AD601694164AA5853A0036F567D9BE.description: Analyze the impact of the Enlightenment on modern government and economic institutions.

62CAF73FBA34496BB8F3C098FCF6719A.description: Describe England’s fiscal, commercial, and technological innovations, including the culture of trade, England’s military success in successive wars with France, and the consequent establishment of a British Empire in North America.

489F0A8AAE494F6C9C908CF84A4602F3.description: Examine the development of parliamentary sovereignty, constitutional mixed government, and liberty in England, including the importance of the English Bill of Rights and how it limited the power of the monarch.

7E191D0CC60C4D74937D207140010D28.description: Identify the causes, essential events, and effects of the English Civil War and the Glorious Revolution.

0862E6F878404FAD8BB69F1A8161E4AB.description: Explain England’s response to Absolutism in Europe, which influenced American thoughts on self-government.

B55409F7AD6E4923A44D976850493FC6.description: Analyze government's source of authority under a constitutional monarchy by explaining how and why powers are limited by a written or unwritten constitution (e.g., English Parliament).

78ECEF25546A4F528591D851E63E36FA.description: Examine rule by enlightened monarchs and how the ideas of the Enlightenment tempered Absolutism (e.g., Joseph II, Frederick the Great, Catherine the Great).

6899432F24C54B91AA8B6689CF3D7E97.description: Describe the theory of Absolutism which supports the exercise of unlimited power according to an inherited divine right to rule (e.g., Louis XIV).

F79182FA0D3A4A12ACD3FE9EF5C79D7F.description: Examine the Dynastic Cycle (Chinese Mandate of Heaven) by explaining its principle that virtuous rulers are bestowed power from a heavenly mandate, yet subject to rebellion if abusive.

ABA7E01FC32C447681CA6015CD0B065C.description: Describe historic and contemporary examples of theocracies, based on the concept that civil affairs should be determined by religious laws and governed by religious leaders.

050D6E3C45BF4E5E8B7AA0B6D8849FDF.description: Distinguish between limited and unlimited forms of government by describing the growing consolidation of political power in Europe manifested in the rise of nation-states and monarchies.

DEE07CAFA987438A93A6E67C003D349C.description: Compare theories and forms of government regarding sources of authority and legitimacy, including the role of the citizen and the concept of individual liberty.

D602AD17F93349688D474CCABE3D05AC.description: The student will analyze developments in politics, science, and philosophy contributing to human advancement and the rise of modern institutions of self-government.

572B3BE0E1B84AB79F53E90440F382D7.description: Explain how overseas expansion led to the development of the trans-Atlantic slave trade.

3FA07DC7D1C54FE3B0B5A879A55C2353.description: Describe the major economic and cultural effects of the Columbian Exchange and explain how the enslavement of Indigenous peoples and Africans was used for the development of colonial economies.

A9567C1C87404260B3F263E9BEF632C4.description: Explain how the origins of modern capitalism, mercantilism, and the market economy in Europe impacted international trading patterns, prompting global exploration and rivalry.

A40B788C88C84543923C5A4261F8F1D1.description: Examine how the Doctrine of Discovery was used to legitimize European colonization of lands and Indigenous peoples.

F656282FD0F74D04B9E78E0A131D4405.description: Explain the economic and religious motivations that prompted European exploratory expeditions into the Western Hemisphere and describe how these expeditions led to the expansion of the Spanish and Portuguese empires in Latin America.

4C136B7FEA7440BBA4DB59E509354078.description: Analyze migration, settlement patterns, and cultural diffusion caused by a competition among European nations during the Age of Exploration.

8C30E3244A3A47FC964A972807FEE61A.description: Describe the accomplishments of major figures of the Scientific Revolution (e.g., Nicolaus Copernicus, Johannes Kepler, Galileo Galilei, Francis Bacon, Isaac Newton) as well as the impact of Islamic and Hindu learning on global scholarship and scientific thought.

929A40415E204B0897F950280195B7FC.description: Explain how the scientific method and new technologies, such as the telescope and microscope, led to new theories of the universe.

52DD84A82E624C2AA87671B50028E6F2.description: Evaluate the legacy of the Scientific Revolution on society, focusing on major theories and discoveries.

077EAD8DA77A49AFA7663F3D970E3F92.description: Explain new ways of disseminating information, such as Gutenberg’s invention of the printing press and the translation of the Bible into the vernacular.

138DED528834403CB2FD820266559F30.description: Describe tensions between religious and secular authorities and doctrines, including the English Reformation and the consolidation of royal power.

AF6FED1128054FED951C9214A442B99B.description: Explain the purposes and policies of the Catholic Counter-Reformation.

2C38B79422DA478392B5A86314B4D95C.description: Trace the spread of Protestantism across Europe, including Lutherans, Reformed (Calvinist), Church of England, Anabaptists, and the effects on European society (e.g., idea and practice of religious tolerance, Calvinist work ethic).

4ABEB55F3357406D84C211CD50E04E39.description: Explain reasons for the growing discontent with the Catholic Church, including the main ideas of Martin Luther and John Calvin, and the role of William Tyndale.

6F4193CBF8D04B8E8DF5E4007DE3F56D.description: Summarize the causes of and influence of the theological movements of the Reformation and how those movements subsequently transformed society.

66187FF9CA4F4D7F979930EEF9C7AADC.description: Describe how humanism furthered the values of republicanism, liberty, and individualism.

5AF5FFEF57BD41D8B9347B90771507F8.description: Examine intellectual development and advances (e.g., vernacular literature and expanded literacy, the arts, engineering, human anatomy), focusing on the selected historical figures (e.g., Machiavelli, Michelangelo, da Vinci, Raphael, Erasmus).

935FEACA36664837B46518D1B140A9FB.description: Assess the origins and significance of the Italian Renaissance and the revival of classical learning

6EEDD9F1B5D14864917D83C3A849F371.description: Describe the impact of medieval English legal and constitutional practices, as established in the Magna Carta, on the rise of modern democratic principles (e.g., common law, limitation of a monarch’s power, parliament, habeas corpus, and concepts related to the rule of law).

47D7A38D0C2741C09AD26F07A3FE27C7.description: The student will analyze patterns of social, economic, political, and cultural changes during the Late Middle Ages to the Age of Exploration.

3717ECFA33514683AEC8825292029DEB.description: Describe the contributions of the Byzantine Empire, including the influence of Constantine on Christianity and the significance of the Justinian Code.

620E2E6DE0E0405BAC0A4DB18C9609B2.description: Compare the impact of Greek and Roman philosophers, including Plato, Aristotle and Cicero including their lasting influence on ideas and principles of government.

0EF18469CA474010A007D8FA9173242E.description: Evaluate the contributions of the Roman civilization to law and government by describing the Roman Republic’s development of the principle of separation of powers, the concept of civic duty, written laws, and the rule of law.

9472414170B64A148A6B2DC994CC8974.description: Explain ancient Athens’ experience with direct democracy and identify modern political principles which developed in ancient Greece (e.g., the city-state, civic participation through voting, law-making bodies).

0C6BD744899243E999089012778C7D59.description: Examine the influence of Judeo-Christian ethics and Mosaic law on early American political and legal systems, as well as modern legal systems.

F09F5F21B3AA492E9A20B0BCDF2A51FB.description: Describe ancient Mesopotamia’s Code of Hammurabi as one of the earliest legal codes.

95858F2232E84D919646BE4F967613EA.description: Compare the origins and spread of the world’s major religions and philosophies, including Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism, Christianity, Islam, Confucianism, and Sikhism.

B2EE309B92FE4301A7F89D8825A5A81B.description: Analyze the influence of religious, political, and philosophical ideas on society.

24288DD241564C39A823A3C2ACD84C55.description: Describe the institution of slavery prior to the 15th century as a widespread result of warfare and economic practices.

459624B250A24E9BA332C669916F4658.description: Explain different ways in which societies interact across regions (e.g., trade, exploration, colonization) resulting in cultural diffusion (e.g., the Silk Road, Trans-Saharan exchange).

A82194A785514FD8A647A042A3DE8284.description: Explain how geographical and environmental factors impacted settlement and cultural development.

8E79A88885CD4BCAA23AD168F556BAEE.description: The student will analyze the impact of the patterns of ancient political, economic, and cultural development.

1ADB3D463A474D2288C54E3A5DA36498.description: Construct presentations or products for a designated audience, using research and reasoning to enhance understanding of a topic or issue.

749CD5A91CEB4EE7A73FB94AE9DA2BDC.description: Integrate quotes and summaries of research findings into written products while avoiding plagiarism.

AC7DCAB9B37B48DC84C6AF52EE204354.description: Develop self-generated theses or claims related to independent research and investigations using credible and relevant sources.

647495E4CC4C4D038846A86FF16A1A13.description: Engage in authentic research to acquire, refine, and share knowledge through written presentations and products.

B75711E4BB354A4C924191D3F4544B5B.description: Compose argumentative written products, including a precise claim as distinguished from opposing claims, organizing logical reasoning, and providing credible evidence to develop an argument.

C212FBE466294CB7B0E421FFA6FE3B4F.description: Compose informative essays and written products, developing a thesis, citing and incorporating evidence from multiple sources and maintaining an organized, formal structure.

E3AADBA3BEF846ADA5C2575765918AA8.description: Summarize and paraphrase, integrate evidence, and cite sources to create written products, research projects, and presentations for multiple purposes related to social studies content.

66B10E39B759422C8F19393BB82C5D0F.description: The student will develop a variety of evidence- based written products designed for multiple purposes.

1E7F262B92BA420FBB0614D62EEB9417.description: Actively listen, evaluate, and analyze a speaker’s message, asking questions while engaged in collaborative discussions about social studies topics and texts.

DD52E175B6264BCA9A2DF2920BF0984E.description: Evaluate the author’s point of view, potential bias, and how authors can reach different conclusions regarding the same issue.

52BCE884BBEF4637BDE4D88828C74D27.description: Evaluate the extent to which historical or cultural perspectives affect an author’s stated or implied purpose.

A1C4894125804A65ACAAAFE4CA8F9993.description: Apply critical reading and thinking skills to interpret, evaluate, and respond to a variety of complex texts and perspectives.

7A571B3DBA1243968CA7704B3D9FA050.description: Analyze information from visual, oral, digital, and interactive texts (e.g., maps, charts, images, political cartoons, videos, artwork) in order to draw conclusions and defend arguments.

803884408E6044B188DE1E0704D9D96D.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, evaluating features such as author, date, and origin of information.

5C0E1339F0C14D74A82E63D7EBD89BA1.description: Comprehend, evaluate, and synthesize textual sources to acquire and refine knowledge in the social studies.

2283DAA1A0FC4D0DBD0D3E6B4032ECB9.description: The student will engage in critical, active reading of primary and secondary sources related to social studies concepts.

E5564EC3CA344AC9ABE02F5AC083411F.description: Evaluate the impact, both intended and unintended, of government policies on market outcomes at national and global levels, past and present.

1EA6992B6B2647C6AC6549D590CEA114.description: Construct arguments using a combination of evidence regarding solutions used by nations to address historical or contemporary economic issues.

63EEF2ECEEA349BC94040AC03CBB61A7.description: Evaluate economic data from charts and graphs, noting trends and making predictions.

80419619DB4B4940A2236B154C78EB7D.description: Identify the principles of economic systems and develop an understanding of the benefits of a market system in local, national, and global settings.

99F6F6FCBD444BFDA2772E7DDF120FF8.description: Evaluate the extent to which political and economic decisions have had significant impact on human and physical environments of various places and regions.

3DE85498D00042A5BCA60578DB706F95.description: Compare and analyze complex maps and mapping technologies to analyze spatial patterns of human and physical environments, explaining relationships between the environment and events, past and present.

6DEFFBC2326F4E4D8E97674E5FB772B0.description: Actively engage in asking and answering geographic questions by acquiring, organizing, and analyzing multiple sources of data and information about the world’s past and present.

1A97357D3B78476BBB111EAE86251CEA.description: Demonstrate a mastery of geographic concepts and the use of geographic tools to understand the impact of geography on the past and present.

8050C3286E14417B9F6E6F8595A49899.description: Evaluate how multiple, complex events are shaped by unique circumstances of time and place; construct and interpret parallel timelines.

81E175D0BB3445AFA1122F542883AEB0.description: Analyze complex and interacting factors that influence multiple perspectives during different historical eras and contemporary events.

365DB4A30D6C4B6EBCAECD50E4A7351A.description: Gather and evaluate the usefulness of various formats of evidence for specific inquiry, analyzing the broader historical context, and assessing potential bias and credibility of sources.

D53D07614B61440695C269200712C460.description: Develop skills which demonstrate an understanding of historical events and the people who shaped our history.

137504F8B50E4735B0759E8C0101817C.description: Analyze the impact of constitutions, laws, treaties, and international agreements, by comparing how various governmental powers and responsibilities have changed over time.

849804F720C647F4B2454FA8E66CF5C1.description: Evaluate the impact of the structure and powers exercised by governmental systems on public policy, using historical and contemporary examples.

B2512FA9B8C5410687543D555807A7F2.description: Evaluate various significant documents from the United States and other nations to compare civic virtues and principles of political systems.

7DEBAFC0FC92480DA6C969AED6CBE195.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of government, the benefits of democratic systems, and their responsibilities as citizens.

92A92548D994437B8809D45F8F3133C8.description: The student will use interdisciplinary tools to acquire, apply, and evaluate content understanding of the four strands of social studies.

61BBD012AF6A40B58062D7EEC6EA4946.description: Demonstrate understanding of content through the development of self-driven inquiries and the completion of multi-staged, authentic tasks and assessments.

EDE08CA02BE74D7F8CF3E947388E4A44.description: Reinforce critical thinking by evaluating and challenging ideas and assumptions, analyzing and explaining inconsistencies in reasoning.

CD6CDCBBDB6443A2AEDE35432FC29800.description: Evaluate points of agreement and disagreement from reliable information and expert interpretations used to answer supporting questions related to content knowledge.

F1CF701721444E6680F7622EF3FD0B23.description: Develop, investigate, and evaluate plausible answers to essential questions that reflect enduring understandings across time, real world circumstances, and social studies disciplines.

9A764B7F671E4DC9A1DB9AFB33DFFF89.description: Develop practices which demonstrate an understanding that social studies involves the evaluation of evidence.

A67E59DDD86D46C7B5E37BF3067BC3C9.description: Gather and evaluate information regarding complex problems, assessing individual and collective actions taken to address them.

F6B904F40D37451F85F119B57FEB8587.description: Engage in a range of deliberative and democratic processes to develop strategies to address authentic, real-world problems in community and out-of-school contexts.

CCB2527B9A40425C8955888225626403.description: Evaluate the impact of perspectives, civil discourse, and democratic principles on addressing civic issues.

D94084C4A76B4332B5933C19DE809804.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the virtue of civil discourse to analyze and address real- world problems.

A7EF38815A7B48CB8A4B3AC2B211158F.description: The student will apply critical thinking skills to address authentic civic issues.

document.title: Oklahoma Academic Standards SOCIAL STUDIES

228EFE29FD2A415DA1E492295734EBE0.description: Describe foreign policies exemplified by the United States’s withdrawal from Afghanistan, responses to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and the Israel-Hamas conflict.

17AE54BC0477416BAD38A31DE1F1E634.description: Examine the United States-Mexico border crisis and the effects of Administration policies.

7C0D9A4214744B38B4BE18F9A719CB8F.description: Describe the challenges and accomplishments of the President Joseph Biden administration.

6F3F0A2EDD254E1ABA34B00297C38ABC.description: Analyze the impact of appointments to the U.S. judicial system and the Supreme Court (e.g., Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization and the overturning of Roe v. Wade).

6EBF8A1C39634CF9A00F09ADFC6BF3A2.description: Identify discrepancies in 2020 elections results by looking at graphs and other information, including the sudden halting of ballot-counting in select cities in key battleground states, the security risks of mail-in balloting, sudden batch dumps, an unforeseen record number of voters, and the unprecedented contradiction of “bellwether county” trends.
